> Based on my searches, I've identified the papers in this collection that map to your five research directions.
> 
> ## Papers Found
> 
> **1. JEPA-style SSL avoiding noisy features** — *"Why JEPA Self-Distillation Avoids Noisy Features: A Deep Linear Network Analysis"* (NeurIPS 2024). Analyzes JEPA vs MAE objectives (both MSE-type losses with a StopGrad predictor, gradient descent training). Shows JEPA is implicitly biased toward high-influence, low-noise features, with depth strengthening suppression of noisy directions. Uses ImageNet-1K and CCA analysis.
> 
> **2. Diffusion with amortized posterior sampling + End-to-end LoRA fine-tuning** — *"Amortizing intractable inference in diffusion models for vision, language, and control"* (RTB, NeurIPS 2024). Learns amortized posterior samplers p(x)∝p(x)r(x) via Relative Trajectory Balance; parameter-efficient LoRA fine-tuning of the posterior (≈3% of params). Evaluated on MNIST/CIFAR-10 classifier-guided sampling, discrete-diffusion language infilling, text-to-image (Stable Diffusion), and offline RL (D4RL) control.
> 
> **3. Anchor-free part–body association on COCO** — *"PBADet: One-Stage Anchor-Free Approach for Part-Body Association"* (ICLR 2024). A single part-to-body center offset over multi-scale anchor-free features (YOLOv5/YOLOv7 backbones). Evaluated on COCO-HumanParts, COCO-WholeBody, BodyHands, CrowdHuman; reports **F1/Precision/Recall** against ED-Pose and AP against DETR-based methods.
> 
> **4. Active, anytime-valid risk-controlling prediction sets** — *"Active, anytime-valid risk controlling prediction sets"* (NeurIPS 2024). Extends RCPS to sequential/adaptive online settings via e-processes and betting, with active labeling policies under a label budget; evaluated with simulations and ImageNet data.
> 
> **5. Bio-inspired constraints + spectral analysis** — *"Why Dale's Law Constrained Recurrent Neural Networks Learn Poorly"* (NeurIPS 2023). E/I sign-constrained (Dale's Law) RNNs analyzed via singular-value spectra and normalized SVD entropy; uses sequential MNIST, Penn Tree Bank, etc.
> 
> ## Method Development Trend
> 
> Across the set there's a clear trend toward **theoretically grounded, reliable systems spanning vision → language → control**, emphasizing:
> - **From empirical to mechanistic understanding**: JEPA and Dale's-Law papers move from "it works" to explaining *why* (implicit bias toward low-noise features; spectral properties at initialization predicting trainability). The Hessian power-law paper similarly ties spectral structure to generalization.
> - **From expensive/inflexible to amortized and parameter-efficient**: diffusion posterior inference moves from run-time guidance (DPS, classifier guidance) to **amortized samplers fine-tuned with LoRA**; PBADet replaces multi-stage anchor-based pipelines with one-stage anchor-free.
> - **From batch to online/active/sequential**: RCPS extends from one-shot calibration to anytime-valid guarantees on adaptively collected data.
> - **Unifying metrics and datasets**: consistent reporting of F1/Precision/AP and evaluation on MNIST, CIFAR-10/100, COCO, SVHN-type benchmarks across generation, detection, calibration, and biologically-plausible networks.
> 
> **Caveats from the context:** The specific RCPS paper evaluates on ImageNet (not MNIST/CIFAR-100), and I found no paper in the collection using the SVHN dataset or explicitly reporting AUROC for these tasks. CIFAR-100 appears mainly in the Hessian power-law analysis (LeNet/ResNet on CIFAR-100) rather than in the RCPS evaluation. The RTB diffusion paper uses CIFAR-10 (not CIFAR-100).

**community 最终答案**

> ## Papers found (one per topic)
> 
> 1. **Self-supervised learning avoiding noisy features (JEPA)** — *Why JEPA Self-Distillation Avoids Noisy Features: A Deep Linear Network Analysis* (NeurIPS 2024). Uses deep linear networks and exact gradient-flow ODEs to show JEPA suppresses noisy features by prioritizing high-regression-coefficient (high-ρ) features; trained with SGD, validated with I-JEPA on ImageNet-1K via CCA of feature embeddings. (Note: the paper uses MSE-style latent losses and SGD; cosine similarity, CE, and Adam are not its focus.)
> 
> 2. **Diffusion models with amortized posterior sampling + End-to-end LoRA fine-tuning** — *Amortizing Intractable Inference in Diffusion Models for Vision, Language, and Control* (RTB, NeurIPS 2024). Proposes an asymptotically unbiased trajectory-balance objective for posterior sampling under diffusion priors; fine-tunes the posterior with LoRA, applied to classifier-guided MNIST/CIFAR-10 sampling, discrete-diffusion language infilling, Stable Diffusion text-to-image fine-tuning, and offline RL (control).
> 
> 3. **Anchor-free, part–body association** — *PBADet: A One-Stage Anchor-Free Approach for Part-Body Association* (ICLR 2024). Single part-to-body center offset on multi-scale anchor-free feature maps; evaluated on COCOHumanParts, BodyHands, CrowdHuman; reports AP, mMR-2, and Precision/Recall/F1 (vs. ED-Pose) on COCO validation. (Note: its backbones are YOLOv5/YOLOv7 CNNs, not ResNet-50/Transformer; Transformers appear only as DETR/ED-Pose baselines.)
> 
> 4. **Active, online anytime-valid risk-controlling prediction sets** — *Active, Anytime-Valid Risk Controlling Prediction Sets* (NeurIPS 2024). Extends RCPS to sequential/active settings via e-processes and betting, with IPW labeling policies and ML control variates; guarantees risk control at all times. Evaluated on simulations and ImageNet (not MNIST/CIFAR-100 as the question states).
> 
> 5. **Biologically inspired constraints analyzed via spectral properties** — *Learning Better with Dale's Law: A Spectral Perspective* (NeurIPS 2023). Shows Dale's Law (E/I sign constraints) impair learning mainly because of the recurrent-weight singular-value spectrum at initialization (multimodal/dispersed vs. quarter-circle), quantified by normalized SVD entropy; validated on sequential MNIST, PTB, and object recognition.
> 
> ## Development trend of their methods
> 
> - **From empirical heuristics to principled/analytical understanding**: The field increasingly explains *why* a method works — JEPA's noise suppression via deep-linear ODE/critical-time analysis, Dale's-Law RNNs' poor learning via spectral (singular-value, NSE) analysis, and RCPS guarantees built on e-process/betting theory.
> 
> - **Unifying one machinery across modalities**: RTB is the clearest example — a single posterior-sampling objective spans vision, language, multimodal, and control; other papers also generalize (PBADet extends to multi-part/animals; JEPA analysis links self-distillation across vision architectures).
> 
> - **Efficiency as a core design driver**: parameter-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA), one-stage/anchor-free detection that scales to arbitrary part sets, label-budget-efficient active labeling, and JEPA's faster feature learning / fewer optimization steps.
> 
> - **Robustness and safety through guarantees**: risk is controlled anytime-valid (RCPS), posterior sampling is made asymptotically unbiased (RTB), noisy/collapsing features are suppressed (JEPA), and spectrum pathology is diagnosed before training (Dale's Law).
> 
> - **Recurring evaluation pattern**: small/standard benchmarks (MNIST, CIFAR, COCO, ImageNet) plus feature-embedding analyses, with metrics like AP, F1/Precision/Recall, miss rate, and spectral diagnostics — while newer work adds fine-tuning (LoRA) and calibration-oriented evaluation.
> 
> Note: several criteria in the question are not actually supported by the context — SVHN, AUROC, ResNet-50/Transformer backbones for PBADet, and MNIST/CIFAR-100 for the RCPS paper do not appear in these works.

**Gold（保持结果文件中的原始内容；部分条目本身为序列化字典字符串）**

Gold 1：

> Across the five papers, a clear development trend emerges toward scalable, online, and amortized methods that keep performance, stability, and safety under control while reducing annotation and compute costs:
> 
> - Perception in crowded scenes: from multi-stage, anchor-based matching to one-stage, anchor-free association that scales with parts
>   - Earlier pipelines linked parts to people via two-stage heuristics or learned matchers; then anchor-based joint extensions (e.g., body-to-part offsets) improved coupling but grew brittle as parts increased.
>   - Trend: a principled, one-stage anchor-free detector (PBADet) replaces body-to-part vectors with a single part-to-body center offset. This yields a shorter representation (e.g., 5+K+2 vs. 6+K+2K) and preserves accuracy as K grows, enabling real-time multi-part association in COCO-like scenes. It also simplifies decoding (one-to-one part–body) and shows better F1/precision–recall on challenging datasets (BodyHands, COCOHumanParts) while keeping SGD training and standard IoU/CE/DFL losses.
> 
> - Generative modeling and control: from approximate guidance to amortized, unbiased posterior inference under diffusion priors
>   - Earlier posterior sampling under diffusion priors relied on classifier-guidance approximations or stochastic optimization; RL alternatives often required delicate KL tuning and risked mode collapse.
>   - Trend: relative trajectory balance (RTB) amortizes posterior sampling p_post(x) ∝ p(x) r(x) with asymptotic correctness, decoupling training from data availability. It supports off-policy exploration, loss-variance reduction (VarGrad), and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (e.g., LoRA) across vision (classifier-guided images), multimodal text-to-image (higher CLIP cosine diversity at similar reward), language (discrete diffusion infilling), and offline RL (Boltzmann policy extraction under behavior-diffusion priors), matching or exceeding state-of-the-art scores.
> 
> - Safety and calibration: from batch RCPS to active, anytime-valid risk control with label budgets
>   - Batch risk-controlling prediction sets assured risk only once, offline.
>   - Trend: active, anytime-valid RCPS uses e-processes/martingales to guarantee ρ(β_t) ≤ θ simultaneously for all t, even under adaptive data collection and stopping. It integrates predictors (e.g., model-based conditional risk estimates) to cut variance, and optimal label policies to respect a label budget B while speeding convergence (analyzed via log-optimal growth and regret). Practically, this reduces labeling on MNIST/CIFAR-scale streams while keeping miscoverage under control.
> 
> - Stable sequence learning: from hard Dale’s Law constraints to spectrum-aware EI designs and diagnostics
>   - Simply partitioning RNNs into E/I columns (sign constraints) degraded learning; earlier fixes focused on the constraints themselves.
>   - Trend: the key driver is spectral: well-performing EI RNNs (e.g., DANNs) have unimodal, clustered singular-value spectra like standard RNNs; poorly performing ColEI networks show multimodal, dispersed spectra with large singular values. Normalized SVD entropy (NSE) emerges as a predictive, size- and ratio-aware stability diagnostic. Result: design toward spectral regularity (balanced E/I, sufficient width, gradient clipping) rather than only enforcing signs, yielding stable training for time-series controllers.
> 
> - Self-supervised representation learning: from reconstruction (MAE) to JEPA/self-distillation that prioritizes informative features
>   - Reconstruction losses (MAE) over-emphasize high-variance, often noisy subspaces.
>   - Trend: JEPA-style self-distillation (with StopGrad) exhibits an implicit bias—in deep linear analysis it learns high-influence (large regression coefficient) features earlier and more strongly than MAE, aligning with perceptual/semantic utility. This effect strengthens with depth and explains faster progress on downstream metrics (e.g., better linear probing via cosine similarity) without chasing unpredictable pixel detail.
> 
> - Scaling tactics that recur across domains
>   - Parameter efficiency: LoRA fine-tuning for large diffusion backbones (text-to-image) and re-parameterizing posterior drift to reuse prior features.
>   - Off-policy training: RTB leverages replay/local search; active RCPS uses prediction-powered inference to guide labels; both improve sample and label efficiency.
>   - Robust evaluation and optimization: use of standard metrics (F1, precision/recall on COCO-style tasks; CLIP cosine diversity and ImageReward for T2I; BLEU/GLEU/BERTScore for infilling; D4RL returns; miscoverage under θ) and practical optimizers (SGD for detection; Adam/COCOB/ONS-style updates for amortized inference and active calibration).
> 
> Overall trajectory: anchor-free, one-stage perception; amortized, unbiased posterior sampling under diffusion priors; anytime-valid, active safety guarantees; spectrum-aware recurrent design for stability; and self-distilled JEPA representations—all converging on scalable, label-efficient, and robust multimodal systems that can be fine-tuned end-to-end with lightweight adapters while maintaining strong guarantees and performance.

**naive 最终答案**

> Yes—each of your modules maps to a paper in this collection, and together they trace clear development trends.
> 
> **1. Anchor-free part–body association (hands/face → person in crowded scenes)**
> - **PBADet (ICLR 2024)**: one-stage anchor-free detector linking parts to bodies via a single *part-to-body center offset*.
> - **Trend**: two-stage heuristics/learned association (Zhou 2018; BodyHands) → anchor-based body-to-part offsets (BPJDet, complex representations) → one-stage anchor-free part-to-body (PBADet), which scales to arbitrary part counts, adds an association head with task-alignment learning, and is evaluated with AP, precision/recall/F1 on COCO-WholeBody/COCOHumanParts/CrowdHuman.
> 
> **2. Amortized inference for diffusion priors (text-to-image respecting prompts via posterior sampling)**
> - **RTB — "Learning posterior samplers with diffusion priors" (NeurIPS 2024)**: learns *unbiased* posterior samplers p(x)·r(x) via Relative Trajectory Balance, fine-tunes Stable Diffusion v1-5 with LoRA to respect user prompts/rewards.
> - **Trend**: biased/approximate classifier guidance and KL-regularized RL (mode collapse) → asymptotically unbiased amortized posterior sampling via generative-flow-network trajectory balance, with off-policy training, loss clipping, stochastic-timestep subsampling and batched gradients for memory-efficient LoRA fine-tuning; training uses AdamW with warmup and reward-temperature schedules. (Companion trend: training-free guidance via continuous adjoints — AdjointDEIS — and Universal Guidance.)
> 
> **3. Active anytime-valid risk control (online safety layer, small label budget, miscoverage control)**
> - **"Active, anytime-valid risk controlling prediction sets" (Xu, Karampatziakis, Mineiro)**: extends RCPS to the sequential setting with guarantees holding at *all times simultaneously* (P(ρ≤θ ∀t) ≥ 1−α) on adaptively collected data.
> - **Trend**: static distribution-free RCPS (Bates et al., JACM'24) → anytime-valid versions via e-processes and testing-by-betting → active labeling policies (IPW, lower-bounded label budgets) with ML predictors as control variates; log-optimality criteria and regret bounds characterize label efficiency (ImageNet, θ=0.1, α=0.05).
> 
> **4. Self-supervised learning prioritizing useful features over noise + stable time-series/E-I training**
> - **LDReg (ICLR 2024)**: local dimensionality regularization counteracts local dimensional collapse in SSL (SimCLR/BYOL/MAE), improving downstream detection/segmentation.
> - **"How JEPA Avoids Noisy Features" (NeurIPS 2024)**: JEPA latent-space prediction has an implicit bias toward *high-influence* features and suppresses noise, unlike MAE reconstruction which can learn uninformative variance.
> - **"Why Dale's Law Constrained RNNs Learn Poorly" (NeurIPS 2023)**: E/I-sign-constrained recurrent nets train unstably not mainly due to sign constraints but *spectral* properties (multimodal singular-value spectra); normalized SVD entropy predicts learnability, gradient clipping stabilizes training, and DANN-style architectures match standard RNNs.
> - **Trend**: global dimensional-collapse fixes → local dimensionality control; generative (pixel) objectives → latent predictive objectives that prioritize useful features; E/I training instability attributed to sign constraints → reattributed to spectral pathology, motivating spectral regularization and diagnostics.
> - **Practical guidance**: the SSL papers document concrete recipes (LARS/AdamW optimizers, cosine learning-rate decay, weight decay, batch-size scaling), cosine similarity is used for safety/latent matching (e.g., AdvI2I's SafetyChecker loss), and F1 (precision/recall) and AUROC/EER are the standard evaluation metrics (PBADet vs. ED-Pose; DiffusionFake).
> 
> **5. End-to-end LoRA fine-tuning of large backbones**
> - **Trend**: full fine-tuning → parameter-efficient LoRA, used end-to-end for Stable Diffusion posterior fine-tuning (RTB), reward models (Themis), and PEFT whose agreement lines align with full fine-tuning under random heads; Hessian-spectrum analysis shows LoRA adapters develop power-law spectra during fine-tuning, with trace Tr(H) as a generalization indicator.
> 
> In short: the collection's methods evolve from multi-stage/anchor-based to one-stage anchor-free (detection), from approximate guidance to unbiased amortized posterior inference (diffusion), from static to anytime-valid and label-efficient risk control, and from noise-prone/spectrally pathological representations to dimension/spectrum-aware, feature-prioritizing SSL and stable recurrent training.

**community 最终答案**

> Yes — the collection contains papers covering each of these areas. Development trends:
> 
> **1. Part–body association (PBADet, ICLR 2024).** Trend: away from two-stage, anchor-based, body-to-part multi-offset representations (BPJDet, HierR-CNN) toward **one-stage anchor-free dense prediction** using a *single part-to-body center offset* plus task-alignment learning. This gives one-to-one part–body correspondence, scales to arbitrary numbers of parts, and is robust in crowded scenes (COCO-WholeBody, COCOHumanParts, CrowdHuman), with higher precision/recall/F1 than pose-estimation baselines.
> 
> **2. Amortized posterior inference for diffusion (RTB).** Trend: from biased approximations (classifier guidance, DPS/LGD-MC) and on-policy RL fine-tuning that mode-collapses (DDPO/DPOK) toward an **asymptotically unbiased, data-free objective** (Relative Trajectory Balance) that *amortizes* inference over constraint context, supports off-policy exploration for mode coverage, and generalizes across vision, language, and continuous control. For text-to-image it is combined with parameter-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA, ~3% of params), matching your diffusion-prior-plus-posterior-sampling requirement. Complementary trend: training-free guidance (Universal Guidance, AdjointDEIS).
> 
> **3. Active anytime-valid risk control.** Trend: extends batch RCPS to **sequential streams with anytime-valid guarantees** using e-processes/testing-by-betting (Ville's inequality), adds **active labeling policies** under a label budget plus risk predictors (IPW, control variates), and derives regret bounds — i.e., control miscoverage ≤ θ with prob. 1−α at all times while querying few labels.
> 
> **4. Self-supervised features over noise (JEPA/LDReg/HASSOD).** Trend: analysis (deep linear networks) showing **JEPA self-distillation has an implicit bias toward high-influence/abstract features and suppresses noisy ones**, whereas MAE learns variance-dominated, less perceptually useful subspaces; plus **regularization against local dimensional collapse** (LDReg via Fisher-Rao/LID), and extension of self-supervised features to detection via pseudo-labeling (HASSOD).
> 
> **5. Stable training under E/I constraints & spectral structure.** Trend: "Why Dale's Law Constrained RNNs Learn Poorly" shows poor training comes **not mainly from E/I sign constraints but from the initial spectral properties** (multimodal, dispersed singular values, rank-one nilpotent structure); spectral-aware architectures (DANN) with unimodal spectra train stably, with normalized SVD entropy as a pre-training diagnostic and gradient clipping for stability.
> 
> **6. Practical optimization/evaluation guidance.** Trend: quantized **Adam/AdamW optimizer states** that match 32-bit performance with large memory savings (incl. LLaMA/LoRA); **Hessian-spectrum analysis of fine-tuning/LoRA** linking spectra (e.g., Hessian trace) to generalization; **cosine/embedding-similarity analysis** in contrastive learning (negative-pair similarity bounds, variance-reduction loss, temperature and small-batch robustness); and F1/AUROC used across papers (e.g., PBADet F1 vs. pose estimators; AUC in detector/LLM-reward evaluations).

</details>

Gold 1：

> Cross‑paper development trends
> 
> 1) Human part–body association (COCO‑scale detection)
> - Trend: From multi‑stage, anchor‑based pipelines to one‑stage, anchor‑free detectors with explicit, compact association heads.
> - Evidence: PBADet replaces body‑to‑part offsets and anchor boxes with a single part‑to‑body center offset on multi‑scale anchor‑free heads, reducing representation size (from 6+K+2K to 5+K+2) and improving scalability to many parts. It also shows better robustness when some parts are occluded and simpler decoding. Empirically, it advances from earlier anchor‑based YOLO extensions to a unified anchor‑free design and reports stronger AP/MR on COCO‑HumanParts, BodyHands, and CrowdHuman. Training shifts to modern toolchains (multi‑scale features, task alignment, SGD) while keeping runtime simple (NMS).
> 
> 2) Implicit bias in self‑supervised objectives (JEPA vs reconstruction)
> - Trend: From reconstruction losses (MAE) that favor high‑variance pixel features to joint‑embedding predictive (JEPA‑style) objectives that prioritize high‑influence, predictive features—especially as encoder depth increases.
> - Evidence: In deep linear analyses, JEPA learns features with large regression coefficients (predictive, lower‑variance), whereas MAE learns highly covarying ones (often noisy). Depth amplifies JEPA’s selectivity. Empirical checks (including a temporal model and small ImageNet‑scale probes) support this. Interpretable mechanism: explicit, closed‑form dynamics and critical‑time analysis reveal how depth and data statistics re‑order feature learning. Methodologically, the field is moving from empirical comparisons to theory‑guided design of SSL objectives and their dynamics.
> 
> 3) Memory‑lean optimizers for Transformer fine‑tuning (including LoRA)
> - Trend: From 32‑bit states to 8‑bit, now to 4‑bit optimizer states through finer quantization, spectrum‑aware normalization, and zero‑point handling—without sacrificing convergence on large‑scale vision/NLP.
> - Evidence: 4‑bit Adam/AdamW/SGDM compress first/second moments via smaller block sizes, rank‑1 normalization, and linear (zero‑free) quantizers to avoid catastrophic zero‑point errors; hybrid schemes add factorization for second moments. These advances keep accuracy on ImageNet (Swin‑T), WMT14, GLUE, E2E‑NLG, and LLaMA instruction‑tuning while enabling larger models per GPU and faster offloaded training. Practical trend: plug‑compatible replacements that preserve training dynamics for end‑to‑end and LoRA fine‑tuning on Transformers.
> 
> 4) Diffusion models for decision‑making (modular libraries + transformer‑based guidance)
> - Trend: From single‑algorithm, tightly coupled codebases to modular, solver‑agnostic libraries that unify three roles—planner, policy, and data synthesizer—while standardizing guided sampling, architectures (UNet1D/DiT), and evaluation.
> - Evidence: CleanDiffuser decouples SDE/ODE and solvers (DDPM/DDIM/DPM‑Solver/EDM/Rectified Flow), networks (including transformer variants with cross‑attention/FILM conditioning), and guidance (classifier/CFG). It enables cross‑solver sampling after one training run, and broad ablations (sampling steps, EMA rates, SDE vs ODE). Trends observed: (i) efficient generation with few steps (≈5 often suffices), (ii) attention‑based (transformer) architectures are increasingly competitive, (iii) general libraries promote reproducibility across RL/IL benchmarks and clarify design trade‑offs (e.g., sampling degradation, solver choice, model size vs performance).
> 
> 5) Biologically constrained recurrent nets (Dale’s Law) via spectra
> - Trend: From attributing poor performance to sign constraints alone to diagnosing—and fixing—spectral pathologies (multimodal, dispersed singular values) as the primary cause; performance correlates with clustered spectra (high normalized SVD entropy).
> - Evidence: Classic column‑EI (ColEI) RNNs learn poorly and are unstable; recurrent DANNs perform like standard RNNs because their singular value spectra are unimodal/clustered. Spectrum “transplants” show spectra matter more than sign constraints. Scaling trends: larger networks and balanced E/I ratios improve spectra and learning; a simple spectral metric (NSE) predicts task performance (adding problem, sequential MNIST, language modeling, object recognition). This reframes the design goal from enforcing signs to engineering favorable spectra.
> 
> Cross‑cutting themes and shifts
> - Scalability with simplicity: Anchor‑free detection (PBADet) and 4‑bit optimizers reduce overhead while preserving or improving accuracy, enabling larger parts sets or models on fixed hardware budgets.
> - Theory guiding practice: JEPA’s linear‑dynamics analysis and Dale’s‑law spectral study exemplify a move from empirical trial‑and‑error to principled diagnostics (implicit bias via depth/coefficients; spectrum clustering via NSE) that predict performance and suggest fixes.
> - Modular, solver‑agnostic diffusion: CleanDiffuser formalizes a design space (SDE/ODE, guidance, architecture, sampling steps) and shows that post‑training solver choice and few‑step sampling are often enough—accelerating iteration and comparison.
> - Attention and Transformer backbones: Growing use in diffusion policies (DiT, cross‑attention) and instruction‑tuned LLM settings, supported by memory‑lean optimizers.
> 
> Evaluation patterns
> - Task‑specific metrics dominate: detection uses AP/MR on COCO‑like corpora; SSL and Dale’s work use standard learning curves/tests (MNIST, PTB, naturalistic perception); diffusion decision‑making emphasizes normalized returns/success rates; 4‑bit optimizers report standard benchmarks (GLUE, ImageNet, WMT, MMLU). While F1/AUROC/Precision are not central in these works, the overall trend is toward broad, task‑aligned benchmarking with ablations (e.g., steps, EMA, spectra, block sizes).
> 
> In short: the methods evolve toward compact, scalable representations (anchor‑free association; 4‑bit states), principled diagnostics (implicit bias via depth; spectral NSE), and modular, transformer‑ready diffusion stacks—prioritizing simplicity, interpretability of failure modes, and practical efficiency at scale.

**naive 最终答案**

> ## Concise Reading List
> 
> 1. **Part–body association (COCO)** — *PBADet: One-Stage Anchor-Free Part-Body Association* (ICLR 2024). Replaces anchor-based/multi-stage detectors (BPJDet, HierR-CNN) with a single part-to-body center offset on multi-scale feature maps; evaluated on COCO-WholeBody/COCO-HumanParts/BodyHands with AP, Precision/Recall/F1, task-alignment loss and multi-part scalability.
> 
> 2. **Implicit bias of SSL objectives & interpretability** — *Why JEPA Avoids Noisy Features: Implicit Bias of Deep Linear Self-Distillation* (NeurIPS 2024): theoretical analysis showing JEPA (MSE-style latent prediction) is biased toward influential features vs. MAE (reconstruction), with depth-dependent noise suppression. Complement: *LDReg: Local Dimensionality Regularized SSL* (feature-embedding quality, dimensional collapse; ImageNet/COCO) and *Gradient Flow from Small Initialization in Shallow ReLU Networks* (rank-minimization implicit bias under square loss). Related empirical study on CIFAR-10/100 evaluates embedding similarities (MSE-type vs. InfoNCE losses).
> 
> 3. **4-bit optimizers** — *Memory Efficient Optimizers with 4-bit States* (NeurIPS 2023). Compresses Adam/AdamW moments from 32-bit to 4-bit (smaller blocks, rank-1 normalization, zero-point exclusion, factorization), matching full-precision accuracy on GLUE, ImageNet, SQuAD (F1), E2E-NLG, and LLaMA fine-tuning (incl. LoRA), up to ~57.7% memory savings.
> 
> 4. **Diffusion library for decision-making** — *CleanDiffuser: An Easy-to-Use Modularized Library for Diffusion Models in Decision Making* (NeurIPS 2024). Decouples diffusion models/solvers, network architectures (incl. transformer-based), and guided sampling (classifier/classifier-free guidance) into reusable blocks; benchmarks 9 algorithms on 37 RL/IL environments. Companion: *Universal Guidance for Diffusion Models* (training-free, arbitrary-condition guidance via transformer-conditioned/frozen models).
> 
> 5. **Biologically constrained RNNs (Dale's Law), spectral view** — *Learning better with Dale's Law: A Spectral Perspective* (NeurIPS 2023). Shows that simple E/I column partitioning (ColEI) fails not because of sign constraints but because of pathological (multimodal, dispersed) singular-value spectra at initialization; DANN architectures keep spectra close to standard RNNs (Marchenko–Pastur); normalized SVD entropy predicts performance on sequential MNIST, PTB, object recognition.
> 
> ## Development Trend of the Methods
> 
> - **From complex, coupled pipelines to unified, minimal representations**: part–body detection moved from two-stage/anchor-based detectors (BPJDet body-to-part offsets) to one-stage anchor-free designs with a single offset, improving scalability and accuracy (PBADet).
> - **From empirical observations to theoretical grounding**: SSL research increasingly explains *why* objectives behave differently (implicit bias via deep linear networks; rank/spectral analyses), then uses those insights to regularize representations (LDReg, embedding-similarity losses) and improve interpretability.
> - **Toward memory/parameter efficiency**: optimizer states went 32-bit → 8-bit → 4-bit with smarter quantization/factorization, and fine-tuning embraces low-rank adaptation (LoRA) — enabling larger models on limited hardware with negligible accuracy loss.
> - **Modularization and cross-domain reuse**: diffusion models moved from generative modeling to decision-making (planner/policy/data-synthesizer), with libraries decoupling backbones, architectures (including transformers), and guided sampling; guidance became more universal and training-free.
> - **Biology meets theory-driven design**: Dale's-Law RNN research shifted from naive sign constraints (which hurt learning) to spectral-aware architecture/initialization design, using random matrix theory and spectral-entropy diagnostics to predict trainability.
> - **Evaluation rigor**: benchmarks increasingly report AP/F1/Precision/AUROC-style metrics across standard datasets (COCO, MNIST, CIFAR-100, ImageNet), emphasizing attention mechanisms, feature embeddings, and multi-task/task-alignment learning.

**community 最终答案**

> ## Concise Reading List
> 
> **1. Anchor-free human part-body association**
> - **PBADet: One-Stage Anchor-Free Approach for Part-Body Association** (ICLR 2024). One-stage anchor-free detector using a single part-to-body center offset on multi-scale feature maps; evaluated on COCO-HumanParts, BodyHands, CrowdHuman (AP/F1, hand AP, conditional accuracy), outperforming BPJDet/HierR-CNN and extending to animal pose.
> 
> **2. Implicit bias of self-supervised objectives & interpretability**
> - **How JEPA Avoids Noisy Features: The Implicit Bias of Deep Linear Self Distillation Networks** (NeurIPS 2024). Theory (deep linear networks) showing latent-space prediction (MSE-type JEPA) is biased to "influential" features while reconstruction (MAE) tracks high-variance/noisy features; ImageNet CCA experiments.
> - **On the Similarities of Embeddings in Contrastive Learning** (InfoNCE vs. variance-reduction/MSE auxiliary loss; CIFAR-10/100, ImageNet, top-1 accuracy).
> - **LDReg: Local Dimensionality Regularized Self-Supervised Learning** (ICLR 2024). Counteracts dimensional collapse of feature embeddings; evaluated on ImageNet linear eval and COCO detection/segmentation.
> 
> **3. Memory-lean optimizers**
> - **Memory Efficient Optimizers with 4-bit States** (NeurIPS 2023). Quantizes Adam/AdamW first/second moments to 4-bit via smaller blocks, zero-point-excluding linear quantizer, rank-1 normalization, and factorization; matches 32-bit on GLUE, SQuAD, ImageNet (Swin-T), E2E-NLG, WMT14, LLaMA-7B/13B/33B fine-tuning (Alpaca); discussed alongside LoRA; up to 57.7% memory savings.
> 
> **4. Modular diffusion library for decision-making**
> - **CleanDiffuser: An Easy-to-use Modularized Library for Diffusion Models in Decision Making** (NeurIPS 2024). Decouples diffusion models/solvers (DDPM, DDIM, DPM-Solver(++), EDM, RectifiedFlow), network architectures (incl. transformer backbones), and guided sampling; benchmarks 9 algorithms on D4RL and Robomimic/PushT/Relay-Kitchen (37 environments).
> 
> **5. Dale's Law recurrent networks, spectral perspective**
> - **Learning better with Dale's Law: A Spectral Perspective** (NeurIPS 2023). Explains why E/I (Dale's Law) RNNs train poorly: not sign constraints but initial singular-value spectrum (multimodal/dispersed ColEI vs. quarter-circle DANN/standard RNNs); normalised SVD entropy predicts performance; sequential MNIST, Penn Tree Bank, object recognition, adding task.
> 
> ## Development Trend of Their Methods
> 
> - **Detection (1):** from multi-stage, anchor-based, body-to-part representations → **one-stage anchor-free dense prediction** with a single part-to-body offset, multi-scale features, and task-alignment learning, scaling to large benchmarks (COCO) and new domains (animals).
> - **Self-supervised learning (2):** from purely empirical SSL → **theoretical/dynamical analysis of implicit bias** (deep linear networks), showing latent-space MSE-type objectives select semantic "influential" features over noisy variance; plus geometric analyses (dimensional collapse, embedding similarity) to regularize and interpret feature spaces.
> - **Optimizers (3):** steady **bit-width reduction 32→8→4-bit** enabled by better quantization (smaller blocks, zero-point exclusion, rank-1 normalization, factorization), making fine-tuning of large Transformers/LLaMA (incl. LoRA-style PEFT) near-lossless at much lower memory.
> - **Diffusion decision-making (4):** from tightly coupled algorithm-specific code → **modular, decoupled libraries** (diffusion models, network architectures, guided sampling as separate building blocks) with unified APIs and reproducible benchmarks.
> - **Biologically constrained RNNs (5):** explanation shifted from **sign constraints to spectral properties** (singular value distribution, SVD entropy at initialization) as the determinant of learning, guiding better architectures/initializations for E/I networks.
> 
> Overall: a common trend toward **unification and simplification** (one-stage, modular, decoupled design), **efficiency without accuracy loss** (4-bit states, fewer sampling steps), and replacing empirical heuristics with **theoretical/spectral accounts** of why methods work.

**Gold（保持结果文件中的原始内容；部分条目本身为序列化字典字符串）**

Gold 1：

> Integrated development trends across the stack (2019–2025) show a clear shift toward scalable, modular, and resource-efficient methods that preserve robustness and interpretability:
> 
> 1) Perception (crowded scenes, part-to-person association)
> - Trend: from two‑stage, anchor‑based heuristics to one‑stage, anchor‑free detectors with explicit part‑to‑body links.
> - Early approaches matched parts to bodies via separate stages or anchor-heavy heads; 2023 anchor-based joint detectors extended representations but scaled poorly with more parts. PBADet (ICLR 2024) consolidates to a single part‑to‑body center offset on anchor‑free heads, enabling: (a) scalability w.r.t. number of parts (representation length no longer grows per part), (b) robustness in occlusion/crowds (COCO/CrowdHuman), and (c) simpler decoding and stable supervision via a one‑to‑one offset that remains valid even when some parts are invisible. The field is converging on multi‑scale, task‑aligned, end‑to‑end training on COCO‑style data with anchor‑free heads for better efficiency and flexibility.
> 
> 2) Decision-making with diffusion models (planners, policies, data synthesis)
> - Trend: from monolithic, task‑specific DM code to modular, solver‑agnostic pipelines that unify planners, policies, and data synthesizers.
> - Sampling efficiency and guidance: CleanDiffuser (NeurIPS 2024) abstracts SDE/ODE backbones (DDPM, DDIM, DPM‑Solver(++), EDM, Rectified Flow) from networks and guidance (classifier/classifier‑free), enabling cross‑solver swaps and step reductions after training. Empirically, 5 sampling steps are often sufficient; higher steps can even degrade performance in some RL tasks (sampling degradation), pushing a trend toward fewer‑step, stable solvers and warm‑starting for real‑time use.
> - Role evolution: diffusion policies increasingly outperform diffusion planners on long‑horizon, sparse‑reward navigation benchmarks (e.g., AntMaze), shifting emphasis from plan‑selection to policy learning with diffusion and Q‑value guidance (e.g., DQL/IDQL). Guidance is trending toward conservative or low‑weight settings to avoid OOD trajectories; masking and inpainting are standard for conditioning history/goals.
> - Architectures: growing use of transformer‑based conditional guidance and FiLM‑conditioned UNets for visuomotor policies, balanced with practical trade‑offs in model size vs inference time.
> 
> 3) Optimizers under memory constraints (scaling LoRA/SFT backbones)
> - Trend: from 32‑/16‑bit to 8‑bit, now to 4‑bit optimizer states with task‑aware quantization.
> - 4‑bit states (NeurIPS 2023) push the boundary by solving key bottlenecks: (a) a zero‑point problem in the second moment (addressed by linear mapping without zero), (b) heterogeneous outliers (handled by smaller blocks and rank‑1 normalization), and (c) hybrid factorization for second moments. These methods retain accuracy across NLU/MT/vision and instruction‑tuning while cutting memory and improving offload throughput—well aligned with LoRA‑based fine‑tuning of large SFT backbones under tight memory budgets.
> 
> 4) Self‑supervised pretraining bias and interpretability (JEPA vs. MAE)
> - Trend: from reconstruction (MAE) to joint‑embedding prediction (JEPA) with self‑distillation.
> - Theoretical results (NeurIPS 2024) show deep JEPA’s implicit bias toward influential (high regression‑coefficient) features rather than merely high‑variance ones prioritized by MAE. Practically, this favors semantic, less noisy visual features—consistent with objectives that avoid overfitting to pixel noise and support more interpretable, transferable representations for perception‑to‑control pipelines.
> 
> 5) Biologically constrained time‑series modules (Dale’s Law in RNNs)
> - Trend: from direct sign‑constrained ColEI RNNs (often unstable) to EI‑respecting architectures with spectrum‑aware initialization and training.
> - Recurrent DANNs (NeurIPS 2023) and analyses show spectral properties (singular value clustering) are more critical than sign constraints per se for stable learning. Normalized SVD entropy predicts performance; balanced E/I ratios and larger widths improve spectra. This shifts the design focus from hard EI constraints to spectrum shaping for stable time‑series models that still respect excitatory/inhibitory separation.
> 
> Cross‑cutting themes and scalability patterns
> - Decoupling and modularity: anchor‑free heads with compact offsets; diffusion frameworks that separate backbone/solver/guidance/architecture; optimizer quantization that decouples moments and normalization; spectrum‑first RNN design. Each promotes scalability (more parts, longer horizons, larger backbones) without proportional complexity growth.
> - Efficiency without sacrificing robustness: fewer diffusion steps (≈5) with solver swaps; 4‑bit optimizers retaining accuracy; one‑stage detectors with constant‑length representations; spectrum‑aware EI networks stabilizing small models.
> - Guidance toward safety and interpretability: conservative sampling in control to avoid OOD; JEPA’s bias toward predictive, less‑noisy features; spectrum metrics guiding stable EI RNNs.
> 
> In summary, from 2023 to 2024 the stack converges on compact, modular, and resource‑aware designs: one‑stage anchor‑free association for vision; unified diffusion pipelines with transformer‑conditioned guidance for control; 4‑bit optimizer states enabling low‑memory LoRA fine‑tuning; JEPA‑style pretraining to emphasize semantic, low‑noise features; and EI RNNs stabilized via spectral shaping. This trajectory improves scalability and deployability in crowded COCO‑style perception and diffusion‑driven robot control under tight compute/memory budgets.

> **1. Vision front-end (hand/face → person association in crowded scenes)**
> - **PBADet** (08b70bc3...): one-stage, anchor-free part-body association detector that links hands/face/feet to their parent person via a single part-to-body center offset, evaluated on COCO-HumanParts, BodyHands, and CrowdHuman.
> 
> **2. Diffusion-driven control with transformer-conditioned guidance**
> - **CleanDiffuser** (c122328b...): modular library covering diffusion planners, policies, and data synthesizers; includes the transformer-based Diffusion Policy (cross-attention conditioning, DiT/CNN-Unet options) and guided sampling.
> - **RTB — Reward Trajectory Balance** (756d1e62...): reward-guided diffusion for unbiased posterior sampling, applied to offline RL control (score-based behavior prior) and Stable Diffusion fine-tuning.
> - **Universal Guidance for Diffusion Models** (9134ed60...): training-free guidance of frozen diffusion models by arbitrary differentiable modalities (segmentation, detection, face, style) via forward/backward gradient and USR refinement.
> 
> **3. Low-memory optimizers + LoRA fine-tuning of large SFT backbones**
> - **4-bit Optimizers** (8d5e1455...): compresses Adam/AdamW optimizer states to 4-bit (block size, rank-1/linear second-moment quantizers, zero-point exclusion), enabling LoRA/instruction fine-tuning of LLaMA-7B/13B/33B on a single 80GB GPU with up to 57.7% memory savings and accuracy matching 32-bit.
> 
> **4. Self-supervised pretraining avoiding noisy pixels / improving interpretability**
> - **JEPA paper: "Why JEPA Self-Distillation Avoids Noisy Features"** (40fde037...): shows JEPA (latent-space prediction/self-distillation) is implicitly biased toward high-influence abstract features and suppresses unpredictable pixel-level noise, unlike MAE-style pixel reconstruction.
> - **HASSOD** (ef986d59...): fully self-supervised object detection with hierarchical whole/part/subpart composition, explicitly adding interpretability and controllability.
> 
> **5. Time-series modules respecting excitatory/inhibitory separation with stable training**
> - **Dale's Law RNN paper** (e63a94c4...): analyzes why sign-constrained E/I (ColEI) RNNs train poorly and shows the issue is spectral (multimodal singular-value spectra), not sign constraints; DANN-style architectures plus gradient clipping restore stable learning.
> 
> **Development trend across these methods:**
> - **Vision**: from multi-stage, anchor-based, body-to-part pipelines (HierR-CNN, BPJDet) toward simpler one-stage, anchor-free, part-to-body representations that scale to larger part sets without accuracy loss.
> - **Diffusion**: from text-conditioned generative models to flexible, training-free universal guidance and reward-based posterior sampling, and from pure generation to decision-making (planners/policies) with transformer backbones for conditioning.
> - **Optimization/adaptation**: from full-precision, full-parameter training toward progressively lower-bit optimizer states (32→8→4-bit) combined with parameter-efficient tuning (LoRA, delta tuning) for memory-constrained fine-tuning of huge backbones.
> - **Self-supervised learning**: from pixel-space reconstruction (MAE) toward latent-space predictive objectives (JEPA) that favor abstract, noise-robust features, plus explicit interpretability (hierarchical part-to-whole structure).
> - **Biologically constrained networks**: from naive sign-constrained EI networks that learn poorly to architectures with healthy spectral properties (DANN) and diagnostic/analytic tools (normalized SVD entropy, gradient clipping) that enable stable training.

**community 最终答案**

> Based on the provided collection, the papers covering your stack end-to-end are:
> 
> **Vision (hand/face→person association in crowded, COCO-style scenes):**
> - **PBADet** (One-Stage Anchor-Free Part-Body Association Detection) — treats human parts as objects linked to a parent body via a single part-to-body center offset; evaluated on BodyHands, COCOHumanParts and CrowdHuman for face/hand-body association.
> 
> **Control (diffusion planners/policies + transformer-conditioned guidance):**
> - **CleanDiffuser** — modular library covering diffusion planners (Diffuser), policies (Diffusion Policy with action chunking, FiLM conditioning, and transformer-based cross-attention fusion), and data synthesizers.
> - **Universal Guidance** — training-free guidance that steers frozen diffusion models with arbitrary differentiable guidance functions (segmentation, object detection, face, classifier signals).
> - (Optionally) **RTB (Reward Trajectory Balance)** — unbiased reward-guided posterior sampling for diffusion/flow models, applied to continuous control with a score-based behavior prior.
> 
> **Efficient adaptation (low-memory optimizers + LoRA SFT of large backbones):**
> - **4-bit Optimizers** — quantized/factorized 4-bit Adam/AdamW states (up to 57.7% memory savings), validated on LLaMA instruction fine-tuning.
> - **NEFTune** — noisy-embedding instruction fine-tuning (works with QLoRA) that substantially improves SFT conversational quality of LLaMA models.
> 
> **Self-supervised pretraining (avoid noisy pixels, better interpretability):**
> - **Why JEPA Avoids Noisy Features** — JEPA latent-space self-distillation implicitly biases toward high-influence features and suppresses noisy pixel-level information versus MAE.
> - (Optionally) **HASSOD** — hierarchical adaptive self-supervised detection that adds whole/part/subpart structure for interpretability.
> 
> **Time-series with E/I separation but stable training:**
> - **Why Dale's Law Constrained RNNs Learn Poorly** — explains E/I sign-constrained (ColEI) RNNs' instability via spectral properties (singular-value pathology, normalized SVD entropy) and shows DANN reparameterization + gradient clipping restore stable learning.
> - (Optionally) **BSO/T-BSO** — binary spiking online optimization for resource-constrained, memory-efficient and stable training of spiking networks.
> 
> **Development trend of the methods:**
> - **Perception:** multi-stage or body-to-part detectors (HierR-CNN, BPJDet) → compact one-stage, anchor-free, part-to-body association (PBADet) with task-alignment learning, more scalable to multiple parts and even animal datasets.
> - **Control:** diffusion models evolved from conditioning-specific training → training-free universal guidance and reward-guided posterior sampling (RTB), with transformer (DiT/cross-attention) backbones and action-chunking policies replacing earlier 1D-Unet designs.
> - **Adaptation:** full 32-bit optimizer states → 8-bit → 4-bit quantized/factorized states; full fine-tuning → parameter-efficient LoRA/QLoRA, plus regularization tricks like noisy embeddings (NEFTune).
> - **Self-supervised learning:** pixel-space reconstruction (MAE) → latent-space predictive/self-distillation (JEPA) that inherently suppresses noisy features, and self-supervised detection moving toward hierarchical, interpretable part-whole structures.
> - **E/I time-series:** sign-constrained networks shifted from "why they fail" analysis (spectral pathology, gradient clipping) toward reparameterized (DANN) and spiking online/binary optimization (BSO/T-BSO) that keep biological E/I separation while achieving stable, low-memory training.

Gold 1：

> {'answer': 'Across these works, a clear progression emerges toward methods that are both scalable and robust under realistic constraints, with a consistent focus on compatibility with modern architectures (Transformers, ViTs, ResNet-like backbones) and standard training pipelines (cross-entropy/MSE losses, fine-tuning, LoRA). 1) Memory-light training (2023→): Optimizer-state compression drops from 8-bit to 4-bit for Adam/AdamW and SGD by addressing quantization outliers and the zero-point problem in second moments. Rank-1 normalization and smaller block sizes make moment quantization reliable; factorizing second moments further cuts memory. These 4-bit optimizers retain accuracy (e.g., SQuAD EM/F1, GLUE, ImageNet, MT BLEU) while enabling larger Transformer/LLM fine-tuning (including LoRA) and faster offloaded training—marking a sustained trend toward hardware-efficient training that preserves CE/MSE objectives. 2) Offline combinatorial learning (2025→): The field moves from online CMAB to Off-CMAB, adopting pessimistic LCBs (CLCB) and formal coverage conditions (∞-norm/1-norm TPM) to guarantee near-optimal suboptimality gaps. This shift reflects practical constraints (no safe online exploration) and supports nontrivial combinatorial decision spaces (learning-to-rank/cascading bandits with ranked lists, LLM caching, influence maximization), handling OOD actions and general feedback. Evaluation centers on suboptimality gap with real tasks, complementing standard metrics (e.g., precision/recall/F1 for QA and ranking tasks used elsewhere). 3) Biologically grounded recurrent models (2023→): Dale’s Law–respecting RNNs evolve from naïve sign-constrained “ColEI” partitions (poor learning) to reparameterized EI designs (DANN) where spectral properties—rather than sign constraints—govern performance. Normalized SVD entropy becomes a predictive diagnostic; spectra that are clustered/unimodal (like standard RNNs/DANNs) yield stable training across sizes and EI ratios. The development trend favors spectral initialization/regularization over hard sign partitioning to achieve scalable, biologically consistent deep networks. 4) Anchor-free vision detection (2024→): Part–body association moves from anchor-based, body-to-part offsets to a single part-to-body offset in one-stage anchor-free detectors. This reduces representation length, improves decoding, and scales gracefully to multiple parts, with state-of-the-art results on COCOHumanParts/CrowdHuman. Training uses standard optimizers (e.g., SGD), task-aligned losses and modern detection heads; the approach coexists with Transformer detectors (DETR variants) and CNN/YOLO heads, emphasizing deployable, efficient multi-part association. 5) Self-supervised learning in latent space (2024→): JEPA replaces pixel-space reconstruction (MAE) with latent prediction, and theoretical analysis shows a deep-encoder implicit bias toward influential (high regression-coefficient) features, avoiding noisy low-value signals. As depth increases, JEPA prioritizes predictive, low-variance semantics—aligning with practice on ViTs and JEPA variants (stop-grad, MSE in latent space), and complementing cosine-similarity-based non-contrastive objectives referenced in the JEPA literature. Overall trend: • Efficiency first: quantized (4-bit) optimizers and anchor-free detection cut memory/compute without sacrificing accuracy, enabling broader fine-tuning (including End-to-end LoRA) on large Transformers/LLMs. • Offline safety and coverage: pessimistic, coverage-aware CLCB bridges theory and practice for combinatorial decisions (ranking, caching), reducing reliance on risky online exploration. • Spectral over constraints: EI RNNs shift from literal sign constraints to spectrum-shaped initialization/regularization, with NSE guiding scalable designs. • Semantics over pixels: JEPA’s latent-space prediction and deep encoders systematically steer learning toward high-influence, less noisy features. These trajectories collectively prioritize scalable accuracy under real-world constraints (memory, offline-only data, biological plausibility), while remaining compatible with standard losses (CE/MSE), similarity objectives, and mainstream Transformer/ResNet-style backbones.'}

**naive 最终答案**

> Based on the available documents, here are the papers matching each theme and the development trend of their methods:
> 
> ## 1. Memory-light optimizer states (4-bit Adam/AdamW & SGD)
> **Paper:** *4-bit Optimizers: Training Large Models with 4-bit Optimizer States* (NeurIPS 2023; doc `8d5e1455…`)
> **Trend:** 32-bit → 8-bit block-wise quantization (Dettmers) → **4-bit**. The authors analyze outlier patterns in first/second moments, use smaller blocks (B128), joint row/column (rank-1) normalization, and solve the "zero-point problem" of the second moment with a linear quantizer that excludes zero; optionally factorize the second moment (Adafactor-style) for extra savings. The compression framework is generic over SGDM/Adam/AdamW and includes a convergence proof for quantized SGD(M). Results: lossless convergence on RoBERTa-L (GLUE/SQuAD), Swin-T (ImageNet), GPT-2, Transformer-Base (WMT14), LLaMA-7B/13B/33B fine-tuning, up to 57.7% memory saved, LLaMA-7B trainable on one 80GB GPU (Transformers + LoRA-compatible fine-tuning workflows are covered).
> 
> ## 2. Offline learning for combinatorial bandit-style decision spaces
> **Paper:** *Offline Learning for Combinatorial Multi-armed Bandits* (Off-CMAB; doc `d8faaa7f…`)
> **Trend:** Online CMAB (costly exploration) → **offline learning from pre-collected datasets** (pessimism principle from offline RL). Core algorithm CLCB combines pessimistic reward estimates (lower confidence bounds) with combinatorial solvers, under two novel data-coverage conditions, achieving a near-optimal suboptimality gap matching the lower bound up to a log factor. Applications: cascading bandits (learning-to-rank), LLM caching (36% inference-cost reduction), and influence maximization. *Caveat: this paper evaluates by suboptimality gap/regret, not F1/Precision — F1/Precision-based evaluation in the collection appears in PBADet (part detection) and causal-discovery papers (G-Sim, RLCD), not in the bandit paper.*
> 
> ## 3. Biologically informed recurrent models with E/I structure (spectral view)
> **Paper:** *Learning better with Dale's Law: A Spectral Perspective* (NeurIPS 2023; doc `e63a94c4…`)
> **Trend:** Naive E/I partitioning (ColEI, column sign constraints) hurts learning not because of sign constraints but because of **pathological singular-value spectra at initialization** (multimodal, dispersed — rank-one nilpotent column-mean structure), vs. the unimodal quarter-circle/Marchenko–Pastur spectra of standard RNNs and recurrent DANN (Dale's ANNs). Spectral properties matter more than sign constraints; normalised SVD entropy (NSE) predicts performance, and gradient clipping mitigates the deficit — motivating spectral regularization/initialization for E/I networks.
> 
> ## 4. Anchor-free detectors for part–body association on COCO
> **Paper:** *PBADet: One-Stage Anchor-Free Part-Body Association* (ICLR 2024; doc `08b70bc3…`)
> **Trend:** Two-stage/anchor-based part–body detection (BodyHands, BPJDet body-to-part offsets, HierR-CNN) → **one-stage anchor-free detection with a single part-to-body center offset** over multi-scale feature maps, with classification/localization/displacement branches and task-alignment learning (TOOD). Validated on BodyHands, COCOHumanParts, CrowdHuman (face-body), and AnimalPose/AP-10K; on the COCO validation set it beats the pose estimator ED-Pose in Precision/Recall/F1 for hands/feet and reaches ~43 AP on COCOHumanParts with a smaller model. (Backbones are YOLO variants; COCOHumanParts comparisons include ResNet-50-based baselines such as FCOS/RetinaNet/Faster-RCNN.)
> 
> ## 5. JEPA / self-supervised learning avoiding noisy latent features
> **Papers:** *Why JEPA Self-Distillation Avoids Noisy Features* (NeurIPS 2024; doc `40fde037…`); *LDReg: Local Dimensionality Regularized Self-Supervised Learning* (ICLR 2024; doc `51526068…`)
> **Trend:** Contrastive SSL → **non-contrastive self-distillation JEPA** (BYOL, data2vec, SimSiam, I-JEPA, V-JEPA), which predicts in latent space rather than reconstructing pixels (MAE). Deep-linear analysis proves JEPA has an implicit bias toward high-influence features (large regression coefficients), suppressing noisy/high-variance features, with depth strengthening the effect; on ImageNet, I-JEPA aligns faster with the low-variance PCA subspace containing perceptual features than MAE. LDReg complements this by countering (local) dimensional collapse via a Fisher-Rao local-intrinsic-dimensionality regularizer, improving SimCLR/BYOL/MAE on ImageNet with **ResNet-50 and ViT-B**, transfer learning, and COCO detection — using cosine-similarity-style objectives.
> 
> **Notes on your compatibility criteria:** Transformers are covered by the 4-bit optimizer paper (RoBERTa/GPT-2/LLaMA) and LDReg (ViT-B); ResNet-50 appears in LDReg and contrastive-learning baselines; cosine similarity appears in contrastive/JEPA objectives; SGD/AdamW and fine-tuning including LoRA are covered by the 4-bit optimizer paper and the Hessian-structure paper (which shows LoRA-only fine-tuning does not induce the power-law Hessian structure of full fine-tuning). No document in the collection explicitly proposes an "End-to-end LoRA" method, and no bandit paper is evaluated by F1/Precision — those gaps cannot be established from the context.

**community 最终答案**

> ## Matched papers
> 
> 1. **Memory-light optimizer states** → *4-bit Optimizers: Training Large Models with 4-bit Optimizer States* (NeurIPS 2023). Compresses Adam/AdamW (and the framework covers SGDM/Adam/AdamW generically) states from 32-bit to 4-bit via smaller blocks (B128), rank-1 normalization, zero-point-excluding linear quantization, and optional second-moment factorization; lossless vs 32-bit on RoBERTa-L, Swin-T, GPT-2, Transformer, LLaMA-7B/13B/33B fine-tuning (Alpaca, MMLU), up to ~57.7% memory savings. Related: *MLMC for Mitigating Compression Bias in Distributed Learning* (SGD/Top-k/2-bit quantization on ResNet18, BERT fine-tuning).
> 
> 2. **Offline combinatorial bandit learning** → *Offline Learning for Combinatorial Multi-armed Bandits* (Off-CMAB/CLCB): first offline framework for combinatorial MAB with pessimistic (lower-confidence-bound) reward estimation, coverage conditions, near-optimal suboptimality gap; applications to cascading/ranking, LLM caching, influence maximization. **Caveat:** its evaluation is by suboptimality gap/regret, *not* F1/Precision — no bandit paper in the collection uses F1/Precision (F1/Precision appears only in detection/causal-discovery works like PBADet, GEEA, G-Sim, RLCD).
> 
> 3. **E/I recurrent models** → *Why Dale's Law Constrained Recurrent Neural Networks Learn Poorly* (NeurIPS 2023): shows E/I (Dale's-law) RNNs fail mainly due to pathological singular-value spectra at initialization, not sign constraints; spectrum transplants and normalized SVD entropy diagnose it; DANN reparameterization recovers standard-RNN-like spectra. This is spectral *analysis/constraint*, not a spectral-regularization training term per se.
> 
> 4. **Anchor-free part–body detection** → *PBADet: One-Stage Anchor-Free Part-Body Association Detection* (ICLR 2024): single part-to-body center offset on YOLOv5/YOLOv7 anchor-free heads with task-alignment learning; validated on BodyHands and COCO-HumanParts, beating BPJDet/HierR-CNN, with Precision/Recall/F1 gains over ED-Pose on COCO; extends to animals.
> 
> 5. **JEPA avoiding noisy features** → *How JEPA Avoids Noisy Features: The Implicit Bias of Deep Linear Self-Distillation Networks* (NeurIPS 2024): deep-linear analysis showing JEPA/self-distillation learns high-influence, low-variance (semantic) features and suppresses noisy ones, unlike MAE reconstruction; ImageNet I-JEPA aligns with perceptual PCA subspace. Related: *LDReg* (local-dimensionality regularization against collapse, ResNet-50/ViT-B) and *On the Similarities of Embeddings in Contrastive Learning* (cosine-similarity theory, variance-reduction loss for small batches).
> 
> **On LoRA/fine-tuning:** no paper titled "End-to-end LoRA" exists in the collection; LoRA appears as a tool — 4-bit optimizer fine-tunes LLaMA (with LoRA in related work), *Investigating the Overlooked Hessian Structure* studies LoRA adapters on TinyLlama, *Agreement-on-the-Line* tests LoRA/IA3/BitFit PEFT, *NFTS* searches adapters/fine-tuning for ResNet/ViT.
> 
> ## Development trend
> 
> - **Optimizers:** 32-bit → 8-bit → 4-bit state compression with increasingly sophisticated quantizers (block/rank-1, zero-point exclusion, factorization), keeping accuracy lossless and integrating with fine-tuning (LLaMA/LoRA, FSDP) and distributed compression (MLMC, SGD).
> - **Decision-making:** online exploration-based bandits → offline/pessimistic (CLCB) learning with data-coverage guarantees, applied to practical systems (ranking, LLM caching, influence maximization).
> - **Bio-plausible RNNs:** from merely enforcing E/I sign constraints (which hurt learning) → recognizing that spectral properties at initialization dominate, motivating spectral-aware initialization/design rather than raw constraint.
> - **Detection:** anchor-based/multi-stage body-to-part offsets (BPJDet) → one-stage anchor-free part-to-body offsets (PBADet), more scalable, better COCO-based AP and Precision/Recall/F1, generalizing to animals.
> - **Self-supervised learning:** reconstruction (MAE, learns noisy/pixel-level features) → latent-space JEPA self-distillation, theoretically shown to prioritize predictive, low-variance features and suppress noise; complemented by dimensionality regularization (LDReg) and cosine-similarity variance control.
> 
> Overall, the trend is from brute-force constraints toward principled, analyzable designs (quantization-aware statistics, pessimism/coverage, spectral and implicit-bias analysis) that deliver robustness/efficiency gains on realistic workloads (Transformers, ResNet-50; cross-entropy/MSE/cosine losses; fine-tuning/LoRA).

### paperscope:trend:45 — 评分与执行路径对照

**问题：** We’re building an edge AI system that must: (a) detect and associate body parts (e.g., hands→person) from video streams with high precision, (b) dynamically choose between chain-of-thought and a direct answer to save tokens, and (c) fine-tune large attention-based Transformers under very tight VRAM; we also have a small EI-constrained RNN handling time-series signals. Are there works showing how to use token-probability trends to trigger or skip CoT, quantize optimizer states to ~4-bit for memory-efficient fine-tuning, design anchor-free part–body association models, and analyze spectral properties to stabilize EI RNNs while guiding self-distillation to ignore noisy features? Ideally they report CE/MSE objectives, discuss feedforward heads and Transformer-based conditional guidance (ResNet-50–class backbones are fine), and provide implementation diagrams we can follow.Please summarize the development trend of their methods.

**Gold（保持结果文件中的原始内容；部分条目本身为序列化字典字符串）**

Gold 1：

> {'answer': 'Across the five works, the methods show a clear progression toward more scalable, efficient, and principled control of computation and memory, with measurable signals guiding when and how to expend resources.\n\n1) Part–body association in vision moves from anchors to lean, one-stage anchor-free designs\n- Earlier joint detectors extended anchor-based heads (e.g., BPJDet), increasing representation length as parts grow and complicating post-processing.\n- The ICLR 2024 PBADet reframes the problem anchor-free: one offset per part to the body center on multi-scale feature maps, plus a dedicated association head. This trims the representation, decouples the number of parts from head size, and simplifies decoding. It trains with established detection objectives (IoU/DFL for boxes, a classification loss, and a supervised association loss), and provides pipeline/representation diagrams. Trend: from multi-stage, anchor-heavy coupling to a single-stage, anchor-free formulation that scales gracefully to many parts and stays robust when parts are occluded.\n\n2) Chain-of-thought (CoT) evolves from “always-on” prompting to token-efficient, signal-driven gating\n- CoT historically improves math/symbolic problems but can be neutral/negative elsewhere; the 2025 Token Signature study quantifies this using the monotonicity of decoded token probabilities.\n- Two indicators (Instance SC and Aggregated SC via Spearman correlation over the first ~50 tokens) predict whether CoT will help on a benchmark; Aggregated SC reaches ~89% accuracy across diverse tasks.\n- A lightweight logistic model (trained with cross-entropy) turns the instance-level signal into Dynamic CoT, choosing between CoT and direct answer. It preserves accuracy while cutting tokens by ~35–39%, and the decision transfers to closed-source models via voting across small open-source models. Trend: from static CoT prompts to dynamic, probability-trend–based routing that saves compute without sacrificing precision.\n\n3) Optimizer-state compression drives fine-tuning from 8-bit to robust 4-bit, with principled fixes for failure modes\n- Earlier low-precision optimizers stabilized at 8-bit; the NeurIPS 2023 4-bit study shows first/second moments have complex outliers and that block size and mapping matter.\n- Practical advances: smaller blocks for first moment; rank-1 normalization (row/column max) for second moment; exclusion of the zero point (linear quantizer) to avoid catastrophic mis-scaling of 1/sqrt(v). A hybrid path factorizes second moments and quantizes 1D states.\n- Results span NLU, MT, image classification, and LLM instruction tuning: comparable accuracy to full precision, reduced memory (up to ~57% total training memory with optimizer offload), and throughput gains. Trend: memory-efficient fine-tuning shifts from “coarse 8-bit blocks” to carefully engineered 4-bit quantization/factorization, explicitly addressing zero-point errors and outliers to remain accurate under tight VRAM.\n\n4) EI-constrained RNNs shift from sign constraints to spectrum-aware design for stability and learning\n- The NeurIPS 2023 Dale’s Law work shows sign constraints (ColEI) alone often impair learning; the dominant factor is the singular value spectrum at initialization.\n- Good performance correlates with unimodal, clustered singular values (as in standard RNNs/DANNs). Normalized SVD entropy (NSE) emerges as a predictive metric; higher NSE → better learning. Small networks with few inhibitory units worsen spectra and learning; larger or better-balanced EI ratios help.\n- Design guidance: prioritize spectrum shaping over only enforcing signs; DANN-style recurrent parameterizations preserve favorable spectra while respecting Dale’s Law. Trend: from “EI sign partitioning” to spectrum-centric initialization and diagnostics (NSE) that stabilize small EI RNNs for time-series under tight constraints.\n\n5) Self-distillation in JEPA clarifies an implicit bias toward influential (less noisy) features as depth grows\n- The NeurIPS 2024 deep linear analysis shows JEPA/StopGrad objectives (MSE in latent space) bias deep encoders to learn features with high regression coefficients (predictive/influential), unlike MAE which chases high covariance (often noisy).\n- The critical-time dynamics and fixed points reveal a depth-dependent preference: deeper JEPA encoders prioritize predictive, lower-variance directions and suppress noisy ones—supporting practice where JEPA-style self-distillation yields abstract, robust features.\n- Trend: from reconstruction losses that track variance to latent prediction that favors stable, high-signal features as networks deepen—useful for building compact, noise-averse representations under edge constraints.\n\nOverall development trends\n- Scalability: vision association compresses representation and decouples parts; CoT selection scales via transferable instance-level signals; optimizer states shrink to 4-bit and factorize; EI RNNs scale with spectrum-aware design.\n- Efficiency and conditional guidance: token probability trends gate expensive CoT; low-bit states plus factorization enable large Transformers under strict VRAM; EI RNN spectra and JEPA’s bias both reduce waste on noisy directions.\n- Principled signals and diagnostics: Spearman-based Token Signature for CoT, NSE for EI RNNs, zero-point analysis for second moment quantization, and deep-linear dynamics for JEPA provide measurable criteria shown in the papers’ diagrams/algorithms.\n- Time pattern: 2023–2025 sees a shift from heuristic, one-size-fits-all (static CoT, anchor-based detectors, 8-bit states, sign-only EI constraints) toward targeted, signal-driven and theory-backed methods (anchor-free association heads, 4-bit quantization with rank-1 normalization and zero-point fixes, spectrum metrics for EI RNNs, and JEPA’s influential-feature bias), with broad validation across tasks and models.'}

**naive 最终答案**

> Based on the provided documents, all four required capabilities are covered:
> 
> **1. Token-probability trends → trigger/skip CoT (TokenSignature, ICML 2025)**
> Uses the monotonicity of token-probability distributions over the decoding path (Spearman correlation, "Instance SC"/"Aggregated SC", first 50 tokens) as a predictor of CoT gain. A logistic-regression-based **Dynamic CoT** then picks CoT vs. direct answer per instance, cutting token consumption by ~39% while matching the better strategy (transferable to closed-source models via voting).
> 
> **2. 4-bit optimizer states (NeurIPS 2023, "4-bit Optimizers")**
> Pushes optimizer states to 4-bit via small-block (B128) quantization of the first moment, rank-1 normalization + zero-point-excluding linear quantizer for the second moment, optionally factorizing the second moment. Matches 32-bit AdamW on GLUE/SQuAD/ImageNet/MT/LLaMA fine-tuning with up to ~58% memory savings (LLaMA-7B on one 80 GB GPU), with convergence proof in the appendix.
> 
> **3. Anchor-free part–body association (PBADet, ICLR 2024)**
> One-stage, anchor-free; extends anchor-free object detection with a **single part-to-body center offset** (one-to-one, always valid) across multi-scale feature maps, with classification/localization/displacement branches (3-layer conv heads) and task-alignment learning; backbone-agnostic (YOLOv5/7/8). Provides a pipeline diagram and CE/MSE-style detection/association losses; ablations show association loss, multi-scale offsets, and task-alignment each help.
> 
> **4. Spectral stability of EI RNNs + self-distillation noise suppression (two papers)**
> - *Why Dale's Law Constrained RNNs Learn Poorly*: shows singular-value spectrum at initialization (not sign constraints) governs EI-RNN learning; recurrent **DANN** (Dale's ANN) architectures have standard-RNN-like unimodal spectra, while ColEI networks have multimodal dispersed spectra. **Normalized SVD entropy (NSE)** predicts performance before training and guides stable design.
> - *How JEPA Avoids Noisy Features*: deep-linear analysis shows JEPA **self-distillation** has an implicit bias toward high-influence (low-variance, semantic) features and suppresses noisy features, with depth strengthening the effect (verified on ImageNet via CCA).
> 
> Additional supporting works: **Universal Guidance (ICLR 2024)** provides Transformer/diffusion-based conditional guidance using a ResNet-50-FPN Faster-RCNN guidance head with anchor-classification + box-regression CE losses; **CleanDiffuser** offers decoupled, pipeline-style implementation diagrams (network → guided sampling → training assembly).
> 
> **Development trend:** methods move from multi-stage/heuristic or anchor-based pipelines to **unified one-stage designs** (PBADet's single part-to-body offset vs. BPJDet's redundant body-to-part offsets); from heuristic/hand-crafted criteria to **learning-based dynamic routing** driven by decoded-signal statistics (Dynamic CoT from token distributions); from 8-bit to **4-bit (and hybrid factorized) optimizer-state compression** that is lossless vs. full precision; and from treating sign constraints/architecture as the bottleneck to **spectral/analytic characterizations** (NSE, deep-linear implicit-bias of self-distillation) that are predictive and theoretically grounded, each accompanied by implementation/pipeline diagrams and explicit CE/MSE objectives for reproducibility.

**community 最终答案**

> Yes—the collection contains works covering all four of your needs, and each shows a clear methodological trend. Here is the trend summary:
> 
> ## 1. Token-probability trends to trigger/skip CoT
> **TokenSignature** (LLM decoding feature analysis) — Trend: moving from "always use CoT" to *instance-level dynamic routing*. They define a **Token Signature** (the evolution of the token-probability distribution along the greedy decoding path) and use **Spearman correlation** as indicators: **Instance SC** (per-question, first ~50 tokens, 69.6% accuracy) and **Aggregated SC** (benchmark-level, 89.2%). A logistic-regression **Dynamic CoT** classifier then selects CoT vs. direct answer per question, cutting token consumption ~39% while keeping accuracy, and transfers to closed-source models via voting. Development trend: probability monotonicity → statistical indicator → learned classifier for on-the-fly CoT gating.
> 
> ## 2. 4-bit optimizer states for memory-efficient fine-tuning
> **4-bit Optimizers** (Adam/AdamW states) — Trend: pushing state precision from 8-bit → **4-bit** via analysis-driven quantization. Key steps: (a) **smaller block size (B128)** for the first moment to handle heterogeneous outliers; (b) **zero-point-excluded linear quantizer** to fix the zero-point problem of the second moment; (c) **rank-1 normalization** (row+column scales) and optional **factorization** of the second moment (4-bit Factor). Trend is from naive block-wise quantization → outlier-aware, rank-1/factorized schemes, reaching ~lossless fine-tuning of LLaMA-7B/13B/33B with up to ~57.7% memory savings, plus a general compress/decompress framework (Algorithm 1).
> 
> ## 3. Anchor-free part–body association
> **PBADet** (one-stage, anchor-free) — Trend: from two-stage/anchor-based methods (Zhou's heuristic matching, BodyHands association networks, anchor-based BPJDet body-to-part offsets) → a **single part-to-body center offset** in an anchor-free dense detector. It adds a displacement branch (3-layer conv {3×3,3×3,1×1}) alongside classification/localization on multi-scale feature maps, uses task-alignment learning and an association loss, and supports arbitrary numbers of parts with one-to-one part↔body correspondence. On BodyHands/COCOHumanParts it beats BPJDet, HierR-CNN, etc., and generalizes to animal part–body association. Trend: multi-stage heuristic → joint one-stage anchor-free with explicit part-to-body offset and task-alignment supervision.
> 
> ## 4. Spectral stabilization of EI RNNs + self-distillation ignoring noisy features
> Two complementary works show the trend of using *spectral/feature-dynamics analysis to guide architecture and objective design*:
> - **Why Dale's Law Constrained RNNs Learn Poorly** — Trend: showing **spectral properties matter more than sign constraints**. ColEI RNNs fail because their column-mean weight structure yields **multimodal, dispersed singular-value spectra**, whereas standard/DANN RNNs have unimodal quarter-circle (Marchenko–Pastur) spectra. They introduce **normalized SVD entropy (NSE)** as a pre-training diagnostic that anti-correlates with error, showing small/balanced E:I networks with clustered spectra train well (trend: sign constraints → spectrum-driven initialization/architecture design, plus gradient clipping for stability).
> - **How JEPA Avoids Noisy Features** — Trend: explaining self-distillation's noise suppression analytically. On deep linear networks, JEPA self-distillation is implicitly biased to learn **high-influence (high-ρ) features first**, with depth strengthening noise suppression, whereas MAE orders by eigenvalue λ—this is why JEPA ignores noisy/spurious features and aligns with the low-variance perceptual subspace. Trend: from empirical observation → exact gradient-flow/critical-time analysis guiding when/why to trust self-distillation targets.
> 
> ## Supporting implementation details
> The relevant papers do report the specifics you asked for: **CE/MSE-style objectives** (pairwise/regression losses in PBADet's detection heads; ranking+autoregressive losses; quantization/convergence analyses), **feedforward/convolutional prediction heads** (PBADet's three conv branches; Reward-stage feed-forward layers), **implementation diagrams/pseudocode** (PBADet pipeline figure, 4-bit optimizer's Algorithm 1 and quantization pseudocode, TokenSignature's schematic diagram), and **ResNet-50–class backbones** appear across the collection (e.g., NEFTune with QLoRA on LLaMA, Swin-T/ImageNet in the 4-bit optimizer work).
> 
> **Overall trend across the four tracks:** from static/heuristic designs toward (a) dynamic, data-driven decision-making (probability-based CoT gating), (b) precision-reduced, outlier-aware compression (4-bit optimizer states), (c) unified one-stage anchor-free joint representations (single part-to-body offset), and (d) principled spectral/feature-dynamics analysis as the guide for both RNN stability and self-distillation robustness.

</details>
