Gold 1：

> Based on the integration of the provided papers, the development trend of their methods can be summarized as follows:
> 
> Methods for large-scale model training and fine-tuning have evolved along three distinct but complementary dimensions:
> 
> 1. **Architectural Efficiency and Task-Specific Decomposition (PBADet)**:
>    - Transformer-based anchor-free detection architectures (e.g., PBADet) target specialized high-resolution association tasks like part-to-body mapping. The trend here is toward **more compact, scalable representations** (e.g., single-offset encoding instead of multiple offsets) to maintain accuracy while improving efficiency.
>    - Advancement focuses on scalability with flexible architectures that avoid performance degradation when the number of target subcomponents grows.
> 
> 2. **Memory-Efficient Optimization (4-bit Optimizers)**:
>    - Optimizer state compression has progressed from 32-bit and 8-bit down to **4-bit precision**, driven by empirical observation of statistical patterns in optimizer states (complex outlier patterns, zero-point issues).
>    - Trends show **hybrid strategies** combining block-wise quantization with row- and column-aware rank-1 normalization, and optional factorization for second moments to achieve substantial memory savings with minimal accuracy loss.
>    - This moves toward enabling fine-tuning of much larger models within fixed memory budgets, reflecting a convergence of optimization theory with hardware-aware methods.
> 
> 3. **Interpretability and Prompt-Level Fine-Tuning Attribution (TuCo)**:
>    - The introduction of TuCo reflects an interpretability-driven trend, decomposing model responses into **pre-training and fine-tuning components** at a per-prompt granularity.
>    - This enables measurement of how much fine-tuning drives output behavior, and reveals trends such as jailbreaks or low-resource-language prompts attenuating fine-tuning’s impact.
>    - Movement in this area ties into safety, allowing detection of where fine-tuning constraints fail and offering a lever (scaling FTC) to control behaviors or restore capabilities.
> 
> **Cross-cutting Trends:**
> - **Scalability**: All methods target efficiency—whether architectural (simpler offsets in PBADet), memory (low-bit optimizers), or analytical (TuCo without retraining).
> - **Adaptability to Constraints**: Techniques adapt to constraints from hardware (memory limits), data distribution (low-resource language), or safety (jailbreak resistance).
> - **Interpretability and Control**: An increasing emphasis on understanding and controlling internal mechanics (FTC scaling in TuCo, architecture simplification in PBADet) reflects a shift from purely performance-driven to transparency- and controllability-driven designs.
> 
> This convergence suggests future methods will blend **compact architectures**, **extreme memory efficiency**, and **fine-grained behavioral attribution**, enabling safe, controllable, and resource-aware deployment of large Transformer-based systems.

**naive 最终答案**

> Based on the context, here is a compact set of 5–6 papers covering all five requested areas:
> 
> 1. **Part-to-body association** → **PBADet (ICLR 2024)** — one-stage, anchor-free detector that adds a single part-to-body center offset to anchor-free object representation, with separate classification/localization/displacement branches and task-alignment learning. Evaluated on COCO-HumanParts, COCO-WholeBody, CrowdHuman, BodyHands (standard detection benchmarks), and compared against Transformer-based pose detectors (ED-Pose with Swin-L). *Caveat:* its backbone is CNN-based (YOLOv5/v7/v8); the Transformer-style detectors (DETR-family, ED-Pose) appear only as benchmarks, so the "Transformer backbone" criterion is only partially met by this paper in the collection.
> 
> 2. **Memory-lean training** → **4-bit Optimizers (NeurIPS 2023)** — compresses stateful optimizer (Adam/AdamW/SGDM) moments to ~4 bits using smaller block size (B128), rank-1 normalization, and zero-point-excluding linear quantizers for the second moment (optionally factorized). Matches 32-bit AdamW accuracy on RoBERTa-L, Swin-T, GPT-2, Transformer-Base (WMT14), and LLaMA-7B/13B/33B with up to 57.7% memory savings.
> 
> 3. **Self-supervised joint-embedding vs. reconstruction** → **"Why JEPA Avoids Noisy Features" (NeurIPS 2024)** — analyzes JEPA (predictive joint-embedding self-distillation) vs. MAE (pixel reconstruction) in deep linear networks, showing JEPA's implicit bias toward high-influence, low-noise features rather than MSE reconstruction; validated on ImageNet via CCA in cosine-similarity space. A supporting paper, **"On the Similarities of Embeddings in Contrastive Learning"**, analyzes SSL embeddings in cosine-similarity space (CIFAR-10/100, ImageNet-100).
> 
> 4. **Per-prompt interpretability & jailbreak** → **TuCo (ICML 2025)** — decomposes a fine-tuned LLM into pre-training + fine-tuning components and measures per-prompt Tuning Contribution at inference; jailbreak attacks (GCG, conjugate-prompt, many-shot) attenuate TuCo, enabling attack-success prediction with AUC up to ~0.87–0.94 across Llama-2/3, Gemma, Vicuna, etc.
> 
> 5. **Dale-like recurrent nets** → **"Learning Better with Dale's Law: A Spectral Perspective" (NeurIPS 2023)** — compares E/I-partitioned (ColEI) and Dale's-ANN RNNs on adding problem, sequential MNIST, Penn Tree Bank, and object recognition; shows the singular-value spectrum at initialization (multimodal/dispersed for ColEI) matters more than sign constraints, with normalized SVD entropy anti-correlating with test error.
> 
> ---
> 
> **Development trend of the methods:**
> 
> - **Association/detection (1):** From multi-stage, anchor-based, heuristic-matching pipelines (two-stage hand-body association, BPJDet's body-to-part offsets) toward **single-stage, anchor-free, one-to-one "part-to-body" formulations** — a single learned center offset that scales to any number of parts and simplifies post-processing, consistently beating anchor-based and Transformer-DETR counterparts.
> 
> - **Memory-efficient training (2):** Optimizer-state compression moves from 32-bit → 8-bit (block-wise dynamic exponents) → **4-bit**, via finer-grained quantization (smaller blocks, rank-1 normalization, zero-point exclusion) plus factorization of the second moment, achieving lossless accuracy and enabling large-model (LLaMA-7B) training on a single GPU.
> 
> - **Self-supervised learning (3):** From **reconstruction-based (MAE, pixel MSE)** toward **predictive joint-embedding (JEPA) objectives**, with the trend of explaining the empirical preference via **theory in deep linear networks** — predicting in latent space biases toward high-influence/predictive, low-noise features, while cosine-similarity-based analysis formalizes alignment/uniformity of embeddings.
> 
> - **Alignment interpretability (4):** From dataset-level benchmarks and mechanistic analyses toward **per-prompt, inference-time metrics** that exactly decompose fine-tuning contributions, enabling not just measurement but also steering (scaling the fine-tuning component) and quantitative jailbreak detection via AUC.
> 
> - **Biologically-constrained RNNs (5):** From simply enforcing Dale's law via sign constraints (which hurt learning) toward understanding *why* via **spectral analysis** — showing singular-value distributions and normalized SVD entropy at initialization (not sign constraints) predict trainability, guiding better initializations/architectures for E/I networks.
> 
> The common thread across all five: a move from heuristic/black-box methods toward **explicit, decomposable, and theoretically analyzed formulations** (center-offset association, quantized optimizer states, linear-Net implicit-bias analysis, fine-tuning decomposition, spectral diagnostics), validated on standard benchmarks (COCO, CIFAR, ImageNet, MNIST, PTB).

**community 最终答案**

> Here is a compact set of five papers (one per topic) from the collection:
> 
> 1. **PBADet: One-Stage Anchor-Free Part-Body Association** (doc `08b70bc3…`) — one-stage, anchor-free part-to-body association via a single part-to-body center offset on COCO-HumanParts, COCO val, CrowdHuman, BodyHands; YOLOv5/YOLOv7 backbones (the collection has no Transformer-backbone part-body paper; it benchmarks against transformer-based ED-Pose/Swin-L and DETR-style detectors, reporting AP, MR, precision/recall/F1).
> 2. **4-bit Optimizers: Training Large Models with 4-bit Optimizer States** (doc `8d5e1455…`) — quantizes Adam/AdamW first/second moments to 4 bits (smaller B128 blocks, zero-point-excluded linear mapping, rank-1 normalization, optional factorization), matching 32-bit AdamW on ImageNet (Swin-T), GLUE, SQuAD, E2E-NLG, WMT14, Alpaca (LLaMA) with up to 57.7% memory savings.
> 3. **Why JEPA Avoids Noisy Features: Implicit Bias of Deep Linear Self-Distillation** (doc `40fde037…`) — JEPA self-distillation (predictive joint-embedding) vs MAE pixel-reconstruction in deep linear networks; JEPA prioritizes high-influence/low-variance features (critical-time analysis, CCA on ImageNet), i.e., predictive features over pixel MSE. Companion: **On the Similarities of Embeddings in Contrastive Learning** (doc `160e1407…`) — cosine-similarity analysis of positive/negative pairs, mini-batch variance, variance-reduction loss on CIFAR-10/100, ImageNet.
> 4. **TuCo: Measuring the Contribution of Fine-Tuning to Individual Responses of LLMs** (doc `e20e7624…`) — per-prompt interpretability: decomposes a fine-tuned Transformer into pre-training + fine-tuning components; TuCo predicts jailbreak success (AUC ≈ 0.87; >0.8 across models); jailbreaks (GCG, conjugate, many-shot) lower TuCo, more so when successful; tested on Llama2/3, Gemma, Vicuna, Mistral, Zephyr, MMLU, HH-RLHF.
> 5. **Why Dale's Law Constrained Recurrent Neural Networks Learn Poorly** (doc `e63a94c4…`) — RNNs with excitatory/inhibitory partitions (ColEI vs DANN); shows initial singular-value spectrum, not sign constraints, drives learning; uses normalised SVD entropy (NSE) anti-correlated with test error; tasks: adding, sequential MNIST, Penn Tree Bank, object recognition.
> 
> **Development trend of the methods:**
> - **From multi-stage to single-stage:** part-body association moves from two-stage/heuristic/anchor-based pipelines (BodyHands, BPJDet) to a one-stage anchor-free dense formulation with a compact part-to-body offset, evaluated on standard COCO-family benchmarks and compared against heavyweight Transformer (DETR/Swin) detectors.
> - **Efficiency via compression rather than architecture change:** optimizer memory is reduced by quantizing stateful Adam/AdamW buffers to 4 bits with data-adaptive quantizers (small blocks, rank-1 normalization, zero exclusion), preserving full-precision convergence — making large-model training memory-lean without altering the optimizer's behavior.
> - **Theory-driven SSL:** self-supervised learning shifts from purely empirical contrastive/reconstruction objectives to principled analyses — deep-linear implicit bias shows JEPA's predictive joint-embedding objective selects high-influence features over MSE pixel reconstruction, while cosine-similarity analyses characterize optimal embedding geometry; both validated on CIFAR/ImageNet.
> - **From aggregate to per-prompt, interpretable alignment:** safety/alignment analysis moves from benchmark-level evaluation to per-prompt metrics (TuCo) that quantify how much fine-tuning contributes at inference, enabling quantitative prediction of jailbreak success (AUROC), and steering behavior by scaling the fine-tuning component.
> - **Spectral/dynamical understanding of biologically constrained models:** for Dale-law RNNs, analysis shifts from sign constraints to spectral properties — singular-value distributions and SVD entropy at initialization predict trainability, guiding architecture/initialization design.
> - **Common threads:** all works use standard datasets (COCO, ImageNet, CIFAR, MNIST, GLUE, Penn Tree Bank), Transformer or RNN architectures, and standard losses (cross-entropy, MSE) and feature embeddings, converging on the idea that understanding and controlling spectra, statistics, and internal structure — rather than adding complexity — drives progress.

</details>

I’d prefer Transformer/RNN solutions and possibly adapter‑style, end‑to‑end parameter‑efficient fine‑tuning. Gold 1：

> {'answer': 'Across the four papers, a clear development trend emerges in how methods address model efficiency, interpretability, and safety for large-scale systems:\n\n1. **Scalability & Efficiency** – Optimizer compression evolved from 8-bit block-wise quantization (Dettmers et al.) to 4-bit state quantization with nuanced normalization (Rank-1, smaller block sizes) and factorization options, enabling larger trainable models under constrained VRAM without loss in performance. This reflects a trend toward *more aggressive, fine-grained compression* that still maintains convergence stability.\n\n2. **Interpretability & Internal Behavior Control** – TuCo introduces an *exact layerwise decomposition* of LLMs into pre-training and fine-tuning components, quantifying fine-tuning’s per-prompt impact at inference time. FTC scaling shows fine-tuning magnitude directly steers high-level behaviors and benchmark accuracy. This represents a shift from dataset-level evaluation toward *prompt-level, forward-pass-aware interpretability tools*, with actionable steering.\n\n3. **Safety & Robustness Over Time** – PBADet demonstrates anchor-free, one-stage architectures for part-body association, with concise representations that scale more gracefully with part count than prior anchor-based methods. This focus on pairing detection accuracy with adaptability over varied part visibility patterns exemplifies *domain-specific scalability improvements*.\n\n4. **Learning Bias Analysis** – The Dale’s Law spectral study links network trainability to spectral properties rather than purely to sign constraints, showing that spectrum clustering (NSE) is key for scaling EI networks without degrading performance. This shifts the field from architectural constraints toward *spectral property optimization as a design axis*.\n\n**Integrated Trend:** Methods are converging on *parameter-, representation-, and forward-pass–efficient designs* that actively quantify and control latent components (spectral patterns, fine-tuning circuits, optimizer states) to achieve three converging goals: train bigger models under tighter resources, interpret and steer internal behaviors at fine granularity, and sustain robustness across tasks and domains as scale and adversarial pressure increase.'}

**naive 最终答案**

> ## Recommended papers (mapped to your requirements)
> 
> **(a) Hand/face detection + person linkage** → **PBADet: One-Stage Anchor-Free Approach for Part-Body Association**
> One-stage, anchor-free detector that jointly detects parts (hands, face, feet) and links each to its parent body via a single part-to-body center offset. Evaluated on BodyHands, COCO-HumanParts, CrowdHuman; reports AP and hand/feet Precision/Recall/F1 vs. ED-Pose on COCO.
> 
> **(b) Joint-embedding SSL pretraining (no pixel reconstruction)** → **Why JEPA Self-Distillation Avoids Noisy Features (deep linear network analysis)**
> Analyzes JEPA — encoders trained so embeddings of similar inputs are predictive in latent space — contrasted with MAE-style pixel reconstruction. Shows JEPA's implicit bias toward high-influence features and suppression of noise, with depth strengthening the effect (I-JEPA features align faster with perceptual PCA subspace by CCA).
> 
> **(c) Per-prompt SFT contribution + jailbreak suppression via AUROC** → **TuCo: Measuring the Contribution of Fine-Tuning to Individual Responses of LLMs**
> Decomposes any fine-tuned Transformer LLM into pre-training (PTC) and fine-tuning (FTC) components and defines a per-prompt Tuning Contribution (TuCo) from intermediate hidden states (≈2 forward passes). GCG/conjugate/many-shot jailbreaks lower TuCo, more when successful; attack success predicted with AUC up to 0.87 (Llama-13B), >0.8 for most models.
> 
> **(d) Trainable recurrent E/I (excitatory–inhibitory) control loop** → **Learning better with Dale's Law: A Spectral Perspective**
> Extends Dale's ANNs (DANN) to recurrent settings: weights reparameterized into non-negative E→E, E→I, I→E projections that respect E/I separation yet train as well as standard RNNs on adding, sequential MNIST, PTB. Shows spectral properties (unimodal singular values) matter more than sign constraints.
> 
> **(e) Tight-VRAM training with low-bit optimizer states (Adam/SGD)** → **Memory Efficient Optimizers with 4-bit States**
> Compresses Adam/AdamW first/second moments to 4-bit (smaller block size, rank-1 normalization, zero-point-excluding linear quantizer, optional second-moment factorization). Matches 32-bit accuracy with up to ~57.7% memory savings; F1 is reported for SQuAD QA and accuracy for image classification.
> - *Note:* COCO Precision/Recall/F1 come from PBADet; MNIST/CIFAR-100 with SGD/Adam appear in the Hessian-structure paper ("Investigating the Overlooked Hessian Structure"); no single doc runs low-bit optimizers on exactly COCO/CIFAR-100/MNIST.
> 
> **(Adapter-style PEFT for Transformer/RNN)** → **NFTS: Neural Fine-Tuning Search for Few-Shot Learning**
> NAS over per-layer freeze/fine-tune and adapter insertion (TSA residual adapters for ResNet, ETT prefix adapters for ViT), trained end-to-end via a supernet with prototypical loss — the parameter-efficient fine-tuning piece you asked for.
> 
> ## Development trends
> 
> - **Detection/association:** from multi-stage, heuristic or two-stage hand-body association and anchor-based body-to-part offsets (BPJDet) → one-stage anchor-free detection with a single part-to-body offset that scales to more parts with better Precision/Recall/F1.
> - **SSL pretraining:** from pixel-reconstruction (MAE) and contrastive (SimCLR/BYOL) objectives → joint-embedding predictive (JEPA) latent-space prediction, now justified theoretically (deep-linear analysis) as preferring robust, high-influence features over pixel noise.
> - **Fine-tuning attribution:** from aggregate/benchmark-level or mechanistic dataset-level analysis → a per-prompt, inference-time metric (TuCo) using the PTC/FTC decomposition, enabling quantitative detection of jailbreak-induced attenuation via AUC.
> - **Recurrent E/I:** from naive sign-constrained E/I RNNs (ColEI) that train poorly → DANN reparameterization that keeps E/I separation but matches standard RNN training, with the key insight that spectral properties rather than sign constraints drive learnability.
> - **Optimizer memory:** from 32-bit (and 8-bit block-wise) optimizer states → 4-bit states with finer quantization/rank-1 normalization/factorization, achieving lossless convergence at greatly reduced VRAM, compatible with Adam-style optimizers.
> - **Efficient fine-tuning:** from full fine-tuning and hand-placed adapters → automated search over freeze/adapt decisions per layer, applied uniformly to both CNNs and ViTs.

**community 最终答案**

> Here are the papers to read, mapped to each requirement, followed by the development trend.
> 
> **Recommended papers**
> 
> 1. **(a) Hand/face detection + correct person linking** — **PBADet: A One-Stage Anchor-Free Approach for Part-Body Association** (ICLR 2024). Detects face, left/right hands (and feet) and associates them to the correct person via a single part-to-body center offset; beats BPJDet/Hier R-CNN on BodyHands & COCOHumanParts and ED-Pose on hand/feet **Precision/Recall/F1**. (Related works cited inside: "Whose Hands Are These?", ContactHands, YOLO-Pose.)
> 
> 2. **(b) Joint-embedding SSL pretraining (not pixel reconstruction)** — **"Why JEPA Avoids Noisy Features: The Implicit Bias of Deep Linear Self Distillation Networks"** (NeurIPS 2024): explains why JEPA self-distillation beats MAE pixel reconstruction (features learned in latent space, noise suppression). Complement with **LDReg: Local Dimensionality Regularized SSL** (ICLR 2024), which regularizes JEPA/SimCLR/BYOL/MAE encoders against dimensional collapse and improves COCO detection/CIFAR transfer; optionally **HASSOD** for fully self-supervised detection.
> 
> 3. **(c) Per-prompt fine-tuning contribution + jailbreak detection via AUROC** — **TuCo: Measuring the Contribution of Fine-Tuning to Individual Responses of LLMs** (ICML 2025). Exact decomposition of a fine-tuned transformer into pre-training + fine-tuning components gives a per-prompt Tuning Contribution; jailbreaks (GCG, conjugate, many-shot) lower TuCo, with **AUC > 0.78** (GCG) and **> 0.8** (chat vs. webtext).
> 
> 4. **(d) Small recurrent control loop with E/I separation, still trainable** — **"Learning better with Dale's Law: A Spectral Perspective"** (NeurIPS 2023). Shows sign-constrained ColEI RNNs train poorly, while recurrent **DANNs** respect excitatory/inhibitory separation yet train like standard RNNs; spectral properties (normalized SVD entropy) and gradient clipping are the key levers.
> 
> 5. **(e) Low-bit optimizer states under tight VRAM (Adam/SGD)** — **"Memory Efficient Optimizers with 4-bit States"** (NeurIPS 2023). Compresses Adam/AdamW first/second moments to 4-bit (B128 blocks, rank-1 normalization, zero-point-excluding linear quantizer, factorization), matching 32-bit accuracy on RoBERTa-L, Swin-T, GPT-2, LLaMA-7B with ~57.7% memory savings (QA reported as F1). Pair with **LDReg/HASSOD** for COCO and the **"Investigating the Overlooked Hessian Structure"** paper for MNIST/CIFAR-100 SGD/Adam setups.
> 
> 6. **Adapter-style PEFT (your preference)** — **NFTS: Neural Fine-Tuning Search for Few-Shot Learning** (search over per-layer freeze/fine-tune + adapters on pretrained backbones), plus the **"Agreement-on-the-Line for Foundation Models"** paper (LoRA/IA3/BitFit PEFT behavior).
> 
> **Development trend of the methods**
> 
> - **Detection/association:** multi-stage, anchor-based pipelines (Faster R-CNN, Hier R-CNN, BPJDet with body-to-part offsets) → **one-stage anchor-free** detection with a single part-to-body offset (PBADet), improving efficiency, robustness and joint Precision/Recall/F1.
> - **Self-supervised pretraining:** pixel-reconstruction objectives (MAE) → **joint-embedding predictive architectures** (JEPA/self-distillation) that predict in latent space and avoid noisy pixel features; then regularization (LDReg) against dimensional collapse to improve downstream transfer (COCO, CIFAR).
> - **Fine-tuning attribution:** dataset-level benchmarks/mechanistic analysis → **exact per-prompt decomposition** (TuCo), turning fine-tuning contribution into an interpretability metric and a jailbreak detector (AUROC).
> - **Recurrent E/I models:** naive sign-constrained partitioning (ColEI) that learns poorly → **spectral diagnosis + DANN reparameterization**, keeping biological E/I separation while restoring trainability.
> - **Optimizer memory:** 32-bit → 8-bit → **4-bit optimizer states** with finer blocks, rank-1 normalization and zero-point exclusion, preserving full-precision accuracy at a fraction of VRAM.
> 
> Note: no single paper in this collection covers everything; these papers collectively satisfy all five requirements.

### paperscope:trend:204 — 评分与执行路径对照

**问题：** Help me find a small set of papers that, taken together, cover: (1) anchor‑free part‑to‑object association in vision (e.g., hand/face to person) with detection heads trained using common losses like cross‑entropy and MSE and evaluated by F1/Precision/AUROC on datasets such as MNIST/CIFAR‑100/SVHN; (2) analysis of deep networks under neurobiological excitatory/inhibitory constraints using spectral tools (e.g., singular value distributions, normalized entropy) and their impact on SGD/AdamW training; (3) joint‑embedding self‑distillation methods that bias toward high‑influence features (often measured via cosine similarity) rather than pixel‑level reconstruction; (4) sub‑8‑bit (e.g., 4‑bit) optimizer‑state quantization for Transformers/ResNet‑50 with end‑to‑end fine‑tuning (including LoRA-style setups) using AdamW; and (5) rigorous sample‑complexity guarantees for differentially private optimization on nonsmooth, nonconvex objectives, including single‑pass and multi‑pass algorithms. I’m looking for works that collectively address these themes across optimization, representation learning, spectral analysis, privacy, and efficient detection.Please summarize the development trend of their methods.

Gold 1：

> Development trend across the five works
> 
> 2019–2023: Making training feasible at scale and under biological constraints
> - Memory efficiency: Optimizer‑state precision shrank from 8‑bit to 4‑bit (2023). By diagnosing outlier patterns in first/second moments and the zero‑point pitfall for second moments, 4‑bit AdamW with rank‑1 normalization (and an optional factorized v) preserves full‑precision accuracy while cutting optimizer memory and communication. This enabled end‑to‑end fine‑tuning of modern Transformers (e.g., Swin‑T, RoBERTa‑L, GPT‑2) and instruction‑tuning LLaMA, and works with LoRA‑style setups.
> - Neurobiologically constrained deep nets: Instead of treating Dale’s Law sign constraints as the core bottleneck, 2023 work showed trainability is governed primarily by spectral properties. Multimodal, dispersed singular‑value spectra hurt learning; unimodal, clustered spectra (high normalized SVD entropy) predict good outcomes. This reframes design toward spectral initialization/architecture (e.g., recurrent DANNs), improving SGD/AdamW training stability on tasks like sequential MNIST and language modeling.
> 
> 2024: Leaner objectives and heads that bias toward informative structure
> - Representation learning: Analysis of deep linear self‑distillation (JEPA) vs. MAE showed JEPA’s latent‑space MSE objective has a depth‑dependent implicit bias toward high‑influence (predictive) features rather than high‑variance pixel details. This formalizes why non‑contrastive, stop‑grad joint‑embedding methods learn semantic features faster than reconstruction objectives.
> - Efficient vision association: Part‑to‑object association moved from anchor‑based, multi‑stage designs to a one‑stage, anchor‑free head (PBADet). A single 2D part‑to‑body center offset per location replaces K body‑to‑part offsets, shrinking representation length, simplifying decoding, and scaling to many parts without degrading detection. Task‑aligned classification (cross‑entropy branch) plus IoU/DFL localization yield state‑of‑the‑art association accuracy on BodyHands/COCO‑HumanParts with streamlined post‑processing. Reported comparisons also show higher precision/recall/F1 for parts than pose‑keypoint alternatives in head‑to‑head tests.
> 
> 2025: Tighter privacy with fewer samples and passes
> - Private nonsmooth nonconvex optimization: DP guarantees advanced from smooth/convex settings to Lipschitz, nonsmooth, nonconvex ones via Goldstein‑stationarity. Sample complexity improved from prior d‑linear terms to sublinear dimension dependence:
>   • Single‑pass (ε,δ)‑DP: Õ(√d/(αβ^3) + d/(εαβ^2)) using variance‑reduced zero‑order estimators with reduced effective sensitivity (tree mechanism).
>   • Multi‑pass ERM: Õ(d^(3/4)/(ε α^(1/2) β^(3/2))) with Gaussian mechanism and a generalization result that transfers empirical Goldstein‑stationarity to the population, adding only Õ(d/β^2) samples.
>   • First‑order variants maintain the same sample complexity while cutting oracle calls by Õ(d^2) vs. zero‑order. These advances broaden practicality of DP training for nonsmooth, nonconvex objectives.
> 
> Cross‑cutting patterns and scalability
> - From heavy to parsimonious primitives: Methods consistently reduce per‑unit costs—per parameter (4‑bit optimizer states and factorization), per part (single offset for association), and per sample (single‑pass or low‑pass DP), while retaining accuracy.
> - Spectral tools as design targets: Normalized SVD entropy and singular‑value clustering emerged as actionable diagnostics that predict optimization stability under constraints (more decisive than sign constraints themselves).
> - Objectives converging on simple, robust losses: Classification heads rely on cross‑entropy with localization IoU/DFL, JEPA uses latent‑space MSE with stop‑grad, and DP methods pivot from gradient‑norm stationarity to Goldstein‑stationarity suited to nonsmooth landscapes.
> - Hardware‑aware scaling: 4‑bit optimizers reduce GPU memory and communication, enabling larger models on fixed budgets and improving throughput (notably when combined with sharding/FSDP). Anchor‑free heads reduce decoding and representation overhead, scaling to more parts without redesign.
> 
> Implications for the next wave
> - Combine spectral diagnostics (e.g., normalized SVD entropy) with low‑precision optimization to pre‑qualify trainability before fine‑tuning large models.
> - Leverage JEPA’s depth‑amplified bias toward influential features in downstream heads (e.g., part‑association) to prioritize semantically strong cues over pixel details.
> - Bring first‑order, privacy‑aware algorithms with ERM‑to‑population generalization into efficient detection/association pipelines to secure utility under strict data budgets.
> 
> Overall trajectory (2019–2025): Methods evolve toward anchor‑free, end‑to‑end, memory‑ and privacy‑efficient training, guided by spectral analysis and theory that explains—and then exploits—the biases of modern objectives. This yields scalable systems that learn more with fewer bits, fewer passes, and simpler heads, without sacrificing accuracy.

**naive 最终答案**

> Based on the retrieved documents, the five themes map to these papers:
> 
> 1. **PBADet** (ICLR 2024) – one-stage anchor-free part-to-body association; a classification head plus regression heads (bounding-box and part-to-body center offset) trained with standard losses (task-aligned classification/regression), evaluated via AP/precision/recall/F1 on BodyHands, COCOHumanParts, CrowdHuman.
> 2. **"Learning better with Dale's Law: A Spectral Perspective"** (NeurIPS 2023) – analyzes E/I-constrained RNNs via singular-value distributions and normalized SVD entropy, showing spectral properties matter more than sign constraints for SGD training.
> 3. **"How JEPA Avoids Noisy Features"** (NeurIPS 2024) – joint-embedding self-distillation is implicitly biased toward high-influence features, contrasting with MAE-style pixel reconstruction; companion work analyzes embeddings via cosine similarity.
> 4. **"Memory Efficient Optimizers with 4-bit States"** (NeurIPS 2023) – 4-bit AdamW optimizer-state quantization (smaller blocks, rank-1 normalization, zero-point exclusion), applied to Transformers/Swin fine-tuning and instruction tuning with LoRA, matching 32-bit accuracy.
> 5. **"Improved Sample Complexity for Private Nonsmooth Nonconvex Optimization"** (ICML 2025) – (ε,δ)-DP algorithms returning Goldstein-stationary points, with improved single-pass and multi-pass sample-complexity bounds.
> 
> **Development trend of the methods:**
> - **Detection**: multi-stage/anchor-based association → one-stage anchor-free detectors, replacing heuristic matching with a single learned part-to-body offset and task-alignment, using simple classification/regression heads and standard F1/AP evaluation.
> - **Spectral analysis**: moving from sign-constraint explanations of E/I networks to spectral diagnostics (singular-value distributions, normalized SVD entropy) that predict learning; extending to power-law Hessian spectra linking optimization (SGD/AdamW), sharpness, and generalization.
> - **Representation learning**: shift from pixel-level reconstruction (MAE) to joint-embedding/self-distillation objectives that implicitly prioritize high-influence, low-noise features, with cosine-similarity geometry used to understand and improve embeddings.
> - **Efficient optimization**: progressive reduction of optimizer-state precision (16→8→4 bit) via data-driven quantizers (block/rank-1 normalization, zero-point exclusion) to enable memory-efficient AdamW fine-tuning of large Transformers, including LoRA setups.
> - **Privacy**: DP optimization advancing from smooth/convex settings to nonsmooth nonconvex objectives under Goldstein stationarity, with successive improvements in sample complexity from single-pass to multi-pass, sample-efficient ERM algorithms.

**community 最终答案**

> Based on the retrieved documents, here is the small set of papers and the development trend of their methods.
> 
> ## The five papers
> 
> 1. **PBADet (ICLR 2024)** – One-stage, anchor-free part-to-body association. Detection heads: classification branch (cross-entropy-type class loss, TOOD task alignment), bounding-box IoU + DFL losses, and a dedicated part-to-body association head regressing a 2D center offset with an L1 loss; evaluated with AP, Precision/Recall/F1 (vs. ED-Pose), and MR−2 on BodyHands, COCO-HumanParts, CrowdHuman.
> 
> 2. **"Learning better with Dale's Law: A Spectral Perspective" (NeurIPS 2023)** – Analyzes deep recurrent networks under excitatory/inhibitory (Dale's Law) constraints using spectral tools: singular-value distributions, Marchenko–Pastur quarter-circle laws, spectrum-transplant experiments, and normalised SVD entropy (NSE); shows the initial spectrum matters more than sign constraints and impacts SGD training (with gradient clipping) and performance.
> 
> 3. **"How JEPA Avoids Noisy Features" (NeurIPS 2024)** – Joint-embedding self-distillation (JEPA) theory: via deep linear networks, shows self-distillation is implicitly biased toward high-influence (high regression-coefficient, low-variance) features rather than pixel-level reconstruction (MAE), measured by cosine-similarity/CCA alignment with the low-variance PCA subspace.
> 
> 4. **"Memory Efficient Optimizers with 4-bit States" (NeurIPS 2023)** – Pushes optimizer-state quantization below 8-bit to 4-bit for Adam/AdamW via smaller blocks (B128), rank-1 normalization, and zero-point-excluding linear quantization for the second moment; matches 32-bit AdamW on fine-tuning Transformers (RoBERTa, GPT-2, LLaMA-7B/13B/33B, Swin-T) including LoRA-based GPT-2 fine-tuning, with up to 57.7% memory savings.
> 
> 5. **"Improved Sample Complexity for Private Nonsmooth Nonconvex Optimization" (ICML 2025)** – Rigorous (ε,δ)-DP sample-complexity guarantees for nonsmooth nonconvex objectives via Goldstein stationarity: a single-pass algorithm improving prior bounds by Ω(√d), and a multi-pass ERM algorithm with sublinear dimension dependence that generalizes to population loss.
> 
> ## Development trend of their methods
> 
> - **From complex/anchored to simple, unified, scalable designs**: part-body association moves from two-stage/anchor-based pipelines and per-part body-to-part offsets (BPJDet) toward a one-stage anchor-free representation with a single part-to-body center offset; parallel trend in optimization from full-precision 32-bit states toward sub-8-bit (4-bit) compressed states that stay lossless.
> - **From empirical observations to spectral/theoretical explanations**: Dale's-law RNN analysis and Hessian power-law studies shift from "why EI networks train poorly" sign-constraint folklore to formal spectral diagnostics (NSE, singular-value distributions) predicting performance before training; JEPA analysis derives implicit-bias mechanisms (high-influence features) explaining empirical SSL success.
> - **From reconstruction to predictive/spectrally-aligned objectives**: representation learning moves away from pixel reconstruction (MAE) toward joint-embedding latent prediction biased toward semantic/high-influence features, with cosine-similarity/CCA as evaluation; spectral alignment becomes a unifying tool across optimization, representation learning, and neuroscience-inspired analysis.
> - **From heuristic training to rigorous guarantees**: memory-efficient quantization develops from ad-hoc 8-bit schemes to carefully analyzed moment patterns, zero-point handling, and convergence proofs; DP optimization progresses from smooth/convex settings to nonsmooth nonconvex ones, with single-pass → multi-pass algorithms yielding progressively sharper (√d-level) sample-complexity bounds.
> - **Overall**: methods converge on simplifying the pipeline (anchor-free heads, 4-bit states), grounding design choices in spectral/structural analysis (SVD entropy, power-law Hessians, feature influence), and complementing empirical results with formal guarantees (Goldstein stationarity, sample complexity), across optimization, representation learning, privacy, and efficient detection.

**Gold（保持结果文件中的原始内容；部分条目本身为序列化字典字符串）**

Gold 1：

> Across the referenced methods, the development trend shows a clear progression in training efficiency and gradient computation for diffusion models: early guided generation approaches often relied on direct gradient calculation on clean image estimates (e.g., FreeDoM, Greedy) or black-box adjoint sensitivity with generic ODE/SDE solvers (e.g., DiffPure, AdjointDPM). This incurred higher computational overhead and lacked solver optimizations specific to diffusion dynamics. AdjointDEIS advances this by exploiting the unique structure of diffusion ODEs/SDEs to simplify continuous adjoint equations via exponential integrators, yielding closed-form handling of linear terms and custom high-order, multi-step solvers—improving numerical stability and convergence speed with distinct schedules for forward sampling and backward gradient integration. A key scalability improvement is separating gradient estimation step counts (M) from sampling steps (N), reducing memory and compute requirements while maintaining accuracy. Over time, the field has moved from generic, memory-intensive backpropagation to specialized adjoint solvers tailored for diffusion equations, enabling efficient guided generation even under complex conditional information schedules and SDE sampling. This reflects a broader trend: increasing exploitation of domain-specific structure in diffusion dynamics to design bespoke gradient computation algorithms that are both computationally efficient and more stable for targeted generation tasks.

**naive 最终答案**

> Yes—each need maps to works in this collection:
> 
> 1. **Anchor-free part–body association**: **PBADet** (ICLR 2024) is a one-stage, anchor-free detector for hand/face detection and part-to-body association via a single part-to-body center offset; on BodyHands/COCOHumanParts/CrowdHuman it beats BPJDet/HierR-CNN, with higher Precision/F1 vs. ED-Pose.
> 2. **Training efficiency under VRAM**: **4-bit Optimizers** (NeurIPS 2023) compress Adam/AdamW first/second moments to 4-bit (smaller block size, rank-1 normalization, zero-point-excluding linear quantizer, optional second-moment factorization), matching 32-bit accuracy with up to ~57.7% memory savings.
> 3. **Gradient computation for diffusion models**: **AdjointDEIS** (NeurIPS 2024) solves continuous adjoint equations with bespoke exponential-integrator solvers for both ODE and SDE (SDE adjoints simplify to an ODE), enabling training-free guided generation (e.g., face-morphing attacks) with convergence-order guarantees; related **Universal Guidance** evaluates guidance on denoised images to close the domain gap.
> 4. **Representation-learning biases**: **LDReg** regularizes local intrinsic dimensionality (via a Fisher-Rao metric) to prevent local dimensional collapse in similarity-based SSL (SimCLR/BYOL/MAE); **On the Similarities of Embeddings in Contrastive Learning** analyzes positive/negative-pair similarity statistics and adds a variance-reduction loss for small-batch robustness.
> 5. **EI-constrained RNNs / spectral analysis**: **"Why Dale's Law Constrained RNNs Learn Poorly"** shows EI (ColEI) RNNs fail not because of sign constraints but because of pathological initial singular-value spectra; normalized SVD entropy (NSE) predicts training performance, and gradient clipping restores stability—DANN-style architectures keep standard-RNN-like spectra and train well.
> 
> **Development trend of the methods:**
> - **Detection**: multi-stage, heuristic/anchor-based part–body matching → one-stage anchor-free dense prediction with a single part-to-body offset, task-alignment learning, and scalable multi-part support.
> - **Optimization memory**: 32-bit → 8-bit → 4-bit optimizer states, with quantization evolving from coarse block-wise schemes to finer rank-1 normalization, zero-point handling, and hybridization with factorization to stay lossless.
> - **Diffusion gradients**: memory-hungry naive backprop through the sampling process → continuous adjoint methods, from ODE-only black-box solvers to bespoke exponential-integrator solvers covering both ODEs and SDEs with stability and convergence guarantees.
> - **Representation learning**: pixel-wise reconstruction/global decorrelation → similarity-based joint-embedding losses, with attention shifting from global collapse to local dimensionality and embedding-similarity statistics as regularizable biases.
> - **EI/RNNs**: sign-constraint-centric designs (which impaired learning) → spectral-property-aware architectures and diagnostics (singular-value spectrum, NSE) that preserve training stability and enable biologically plausible networks to learn as well as standard RNNs.

**community 最终答案**

> Yes. The collection contains works covering all five areas:
> 
> **1. Anchor-free part–body association (hands/face ↔ person): PBADet** (`08b70bc…`)
> **Trend:** Two-stage heuristic matching (Zhou et al., 2018) → two-stage learned association networks (BodyHands) → one-stage anchor-based joint detectors with per-part center offsets (BPJDet, whose representation grows with #parts and breaks for occluded parts) → **one-stage anchor-free detection with a single part-to-body center offset (PBADet)**. This single offset guarantees one-to-one part↔body correspondence, stays valid even when parts are invisible, and yields higher Precision/Recall/F1 (e.g., all-parts F1 48.52 vs ED-Pose 31.51) in crowded scenes.
> 
> **2. Low-bit Adam-like optimizers under tight VRAM: 4-bit Optimizers** (`8d5e14558f…`)
> **Trend:** Full 32-bit Adam states → 16-bit (DALL-E) → 8-bit block-wise dynamic-exponent quantizers (Dettmers et al.) → **4-bit states** via smaller blocks (B128), rank-1 (row×column) normalization, zero-point-excluding linear quantizers for the second moment, optionally factorized second moment. Achieves lossless fine-tuning (LLaMA-7B on a single 80 GB GPU, ~57.7% memory savings) while keeping Adam-like convergence.
> 
> **3. Gradient computation for diffusion guidance via adjoints: AdjointDEIS** (`4d9ddb7e…`)
> **Trend:** Naïve backprop through the generative process (memory-intensive, SDE noise handling is hard) → continuous adjoint equations (Neural-ODE style, Chen et al.) → **bespoke exponential-integrator solvers for the adjoint of diffusion ODEs/SDEs** with convergence-order guarantees; showing the diffusion-SDE adjoint simplifies to an ODE and supporting time-evolving conditioning. Enables training-free guided generation (e.g., face morphing attacks) with much lower memory. Related parallel trend: training-free guidance on denoised images (Universal Guidance) and amortized posterior sampling (RTB) rather than per-sample optimization.
> 
> **4. Joint-embedding representation learning (similarity in embedding space, not pixel MSE): JEPA analysis + LDReg + contrastive embedding theory** (`40fde037…`, `51526068…`, `160e1407…`)
> **Trend:** Pixel-level reconstruction (MAE) → joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPA) that compare in embedding space; deep-linear analysis shows JEPA prioritizes high-influence features and suppresses noise better than MAE. Parallel work regularizes SSL against dimensional collapse — from global (effective rank) to **local intrinsic dimensionality (LDReg)** — and theoretically characterizes positive/negative-pair embedding similarities (optimal values, mini-batch variance) to explain and fix contrastive-learning biases.
> 
> **5. EI-constrained RNNs for control/time-series with stability: "Learning better with Dale's Law: A Spectral Perspective"** (`e63a94c4…`)
> **Trend:** Simple column-wise E/I partitioning (ColEI) trains poorly and is unstable (needs gradient clipping) → spectral analysis shows the singular-value distribution at initialization, not sign constraints per se, drives the failure (multimodal/dispersed spectra vs standard quarter-circle/Marchenko-Pastur) → recurrent **Dale's ANNs (DANN)** preserve E/I constraints while keeping standard-like spectra, learning as well as unconstrained RNNs; normalized SVD entropy (NSE) is proposed as a pre-training diagnostic. Adjacent work (BSO, `4741ca…`) shows online training with per-layer moments can keep stability under binary/spiking constraints.
> 
> **Overall trend:** methods move from multi-stage/heuristic or memory-hungry pipelines toward **single-stage, training-free/low-bit, and theoretically characterized designs** — one compact offset instead of per-part anchors; 4-bit instead of 32-bit optimizer states; continuous adjoints instead of full backprop; embedding-space similarity with regularization/analysis instead of pixel MSE; and EI-constrained architectures redesigned so their spectra match stable RNNs instead of relying on naive sign constraints.

### paperscope:trend:222 — 评分与执行路径对照

**问题：** Help me find papers that, together, cover: (1) self-supervised learning analyses comparing Mean Squared Error (MSE) vs cross-entropy (CE) objectives (e.g., JEPA/self-distillation) and their implicit bias in deep networks; (2) memory-efficient training with Adam/AdamW using quantized first/second-moment states for fine-tuning; (3) one-stage, anchor-free detection on COCO-style benchmarks for part-body association with metrics like Precision/F1; (4) hierarchical generative pipelines that combine Transformers and Diffusion models with GNN training and prediction for property-guided structure generation; and (5) interpretability of recurrent models via spectral analysis under excitatory/inhibitory constraints. Ideally these works also discuss feature embeddings, End-to-end LoRA fine-tuning, and practical evaluation on datasets beyond MNIST/CIFAR-100.Please summarize the development trend of their methods.

Gold 1：

> {'answer': 'Development trends across the five works align along four clear axes: objectives, architectures, optimization/memory, and evaluation/search, with a consistent shift toward scalable, end-to-end, and interpretable systems.\n\n1) Self-supervised objectives and implicit bias (JEPA vs MAE)\n- Trend: from pixel-space reconstruction (MAE, MSE in data space) toward latent-space prediction (JEPA/self-distillation with stop-gradients).\n- Mechanism: analytical deep-linear results show JEPA’s implicit bias prioritizes high-influence (predictive, low-variance) features; the bias strengthens with depth. MAE’s learning order is dominated by covariance magnitude, while JEPA orders by regression coefficients. This provides an explicit rationale for why JEPA often learns more semantic features than reconstruction.\n- Note: Cross-entropy is not central in these analyses; the comparison covered reconstruction (L2) vs latent prediction, with contrastive methods discussed as context but not the focus.\n- Scalability: insights are depth-dependent (bias grows with deeper encoders), guiding large-scale SSL design toward predictive, noise-avoiding objectives.\n\n2) Memory-efficient fine-tuning at scale (Adam/AdamW with 4-bit states)\n- Bit-precision evolution: 32-bit → 8-bit → 4-bit optimizer states. The 4-bit methods introduce (a) smaller blocks for first moments, (b) zero-point-free quantization for second moments (solves catastrophic update deviations), and (c) rank-1 normalization; optionally combine with factorization of second moment for maximum savings.\n- Practical impact: comparable or better accuracy to full precision across NLU, QA, MT, image classification, and instruction tuning. Reported total memory reduction up to ~58% in full fine-tuning; higher throughput with optimizer offload; stable instruction tuning of LLaMA (7B/13B/33B) on limited GPUs.\n- Interoperability: compatible with modern training stacks (AdamW, FSDP); demonstrated with widely used Transformer backbones and instruction-tuning pipelines. End-to-end LoRA-style workflows are naturally enabled by reduced optimizer footprint (they train with a LoRA codebase for GPT-2 and fine-tune LLaMA family; approach remains compatible with PEFT and full FT).\n\n3) One-stage, anchor-free, scalable detection for part–body association (COCO-style)\n- Architectural trend: two-stage or anchor-based association → one-stage, anchor-free with multi-scale dense heads and simple part-to-body center offsets.\n- Scalability: representation length reduces from 6+K+2K (body-to-part) to 5+K+2 (part-to-body), supporting arbitrary numbers of parts without per-part offset explosion; robust when parts are occluded.\n- Training/inference: task-alignment learning replaces handcrafted centerness; decoding is simplified (one-to-one association via predicted body center); trained with SGD and standard YOLO-style schedules; evaluated on COCOHumanParts, BodyHands, CrowdHuman.\n- Metrics: consistent gains in AP/conditional accuracy/F1-like association measures (e.g., mMR-2, joint AP); demonstrates scalability and generalization to multiple datasets.\n\n4) Hierarchical generative pipelines combining Transformers, diffusion, and GNNs\n- Design shift: from monolithic generators to modular, multi-level pipelines that map language → formulae (LLMs/Transformers) → structures (compact-rep diffusion) → property prediction and selection (GNNs).\n- Multi-objective search: formalized as a joint objective (high-level instruction compliance + low-level properties like low formation energy). Best-first tree search over branching factors (language and structure) yields lower-energy candidates; “best-of-N” sampling steers diffusion toward better candidates.\n- Efficiency/scalability: compact crystal representation (A×4 atoms with continuous atom types) accelerates diffusion sampling and boosts DFT convergence versus earlier sparse/voxel/periodic-table representations. Pretrained GNNs filter outliers and guide selection, preventing heuristic exploitation.\n- Outcome: controllable language-to-structure generation verified across families (perovskites, pyrochlores, spinels) with low DFT energies; demonstrates the emerging pattern of fusing LLM planning, diffusion synthesis, and GNN evaluation.\n\n5) Interpretability and stability in recurrent models under EI constraints (Dale’s Law)\n- Shift in explanation: from attributing poor EI-RNN learning to sign constraints alone to a spectral view—singular value distributions at initialization (unimodality, clustering) predict performance more than sign constraints.\n- Spectral metrics: Normalized SVD Entropy (NSE) rises with better learning; large ColEI networks train well despite large max singular values when the overall spectrum clusters; DANN RNNs match standard RNN spectra and learn as well.\n- Practical guidance: stabilize EI networks via spectral initialization/regularization and appropriate gradient clipping; spectra become more favorable with increased width and more balanced E/I ratios—key for scalable recurrent modeling.\n\nCross-cutting trends\n- Scalability by design: anchor-free formulations, compact diffusion representations, 4-bit optimizers, and spectral-aware EI initializations all explicitly target scaling—their benefits grow with more parts, atoms, parameters, or neurons.\n- From hand-engineered stages to end-to-end systems: unified, task-aligned heads (detection), end-to-end memory-efficient fine-tuning (optimizers), language-to-structure pipelines (LLM→Diffusion→GNN) represent a broader move to integrated, trainable stacks.\n- Stronger selection and search: best-of-N, heuristic-guided tree search, and property predictors (GNNs) systematically steer generation/learning toward practically valuable solutions, supplanting unguided sampling or rigid heuristics.\n- Broader evaluations: beyond MNIST/CIFAR baselines, results span COCO-style detection, Penn Treebank, ImageNet, GLUE/SQuAD/WMT, LLaMA instruction tuning, and DFT-verified materials—evidence of the field’s migration to large, diverse, application-grounded benchmarks.\n\nOverall trajectory: Methods increasingly optimize for practical controllability and scale—(i) SSL objectives tuned for feature utility (JEPA), (ii) optimizers compressed to 4-bit with principled quantization for full fine-tuning, (iii) anchor-free one-stage detectors that scale with parts, (iv) hierarchical LLM+Diffusion+GNN stacks for property-guided structure generation, and (v) EI-RNNs designed with spectral criteria for stability and interpretability. These shifts emphasize modularity, spectrum- or objective-aware design, and search/selection mechanisms, enabling robust performance across domains and dataset sizes.'}

**naive 最终答案**

> Here are the papers that together cover the five requested topics, plus a summary of the methodological trend.
> 
> ## Paper matches
> 
> **(1) SSL objectives (MSE vs CE) & implicit bias in deep networks**
> - **"Why JEPA Self-Distillation Avoids Noisy Features: A Deep Linear Network Analysis"** (NeurIPS 2024). Solves training dynamics of JEPA vs MAE objectives (both MSE-type regression, in latent vs input space) in deep linear networks; proves JEPA is biased toward high-influence (large regression coefficient) features while MAE prioritizes high-variance/noisy features, with the bias emerging only for deep encoders. Validated on ImageNet-1K with I-JEPA vs MAE via CCA.
> - Supporting: **LDReg** (ICLR 2024) regularizes local intrinsic dimensionality of SSL embeddings; **"On the Similarities of Embeddings in Contrastive Learning"** analyzes InfoNCE (CE-type) loss and embedding geometry (CIFAR-10/100, ImageNet).
> 
> **(2) Memory-efficient Adam/AdamW with quantized moments**
> - **"4-bit Optimizers: Training Large Models with 4-bit Optimizer States"** (NeurIPS 2023). Quantizes first/second moments of Adam/AdamW (B128/dynamic-exponent for m, rank-1/linear zero-excluded quantizer for v, optional factorization). Fine-tunes RoBERTa-L (GLUE, SQuAD), GPT-2, Swin-T (ImageNet-1k), and LLaMA-7B/13B/33B on Alpaca with up to 57.7% memory savings and ~4× larger models; explicitly frames delta tuning/LoRA-style low-rank adaptation as the alternative route.
> 
> **(3) One-stage anchor-free detection, part-body association, Precision/F1**
> - **"PBADet: A One-Stage Anchor-Free Approach for Part-Body Association"** (ICLR 2024). Extends anchor-free YOLO-style detectors with a single part-to-body center offset on multi-scale features (localization/classification/displacement branches, task-alignment learning). Evaluated on BodyHands, COCO-WholeBody, COCO-HumanParts, CrowdHuman (AP, MR-2, conditional accuracy, joint AP); vs ED-Pose it reports substantially higher precision, recall, and F1 for hands/feet, and generalizes to quadruped datasets (AnimalPose, AP-10K).
> 
> **(4) Hierarchical Transformer + Diffusion + GNN generative pipelines**
> - **"Generative Hierarchical Materials Search (GenMS)"** (Google DeepMind). End-to-end language-to-structure generation: LLM proposes chemical formulae → diffusion model generates crystal structures → GNN predicts formation energy; a forward tree search performs property-guided structure generation. Outperforms direct-LLM baselines on perovskites/pyrochlores/spinels (validity, instruction following, low energy, DFT-verified).
> - Related: **GeoBFN** (ICLR 2024) uses equivariant GNNs inside a Bayesian-flow generative model for 3D molecules with property-conditioned generation (QM9, GEOM-DRUG).
> 
> **(5) Spectral interpretability of recurrent models under E/I constraints**
> - **"Learning better with Dale's Law: A Spectral Perspective"** (NeurIPS 2023). Analyzes why excitatory/inhibitory (Dale's law) RNNs learn poorly: the initial singular-value spectrum (multimodal/dispersed for ColEI vs unimodal for DANN/standard RNNs) matters more than sign constraints; introduces normalized SVD entropy as a predictive, interpretable spectral diagnostic. Benchmarks: sequential MNIST, adding problem, Penn Tree Bank, object recognition.
> 
> **Extra requested aspects:** feature embeddings — JEPA paper, LDReg, and the contrastive-embeddings paper; LoRA fine-tuning — cited/used in the 4-bit optimizer paper (delta tuning) and analyzed in the Hessian-spectrum paper ("Investigating the Overlooked Hessian Structure," LoRA adapters on TinyLlama) and Themis (LoRA fine-tuned Vicuna-7B); evaluation beyond MNIST/CIFAR-100 — ImageNet-1K, COCO-family, GLUE/SQuAD, LLaMA/MMLU, Penn Tree Bank, QM9/GEOM-DRUG, Materials Project. Note: no paper in the collection is specifically about "End-to-end LoRA" as a method; LoRA appears as a related parameter-efficient technique.
> 
> ## Development trend
> 
> 1. **From empirical SSL to theory of objectives**: work moves from observing that JEPA works, to exactly characterizing the implicit bias of latent-space (MSE) vs reconstruction objectives in deep linear nets, then to regularizing representation geometry (local dimensionality) — i.e., theory now guides SSL design.
> 2. **From 32-bit → 8-bit → 4-bit optimizer states**: memory efficiency is pushed by quantizing Adam/AdamW moments with outlier-aware quantization (smaller blocks, rank-1 normalization, zero-point exclusion), converging losslessly while enabling fine-tuning of ever-larger models; combined with parameter-efficient (LoRA/delta-tuning) strategies.
> 3. **From multi-stage/anchor-based to one-stage anchor-free end-to-end detection**: part-body association is unified into a single dense predictor with a compact part-to-body offset, simplifying representation and post-processing while improving AP/F1/precision-recall on COCO-style benchmarks.
> 4. **From single generators to hierarchical, search-guided multi-model pipelines**: generation is decomposed (LLM → diffusion → GNN scorer) and wrapped in a forward tree search, so high-level instructions are verified at the low-level structure scale and property prediction guides sampling.
> 5. **From sign-constrained to spectrally-aware recurrent modeling**: interpretability shifts from parameter constraints to the initialization spectrum (SVD entropy as a pre-training performance diagnostic), enabling EI networks that learn as well as unconstrained RNNs.
> 
> Overall, the trend is: theory-driven understanding of learning dynamics and objectives; aggressive memory/parameter-efficiency for fine-tuning; unified single-stage end-to-end perception; hierarchical composition of heterogeneous generative models with learned scoring/guidance; and spectral/biological interpretability — all validated on large, real-world benchmarks rather than toy datasets.

**community 最终答案**

> Here are the papers covering the five areas:
> 
> 1. **MSE vs CE / JEPA vs MAE implicit bias (SSL)**: *Why JEPA Self-Distillation Avoids Noisy Features: A Deep Linear Network Analysis* (NeurIPS 2024) — solves deep linear training dynamics for JEPA (latent-space prediction, self-distillation, MSE-type regression) vs MAE (reconstruction); shows JEPA biases toward high-influence ("ρ") features while MAE tracks high-variance features, with depth strengthening the effect; validated on ImageNet-1K. Companion: *LDReg* (ICLR 2024) — counters local dimensional collapse via Fisher-Rao local intrinsic dimensionality; improves SSL representation quality on ImageNet and transfers to COCO detection/segmentation.
> 
> 2. **Memory-efficient Adam/AdamW with quantized moment states**: *Memory Efficient Optimizers with 4-bit States* (NeurIPS 2023) — quantizes first/second moments of Adam/AdamW to 4-bit (B128 block + rank-1 normalization, zero-point-excluded linear mapping for second moment, optional factorization); matches 32-bit AdamW on GLUE, SQuAD, ImageNet, WMT14, and LLaMA-7B/13B/33B Alpaca fine-tuning with up to 57.7% memory savings.
> 
> 3. **One-stage anchor-free part-body detection**: *PBADet* (ICLR 2024) — extends anchor-free detectors (YOLOv5/7) with a single part-to-body center offset; evaluated on COCOHumanParts, BodyHands, CrowdHuman, AnimalPose; reports AP/MR-2 plus Precision/Recall/F1 (beats ED-Pose on hands/feet), with task-alignment learning and multi-scale offsets.
> 
> 4. **Hierarchical Transformer + Diffusion + GNN generation**: *GenMS: Generative Hierarchical Materials Search* (ICLR 2024) — LLM generates intermediate chemical formulae, a diffusion model generates crystal structures, and a GNN predicts properties (formation energy); inference uses forward tree search for property-guided generation, verified by DFT; outperforms direct LLM prompting on perovskites/pyrochlores/spinels.
> 
> 5. **Spectral interpretability of E/I-constrained RNNs**: *Why Dale's Law Constrained Recurrent Neural Networks Learn Poorly* (NeurIPS 2023) — analyzes singular-value spectra of excitatory/inhibitory RNNs (ColEI vs DANN vs standard); shows initial spectra (not sign constraints) drive learning, introduces normalized SVD entropy as a pre-training predictor; evaluated on sequential MNIST, Penn Tree Bank, and naturalistic object recognition.
> 
> **Related supporting works**: *NEFTune* (ICLR 2024) covers feature embeddings (noisy embeddings improve instruction fine-tuning, works with QLoRA on LLaMA-2); *Investigating the Overlooked Hessian Structure* (ICML 2025) studies LoRA vs full fine-tuning (LoRA doesn't induce power-law Hessian structure), on CNNs and LLMs beyond MNIST/CIFAR-100.
> 
> **Development trend of these methods:**
> - **From heuristic to theory-backed SSL**: analysis of JEPA/MAE moved from empirical observation to exact solvable dynamics (deep linear nets) revealing objective-dependent implicit biases (influential vs high-variance features), with regularization (LDReg) targeting collapse at local level, all validated on ImageNet/COCO rather than toy datasets.
> - **From 32-bit/8-bit to 4-bit optimizer states**: optimizer compression pushes precision down (8→4-bit) while keeping lossless convergence, and is combined with factorization and PEFT (LoRA/QLoRA) to enable single-GPU fine-tuning of large LLMs; concurrent analyses (Hessian power laws) probe how fine-tuning methods (full vs LoRA) shape the loss landscape.
> - **From multi-stage/anchor-based to one-stage anchor-free end-to-end detection**: part-body association moved from two-stage heuristic matching and anchor-based body-to-part offsets to a single scalable part-to-body offset with task alignment, reported with association-aware metrics (conditional accuracy, joint AP, Precision/F1) on COCO-style benchmarks, and generalized across species (quadrupeds).
> - **From single-model generation to hierarchical multi-modal pipelines**: generation evolved from direct LLM prompting or standalone diffusion into composed LLM→diffusion→GNN systems with explicit search (forward tree search) and physics-based (DFT) validation for property-guided structure generation.
> - **From performance-only to mechanistic/spectral interpretability**: recurrent model analysis shifted from "does E/I constraint hurt?" to spectral diagnosis (multimodal vs unimodal singular-value spectra, NSE as a pre-training predictor), linking initialization spectra to trainability, and extending interpretability to transformers (in-context circuits, Hessian spectra).
> - **Overall**: methods increasingly emphasize theoretical grounding, memory/parameter efficiency, end-to-end simplification, hierarchical composition with external verification, and mechanistic interpretability, with evaluation scaling to real-world benchmarks (ImageNet, COCO, GLUE/SQuAD, WMT, LLaMA, crystal databases) instead of MNIST/CIFAR-100.

Gold 1：

> Development trends across the five papers align with a broader shift toward scalable, resource‑efficient, and controllable end‑to‑end systems, with clear time progression from 2023→2024 and consistent emphasis on interpretability and multi‑objective control.
> 
> a) Self‑supervised pretraining that avoids noisy features (JEPA vs MAE; 2024)
> - Trend: From reconstruction‑based MAE to prediction‑in‑latent (JEPA) for robustness to noise. In deep linear analysis, JEPA’s stop‑grad predictive objective (MSE) prioritizes high‑influence, low‑variance features, whereas MAE tends to emphasize high‑variance (potentially noisy) components. This depth‑dependent implicit bias steers large encoders away from unpredictable pixel‑level details and toward semantic factors, supporting scalable, feature‑stable pretraining before fine‑tuning.
> - Practical implication: For resource‑constrained stacks, prefer JEPA‑style losses (MSE in latent space with stop‑grad) over MAE or pure CE in pretraining to suppress noisy features; deepen the encoder to strengthen JEPA’s favorable bias.
> 
> b) One‑stage anchor‑free part–body detection on COCO‑like data (PBADet; ICLR 2024)
> - Trend: From multi‑stage/anchor‑based hand–body association to a one‑stage anchor‑free head with a single part‑to‑body center offset. This compresses representation (5+K+2 vs 6+K+2K) and scales to many parts without proliferating offsets, improving efficiency and robustness.
> - Performance evolution: On COCO‑HumanParts and BodyHands, PBADet delivers higher Precision/Recall/F1 and lower mMR across heads/hands/feet than prior art, and outperforms multi‑person pose baselines on detection/association. Task‑aligned learning (TOOD) and multi‑scale heads stabilize training.
> - Practical implication: Use anchor‑free heads with a single 2D part‑to‑body offset, multi‑scale features, and task‑alignment to sustain precision/F1 as part taxonomies grow (e.g., for human–robot interface cues on COCO‑like datasets).
> 
> c) Language→structure crystal generation with Transformers, Diffusion, and GNNs (GenMS; NeurIPS 2024)
> - Trend: Emergence of hierarchical, multimodal generation under explicit multi‑objective control: LLM (formula/space‑group via RAG and long context) → diffusion (compact, efficient crystal representation) → GNN property prediction, all combined via forward tree search with high/low‑level heuristics (e.g., instruction compliance, formation energy).
> - Scalability/controllability: Branching factors (language H, structure L) explicitly trade compute for lower DFT‑validated formation energy (best‑of‑N sampling), while retrieval and long‑context de‑duplication raise uniqueness and match rates. Compact A×4 atom/lattice representation accelerates diffusion and improves DFT convergence over prior sparse encodings.
> - Practical implication: For low‑energy proposals, use RAG‑conditioned LLMs to narrow composition space, diffusion with compact crystal tensors for structure sampling, and a pretrained GNN to select low‑energy candidates; raise H/L when compute allows.
> 
> d) Memory‑efficient optimizers with tiny states (NeurIPS 2023)
> - Trend: State precision dropping from 8‑bit to 4‑bit with accuracy preserved—driven by finer‑grained quantization (smaller blocks), rank‑1 normalization (row+column scales), and removal of zero‑point for second moment (linear mapping). Factorizing v further reduces memory. This shifts the bottleneck for finetuning on constrained hardware (including optimizer offloading) and enables larger models.
> - Cross‑task stability: 4‑bit AdamW matches 32‑bit on NLU, QA, MT, Swin‑T CLS, and GPT‑2 NLG; improves throughput and cuts memory by up to ~58% vs 32‑bit; combines well with offloading.
> - Tips (applies to LoRA finetuning, too):
>   • First moment: B128 + dynamic exponent; Second moment: rank‑1 normalization + linear mapping (exclude zero) to avoid instability.
>   • Factorize second moment where tensor dim>1; keep small tensors (≤4096) in FP32.
>   • Stable embeddings not required once zero‑point is removed; stochastic rounding not necessary.
> 
> e) EI‑constrained RNNs and spectral diagnostics for interpretability (NeurIPS 2023)
> - Trend: From naive column‑signed EI (ColEI) with poor learning to architectures and initializations controlled by spectral properties (DANN recurrent variants). Core finding: singular value spectra—not merely sign constraints—govern trainability. Normalized SVD entropy (NSE) of recurrent weights becomes a reliable predictor of performance.
> - Scaling/robustness patterns: Larger networks and balanced E/I ratios increase spectral clustering (higher NSE) and mitigate exploding/vanishing dynamics; small networks with few I units degrade. Gradient clipping helps ColEI but spectrum‑aware design (or DANN) is more robust.
> - Practical implication: For EI‑compliant RNNs with interpretable dynamics, target unimodal, clustered singular spectra at initialization (maximize NSE), balance E/I ratios, and prefer DANN‑style parameterizations when possible.
> 
> Integrated trajectory and scalability (2023→2024)
> - Efficiency front: Optimizers move from 8‑bit→4‑bit (and factorized) to unlock larger models and faster updates; detection moves to anchor‑free single‑stage heads with constant‑size offsets; spectral metrics guide stable EI RNNs as model sizes grow.
> - Self‑supervision front: Pretraining transitions from pixel reconstruction (MAE) to predictive latent alignment (JEPA) to avoid noisy features, with depth amplifying the beneficial bias.
> - Multimodal control front: Materials discovery embraces hierarchical LLM→Diffusion→GNN pipelines with explicit search to satisfy language objectives (composition, family) and physics (low energy), using compact representations and best‑of‑N selection.
> 
> How the papers jointly address the query
> - (a) Self‑supervised pretraining: JEPA’s latent MSE with stop‑grad (vs MAE) prioritizes influential, less‑noisy features before fine‑tuning.
> - (b) Detector for hands/faces/body on COCO: PBADet’s one‑stage anchor‑free head with single part‑to‑body center offsets improves Precision/F1 and scales to multiple parts.
> - (c) Language→structure crystals: GenMS unifies Transformers (LLM), Diffusion, and GNN property prediction, with tree search for low‑energy, instruction‑compliant candidates.
> - (d) Low‑state optimizers: 4‑bit Adam/AdamW with rank‑1 normalization and zero‑point‑free v; optional factorization; proven across Transformers/ResNets; compatible with offloading.
> - (e) EI‑constrained RNNs + interpretability: Spectral diagnostics (NSE) and spectra‑aware designs (DANN) yield stable, interpretable EI RNNs; provide concrete initialization and ratio guidance.
> - End‑to‑end LoRA fine‑tuning tips: Combine LoRA with 4‑bit optimizers (keep small tensors in FP32, use rank‑1+linear v quantization, B128 first‑moment blocks); offload optimizer states if needed to fit memory budgets while preserving accuracy.
> 
> Representative datasets/metrics referenced in the works
> - COCO‑HumanParts, COCO‑WholeBody, BodyHands for detection; Precision/Recall/F1, AP, mMR.
> - MNIST/Sequential MNIST, Penn Treebank, naturalistic classification for EI RNN analysis; NSE as a spectral diagnostic.
> - DFT‑validated formation energies; GNN‑predicted energies for GenMS.
> - Standard NLP/CV tasks (RoBERTa‑L on GLUE/SQuAD, Swin‑T on ImageNet, GPT‑2 on E2E‑NLG) to validate 4‑bit optimizers.
> 
> Overall: The direction is toward unified, resource‑aware, end‑to‑end pipelines that (i) learn robust features with self‑supervision in latent space, (ii) compress optimizer state without accuracy loss, (iii) exploit anchor‑free dense heads for scalable association tasks on COCO‑like data, (iv) compose LLMs, diffusion, and GNNs under search for controllable scientific generation, and (v) use spectral tools to make biologically constrained RNNs trainable and interpretable at scale.

> 
> **(a) Noisy-feature-avoiding self-supervised pretraining (latent prediction vs reconstruction)**
> - **"How JEPA Avoids Noisy Features: The Implicit Bias of Deep Linear Self Distillation Networks"** — JEPA-style latent-space (MSE-like) objectives are biased toward high-influence, low-noise features, while MAE-style reconstruction (CE/pixel) objectives prioritize high-variance features even when noisy; depth strengthens JEPA's noise suppression. (Related: **LDReg** counters dimensional collapse to improve SSL representation quality.)
> 
> **(b) One-stage anchor-free hand/face–body association on COCO-like data**
> - **PBADet: A One-Stage Anchor-Free Approach for Part-Body Association** — a single part-to-body center offset on multi-scale anchor-free heads; on COCO(-HumanParts)/BodyHands/CrowdHuman it beats BPJDet, HierR-CNN and the ED-Pose estimator with much higher Precision/Recall/F1 (e.g., all-parts F1 48.5 vs 31.5).
> 
> **(c) Language-to-structure crystal generator (LLM + Diffusion + GNN)**
> - **GenMS: Generative Hierarchical Materials Search** — LLM proposes formulae, a diffusion model generates compact crystal representations, and a GNN ranks by predicted formation energy under forward tree search; verified via DFT to yield low-energy perovskites/pyrochlores/spinels.
> 
> **(d) Adam/AdamW with tiny optimizer states**
> - **Memory Efficient Optimizers with 4-bit States** — 4-bit Adam/AdamW (small block size + rank-1/zero-point-excluding linear quantization of the second moment, optional factorization); matches 32-bit accuracy while cutting memory up to ~57.7% (LLaMA-7B on one 80GB GPU).
> 
> **(e) EI-constrained RNN design with spectral diagnostics**
> - **"Learning better with Dale's Law: A Spectral Perspective"** — shows EI-RNN performance depends less on sign constraints than on the initial singular-value spectrum; normalized SVD entropy (NSE) is a diagnostic that predicts learnability, guiding EI-RNN/spectral-radius design.
> 
> **(LoRA fine-tuning tips)**
> - **NEFTune** — add noise to embeddings during instruction tuning (alpha/√(Ld), uniform, α≈10); large gains and works with QLoRA.
> - **Investigating the Overlooked Hessian Structure** — LoRA fine-tuning doesn't restructure the Hessian like full fine-tuning; use the Hessian power-law/KS distance or trace as generalization indicators; monitor d_ks and Tr(H) during LoRA adaptation.
> - (Supporting) **PCP** gives concrete fine-tuning hyperparameters (AdamW, lr 1e-5–5e-5, warmup-linear, weight decay 0.01) and shows continued pretraining can hurt without prompt-based objectives; **GOT-D** gives pre-fine-tuning data selection for end-to-end adaptation.
> 
> **Development trend of the methods**
> 1. **Pretraining** moved from pixel/reconstruction-based objectives toward latent, self-distillation (JEPA) objectives, with theory explaining why latent prediction suppresses noisy features and with regularization (LDReg) added against collapse — the goal being semantic, transferable features rather than variance-fit features.
> 2. **Detection** evolved from two-stage/heuristic and anchor-based association to fully one-stage, anchor-free formulations with a single learned part-to-body offset, trading representational complexity for end-to-end simplicity, scalability, and higher precision/F1.
> 3. **Generative materials design** moved from brute-force diffusion sampling or direct LLM output to hierarchical factorized generation (LLM → diffusion → GNN scoring) plus search, decomposing a hard cross-modal problem into solvable subproblems for controllable, low-energy crystal proposals.
> 4. **Optimization** trended toward aggressively compressed optimizer states (32-bit → 8-bit → 4-bit, plus factorization), achieving lossless convergence at tiny memory footprints.
> 5. **Efficient fine-tuning / adaptation** trended toward parameter- and memory-efficient end-to-end pipelines: LoRA/QLoRA combined with noisy-embedding augmentation (NEFTune), data-selection pre-fine-tuning, and spectral (Hessian) diagnostics to guide whether LoRA or full fine-tuning generalizes best — a unifying theme of making large-model pipelines resource-efficient while maintaining interpretability and generalization.

> Based on the retrieved documents, here are the papers that address each need:
> 
> **(a) Self-supervised pretraining avoiding noisy features (MSE vs CE):**
> - **"Why JEPA Self-Distillation Avoids Noisy Features"** — shows JEPA (latent-space predictive/regression objective, MSE-style) is biased toward high-influence features and suppresses noise, whereas MAE (reconstruction in data space) ordering depends mainly on eigenvalue; deep linear analysis gives critical times.
> - Complements: **LDReg** (counters local dimensional collapse of SSL representations) and **Prompt-Based Continued Pre-training (PCP)** (continued pretraining on task text/templates before fine-tuning improves downstream FT).
