> - **PBADet** — one-stage, anchor-free part-body association using a single part-to-body center offset; outperforms BPJDet/HierR-CNN on BodyHands and COCOHumanParts, gives leading body MR-2 on CrowdHuman face-body, and substantially higher precision/recall/F1 than ED-Pose for hands/feet.
> 
> **(c) Language-to-structure generator (Transformer + Diffusion + GNN, low-energy crystals):**
> - **GenMS** — LLM proposes chemical formulae → diffusion model (compact A×4 representation) generates structures → GNN predicts formation energy; forward tree search picks low-energy candidates; DFT-verified low-energy crystals (perovskites, pyrochlores, spinels).
> 
> **(d) Adam/AdamW variants with tiny optimizer states:**
> - **4-bit Optimizers** — quantizes Adam/AdamW first/second moments to 4-bit (smaller block size B128, rank-1 normalization, zero-point-exclusion linear quantizer, factorization); matches 32-bit accuracy with up to 57.7% memory savings; enables LLaMA-7B on one 80GB GPU.
> 
> **(e) EI-constrained RNN design with spectral diagnostics:**
> - **"Learning better with Dale's Law: A Spectral Perspective"** — EI (Dale's law) RNNs fail not because of sign constraints but due to multimodal/dispersed singular-value spectra at initialization; normalised SVD entropy (NSE) predicts learning performance before training and guides architecture/EI-ratio design; DANN-style reparameterization trains as well as standard RNNs.
> 
> **Tips for End-to-end LoRA fine-tuning:**
> - **"Investigating the Overlooked Hessian Structure"** — LoRA improves task performance but does NOT induce the power-law Hessian structure that full fine-tuning does; for LoRA adapters the Hessian trace Tr(H) (which consistently decreases) is a more reliable generalization indicator than sharpness, and KS-distance/power-law goodness predicts LLM generalization.
> - **NEFTune** — adding uniform noise scaled by α/√(Ld) to embeddings during instruction fine-tuning dramatically improves quality (works with QLoRA), reduces overfitting, with α≈10 and longer sequences optimal.
> - **GOT-D** — optimal-transport selection of unlabeled data for a pre-fine-tuning stage before targeted fine-tuning (two-stage fine-tuning) improves F1/GLUE under constrained budgets.
> - **Agreement-on-the-Line** — for PEFT methods (LoRA, IA3, BitFit), diversity sources such as random LoRA initialization achieve linear agreement with full fine-tuning, useful for monitoring OOD reliability.
> 
> **Development trend of the methods:**
> - **Self-supervised pretraining**: from reconstructing inputs in data space (MAE, cross-entropy-type) toward predictive latent-space objectives (JEPA, MSE-type), with theory explaining the implicit bias that suppresses noisy features, plus regularization against dimensional collapse (LDReg) and prompt-based continued pretraining before fine-tuning.
> - **Detection**: from multi-stage, anchor-based part-body pipelines (BodyHands, BPJDet body-to-part offsets) toward a streamlined one-stage anchor-free framework with a single part-to-body offset (PBADet), improving scalability, efficiency, and association precision.
> - **Materials generation**: from direct LLM prompting of CIF/xyz files (near-0% success) toward a hierarchical LLM→diffusion→GNN pipeline with search/selection (GenMS), mirroring cascaded/hierarchical text-to-image diffusion.
> - **Optimizers**: from 32-bit states to 8-bit to 4-bit Adam/AdamW with increasingly careful quantization (block size, rank-1 normalization, zero-point exclusion, factorization) achieving lossless accuracy at a fraction of memory.
> - **EI RNNs**: from ignoring biological constraints toward EI/Dale's-law networks, with the key insight shifting from sign constraints to initialization spectra, using NSE as a pre-training diagnostic for architecture design.
> - **Fine-tuning**: from full-parameter fine-tuning toward parameter-efficient adapters (LoRA/QLoRA), with growing understanding that LoRA behaves differently from full fine-tuning (no power-law Hessian emergence), and recipes such as noisy embeddings, pre-fine-tuning data selection, and agreement-based monitoring to improve robustness.

**Gold（保持结果文件中的原始内容；部分条目本身为序列化字典字符串）**

Gold 1：

> Development trends across the five works converge on scaling, robustness, and efficiency, with clear shifts in training paradigms, architectures, and evaluation:
> 
> 1) One‑stage, anchor‑free part–body association (ICLR 2024):
> - Trend: From multi‑stage, anchor‑based pipelines to a single‑stage, dense, anchor‑free detector that encodes a single 2D part‑to‑body offset. This compresses representation length (from 6+K+2K to 5+K+2), simplifies decoding, and scales to arbitrary part sets.
> - Scalability and generalization: Multi‑scale heads and task‑alignment learning improve robustness; training with SGD; evaluated on COCOHumanParts/COCO‑WholeBody/CrowdHuman with AP/MR−2 and association mMR−2. Precision/Recall/F1 appear in the ED‑Pose comparison, indicating broader utility in quality‑of‑association measurement.
> - Architecture/benchmarks: Anchor‑free heads on YOLOv7/YOLOv5; tested on COCO‑style datasets, showing stronger cross‑dataset transfer than anchor‑based BPJDet.
> 
> 2) Implicit bias in label‑free representation learning (NeurIPS 2024):
> - Trend: Shift from masked reconstruction (MAE) toward JEPA/self‑distillation in latent space. In deep linear encoders, JEPA exhibits a depth‑dependent bias to learn high‑influence features (large regression coefficient ρ) rather than merely high‑variance features emphasized by MAE.
> - Loss and feature behavior: Both objectives use MSE, but differ in learning dynamics; JEPA’s bias strengthens with depth. The analysis uses cosine‑like similarity constructs in generative settings and highlights when JEPA prioritizes predictive, less‑noisy features.
> - Practical implication: Explains why latent prediction often reaches semantic features faster than pixel‑space reconstruction, informing self‑supervised learning design.
> 
> 3) Spectral analyses of EI recurrent deep networks (NeurIPS 2023):
> - Trend: The main limiter of EI RNN learning shifts from sign constraints to spectral properties. Column EI networks show multimodal, dispersed singular‑value spectra that harm stability; recurrent DANNs (EI‑compliant) recover clustered, unimodal spectra similar to standard RNNs.
> - Stability metric: Normalized SVD entropy (NSE) emerges as a predictor of learning and stability across tasks (adding problem, sequential MNIST, Penn Tree Bank), tying performance to singular‑value clustering rather than just maximal singular values.
> - Design guidance: Larger, more balanced E/I splits improve spectra and learning; spectra transplantation experiments show spectrum matters more than sign constraints.
> 
> 4) Memory‑efficient training with 4‑bit optimizer states (NeurIPS 2023):
> - Trend: From 8‑bit to 4‑bit optimizer states, solving second‑moment zero‑point failure via linear mappings and rank‑1 normalization, and combining with factorization for further savings.
> - Practical impact: 4‑bit Adam/AdamW (and SGDM in the framework) match FP32 accuracy across NLU/CLS/QA/MT and instruction fine‑tuning; end‑to‑end LoRA fine‑tuning benefits from reduced communication and memory, enabling larger models under fixed budgets.
> - Evaluation and scalability: Reports EM/F1 on SQuAD and AUC on vision; FSDP and optimizer offload show speed/memory gains; enables training of larger OPT/LLaMA under the same hardware.
> 
> 5) Diffusion models with conditional guidance for cross‑domain deepfake detection (NeurIPS 2024):
> - Trend: Frozen Stable Diffusion is guided by detector features (via attention‑based filter/weight modules and zero‑conv) to reconstruct source/target faces, forcing encoders to learn disentangled, generalizable features without inference overhead.
> - Generalization: Significant AUC/EER gains on unseen datasets (Celeb‑DF, DFDC‑P, WildDeepfake, DFD, DiffSwap) across EfficientNet‑B4/ViT backbones. Attention (CBAM, MHA) and cosine similarity on latent feature embeddings supervise the weighting of source/target cues.
> - Deployment: Plug‑and‑play training; inference remains a standard feedforward classifier head on the backbone.
> 
> Cross‑cutting trends (2023–2024):
> - Scalability and efficiency: Anchor‑free detection reduces representation costs; 4‑bit optimizers and factorization cut training memory while preserving accuracy; FSDP/offloading further improve throughput.
> - Robust generalization: JEPA‑style latent prediction and diffusion‑guided feature conditioning shift learning toward predictive, low‑noise features; EI RNNs move from structural constraints to spectrum‑centric design for time‑series stability.
> - Practical architectures and optimizers: Methods are implemented on YOLOv7/YOLOv5, EfficientNet‑B4, ViT, Swin‑T and trained with SGD/Adam/AdamW; COCO‑style evaluations remain the norm for vision detection tasks.
> 
> Overall, the trajectory is toward leaner representations and training (anchor‑free offsets, 4‑bit states), spectrum‑aware stability in recurrent deep networks, and feature‑level guidance (JEPA, diffusion) that improves cross‑domain robustness without increasing inference complexity.

**naive 最终答案**

> ## Matching Papers
> 
> **1. One-stage anchor-free part–body association (COCO/COCO-WholeBody style)**
> - **PBADet: One-Stage Anchor-Free Part-Body Association Detection (ICLR 2024)** — builds on YOLOv5/YOLOv7-style anchor-free heads with a single part-to-body center offset + task-alignment loss. Evaluated on COCO-HumanParts (derived from COCO), CrowdHuman, BodyHands; vs ED-Pose on COCO val it reports higher Precision/Recall/F1 for hands/feet.
> 
> **2. Implicit bias of label-free representation learning (JEPA/self-distillation vs MAE)**
> - **Why JEPA Self-Distillation Avoids Noisy Features: A Deep Linear Network Analysis (NeurIPS 2024)** — solves JEPA vs MAE (MSE-type objectives, eq. 5) dynamics in deep linear networks; shows JEPA biases toward high-influence/low-variance features, MAE toward high-covariance (noisy) ones.
> - **On the Similarities of Embeddings in Contrastive Learning** — complements with cosine-similarity geometry of embeddings under InfoNCE-style (cross-entropy) losses: optimal positive alignment + negative separation at −1/(n−1), mini-batch variance-reduction loss. *(No single paper contrasts MSE vs cross-entropy head-to-head with cosine similarity; these two cover the components.)*
> 
> **3. Spectral analysis of excitatory–inhibitory recurrent networks**
> - **Why Dale's Law Constrained Recurrent Neural Networks Learn Poorly (NeurIPS 2023)** — spectral (singular-value) analysis of ColEI/DANN RNNs on time-series/sequence tasks (adding problem, sequential MNIST, PTB, object recognition); shows the singular-value spectrum (normalized SVD entropy) — not sign constraints — explains instability/exploding gradients and poor learning.
> 
> **4. Memory-efficient 4-bit optimizer states**
> - **4-bit Optimizers: Training Large Models with 4-bit Optimizer States (NeurIPS 2023)** — 4-bit first/second moments for Adam/AdamW/SGDM via smaller blocks, rank-1 normalization, zero-point-excluded linear quantizer, and factorization (up to 57.7% memory savings). It frames LoRA as the delta-tuning alternative but does **not** itself run end-to-end LoRA fine-tuning. *(Themis paper fine-tunes Vicuna-7B with LoRA; Hessian paper analyzes LoRA fine-tuning of TinyLlama — LoRA and 4-bit states are covered in separate papers.)*
> 
> **5. Diffusion-guided cross-domain deepfake detection**
> - **DiffusionFake: Enhancing Generalization in Deepfake Detection via Guided Stable Diffusion** — ControlNet-style GuideModule injects detector features into frozen Stable Diffusion to reconstruct source/target faces; tested with EfficientNet-B4 and ViT-B, cross-dataset (FF++→Celeb-DF etc.), improving AUC/EER (not Precision/F1) with no inference overhead. *(Attention is used in filtering/weighting; metrics are AUC/EER rather than Precision/F1.)*
> 
> ## Development Trend of the Methods
> 
> - **Detection:** two-stage/anchor-based → one-stage anchor-free; associations simplified from many body-to-part offsets to a single scalable part-to-body center offset, with task-alignment learning; validated on COCO-derived benchmarks and extended to animals, beating pose estimators in Precision/Recall/F1.
> - **Self-supervised learning:** pixel-space reconstruction (MAE) → joint-embedding prediction (JEPA/self-distillation); theory (deep linear nets) shows objective choice changes *feature learning order* (influential vs noisy features); contrastive analysis formalizes optimal embedding geometry (alignment + uniform negative separation) and fixes mini-batch variance, with cosine similarity as the core metric.
> - **Recurrent E/I networks:** sign constraints were blamed → spectral (singular-value) analysis shows the *initial spectrum* (multimodal, dispersed singular values, low NSE) drives instability and poor learning, guiding better initializations; DANN robustness highlights architecture-dependent spectra.
> - **Optimizers:** 32-bit → 8-bit → 4-bit states; from naive block-wise quantization to outlier-aware small-block/rank-1 normalization and zero-point exclusion, combined with factorization and orthogonal memory tricks (LoRA-type delta tuning, sharding/offloading); enables 4× larger models under the same memory.
> - **Deepfake detection:** forgery simulation/attention-based feature engineering → generative guidance (frozen diffusion + ControlNet-style conditioning) that forces disentangled source/target feature learning, improving cross-domain generalization as a plug-and-play module over CNNs and ViTs.
> 
> **Caveats:** no single retrieved paper combines 4-bit optimizer states with end-to-end LoRA fine-tuning, and DiffusionFake reports AUC/EER rather than Precision/F1; the "MSE vs cross-entropy with cosine similarity" contrast is split across two representation-learning papers.

> Based on the retrieved context, here is the paper set that collectively covers the five topics, followed by a summary of the development trend.
> 
> ## Matching papers by topic
> 
> **1. One-stage, anchor-free part–body association on COCO-style benchmarks**
> - **PBADet (ICLR 2024)** — "One-stage anchor-free part-body association." Extends anchor-free object detection (YOLOv5/YOLOv7 anchor-free heads) with a single part-to-body center offset; evaluated on COCO-HumanParts, COCO val, BodyHands, CrowdHuman, AP-10K; reports AP, Precision/Recall/F1 (e.g., vs. ED-Pose on COCO val for hands/feet). ✓
> 
> **2. Implicit bias of label-free representation learning (JEPA/self-distillation vs. masked reconstruction; MSE vs. cross-entropy; cosine similarity)**
> - **"How JEPA Avoids Noisy Features: The Implicit Bias of Deep Linear Self-Distillation Networks" (NeurIPS 2024)** — analyzes JEPA/self-distillation vs. MAE (masked reconstruction) with exact deep-linear dynamics; both objectives are MSE (latent-space vs. input-space); shows JEPA prioritizes high-influence, low-variance features, verified by CCA on ImageNet I-JEPA vs. MAE. ✓ (covers JEPA vs. MAE with MSE)
> - **"On the Similarities of Embeddings in Contrastive Learning"** — analyzes label-free contrastive learning via cosine similarity of feature embeddings; characterizes InfoNCE (cross-entropy-style) loss optima (positive similarity 1, negative −1/(n−1)); proposes variance-reduction loss. ✓ (covers cosine similarity + cross-entropy/InfoNCE)
> - Together these two cover the full topic 2 (MSE-based JEPA vs. reconstruction, and cross-entropy/InfoNCE contrastive with cosine-similarity embeddings).
> 
> **3. Spectral analyses of E–I recurrent networks for time-series modeling, stability via singular values**
> - **"Learning better with Dale's Law: A Spectral Perspective" (NeurIPS 2023)** — excitatory–inhibitory RNNs (ColEI vs. DANN); spectral analysis of recurrent weights; multimodal/dispersed singular-value spectra vs. Marchenko–Pastur quarter-circle; normalised SVD entropy (NSE) as a stability/performance diagnostic (exploding/vanishing gradients); evaluated on time-series tasks (adding problem, sequential MNIST, Penn Tree Bank). ✓
> 
> **4. Memory-efficient training via 4-bit optimizer states (Adam/AdamW/SGD) and LoRA fine-tuning**
> - **"Memory Efficient Optimizers with 4-bit States" (NeurIPS 2023)** — 4-bit quantization of first/second moments for SGDM/Adam/AdamW; smaller block size, rank-1 normalization, zero-point exclusion; up to 57.7% memory savings; lossless fine-tuning of RoBERTa-L, Swin-T, GPT-2, LLaMA-7B/13B/33B on a single 80GB GPU; explicitly discusses LoRA as a complementary parameter-efficient method. ✓
> - **"Investigating the Overlooked Hessian Structure" (ICML 2025)** — SGD training (LeNet) and end-to-end LoRA fine-tuning (TinyLlama on MathQA); power-law Hessian spectra and generalization. ✓ (covers SGD + LoRA fine-tuning angle)
> 
> **5. Diffusion models with conditional guidance for cross-domain deepfake detection (attention, Precision/F1)**
> - **DiffusionFake** — plug-and-play framework injecting detector features into a frozen pre-trained Stable Diffusion via a ControlNet-inspired GuideModule (Feature Filter/Weight modules with attention) to reconstruct source/target images; improves cross-domain deepfake detection (FF++→Celeb-DF, WildDeepfake, DFDC-P, DFD, DiffSwap) with EfficientNet-B4 and ViT-B backbones; trained with Adam. **Partial match:** it uses attention and Transformer (ViT-B) backbones and Adam, but the retrieved content reports **AUC/EER**, not Precision/F1. (Precision/Recall/F1 appears in PBADet, but for part–body association, not deepfake detection.)
> 
> ## Development trend
> 
> - **Detection:** from multi-stage, anchor-based, body-to-part pipelines toward single-stage anchor-free formulations with a single part-to-body offset — simpler, scalable representation with stronger AP/F1 (PBADet vs. BPJDet/HierR-CNN).
> - **Self-supervised representation learning:** from empirical SSL to theoretical characterization of implicit bias — deep-linear analyses showing loss choice (MSE reconstruction vs. cross-entropy/InfoNCE) and geometry (cosine similarity on embeddings) determine which features are learned and how fast (JEPA's influential/low-variance features vs. MAE's variance-dominated features).
> - **Recurrent networks:** from unconstrained RNNs to biologically constrained excitatory–inhibitory networks, with spectral/singular-value analysis (NSE, spectrum transplant) replacing sign-constraint explanations for training stability — motivating spectral-aware initialization.
> - **Optimization/memory:** from full-precision 32-bit optimizer states to 4-bit quantized states (smaller blocks, rank-1 normalization, zero-point exclusion) enabling single-GPU large-model training, increasingly combined with parameter-efficient end-to-end fine-tuning such as LoRA.
> - **Deepfake detection:** from purely discriminative detectors to generative-model-guided training — frozen diffusion models with attention-based control modules force detectors to learn disentangled source/target features, improving cross-domain generalization with ViT/EfficientNet backbones.
> 
> **Caveats:** DiffusionFake reports AUC/EER rather than Precision/F1; the JEPA implicit-bias paper uses MSE objectives (cross-entropy contrast is covered by the separate embeddings-similarities paper); the 4-bit optimizer paper treats LoRA as a complementary/related method rather than combining them in one pipeline (the LoRA end-to-end fine-tuning is covered by the Hessian-structure paper).

I’m also comparing latent‑space prediction vs pixel reconstruction objectives (MSE vs CE) and want works that use cosine similarity probes and standard stochastic optimizers (Adam/AdamW/SGD). Which papers should I read?Please summarize the development trend of their methods.

Gold 1：

> Development trends across the five works converge toward resource‑efficient, end‑to‑end systems that generalize better by exploiting architectural simplifications, pretrained generative models, spectral control, and low‑precision optimization. The key trajectories and their time characteristics are:
> 
> 1) From anchor‑based, multi‑stage detection to one‑stage, anchor‑free, scalable association (2019–2024)
> - Shift: PBADet (ICLR 2024) replaces multi‑stage/anchor‑based body‑to‑part schemes with a one‑stage, anchor‑free design that adds a single part‑to‑body center offset. Compared to earlier extensions like BPJDet (2023), PBADet compresses the representation length and simplifies post‑processing, improving speed and robustness.
> - Scalability: The single offset scales to any number of parts without degrading performance, and generalizes beyond humans (e.g., wheels‑and‑cars; animal parts in AP‑10K), enabled by multi‑scale features and task‑alignment learning.
> - Practical stack: Standard optimizers and metrics are retained (SGD for training; CE/IoU losses; multi‑scale attention; Precision/Recall/F1 reported versus pose baselines). Datasets include COCO‑HumanParts and CrowdHuman, showing cross‑dataset robustness.
> 
> 2) From artifact‑specific deepfake cues to diffusion‑guided, Transformer‑conditioned generalization (2021–2024)
> - Shift: DiffusionFake (NeurIPS 2024) moves from hand‑crafted artifact simulation to reversing the generative process with a frozen Stable Diffusion model. A ControlNet‑style guide (cross‑attention, zero‑conv) injects detector features to reconstruct source/target faces, forcing disentangled representation learning that transfers to unseen forgeries.
> - Generalization: Consistent cross‑domain gains (e.g., Celeb‑DF, DFDC‑P, WildDeepfake, DiffSwap) without inference overhead; the framework remains plug‑and‑play for diverse backbones (EfficientNet/ViT).
> - Objective/tooling: Joint losses mix latent‑space denoising (L2 in diffusion), CE for classification, and cosine similarity‑based weighting between input and source/target latents; standard Adam optimization is used. This exemplifies a broader trend of exploiting pretrained diffusion models for robust features rather than artifact classifiers.
> 
> 3) From sign‑constrained EI RNNs to spectrum‑aware stabilization under Dale’s Law (pre‑2020 to 2023)
> - Problem: Naively imposing EI column sign constraints (ColEI) often harms learning due to multimodal, dispersed singular‑value spectra and exploding/vanishing gradients.
> - Shift: The 2023 spectral analysis shows performance depends more on singular‑value clustering than on sign constraints per se. Recurrent DANNs retain Dale’s Law but match standard RNN spectra and performance. Normalized SVD entropy (NSE) emerges as a compact predictor of stability/performance.
> - Design guidance: For resource‑constrained sensor RNNs, prioritize spectral initialization/control and balanced E/I ratios; gradient clipping helps. Trend is toward principled spectral criteria (NSE), not only architectural constraints.
> 
> 4) From 8‑bit to 4‑bit optimizer states with zero‑point‑aware quantization and factorization (2022–2023)
> - Shift: Memory Efficient Optimizers with 4‑bit States (NeurIPS 2023) push optimizer memory from 8‑bit to 4‑bit by (a) excluding the zero point for second moments (linear mapping), (b) rank‑1 normalization (row/column scales) to handle outliers, and (c) optional factorization of the second moment (Adafactor‑style) for further savings.
> - Practicality: Maintains accuracy on vision (ImageNet/Swin‑T), NLU (GLUE), QA (SQuAD), MT (WMT14), and instruction tuning (LLaMA‑7B/13B/33B) using Adam/AdamW, with reported Precision/F1 and BLEU close to FP32. Integrates naturally with FSDP and enables small‑GPU fine‑tuning; compatible with low‑rank adapters (LoRA context) for end‑to‑end, resource‑constrained training.
> 
> 5) Objective shift: latent prediction (JEPA) vs pixel reconstruction (MAE) clarifies what features are learned (2024)
> - Theory: Deep linear analysis shows JEPA (latent prediction with stop‑grad) prioritizes influential, predictive features (high regression coefficients) and does so more strongly with depth, whereas MAE (pixel MSE) prioritizes highly covarying/high‑variance features.
> - Implication: For perception tasks under limited compute/data, latent‑space prediction (JEPA‑style) better targets semantic, low‑variance structure; pixel MSE can over‑weight fine‑grained, noisy details. This theoretical insight aligns with practice where diffusion‑guided and JEPA‑like objectives improve generalization speed/quality.
> 
> Overall system trend relative to the query
> - (a) Part association for HMI: One‑stage, anchor‑free detectors (PBADet) using multi‑scale attention and task alignment provide fast, scalable hand/face‑to‑body linkage on COCO‑family data with standard SGD training and CE/IoU losses.
> - (b) Robust face‑swap detection: Generative guidance (DiffusionFake) uses Transformer‑style conditioning into a frozen diffusion model, with cosine‑similarity probes, CE classification, and MSE denoising—improving cross‑dataset generalization with no inference overhead.
> - (c) Stable EI RNNs: Spectrum‑aware EI designs (DANN RNNs) and NSE‑guided initialization/stability tackle exploding gradients better than sign constraints alone, especially for smaller networks or skewed E/I ratios.
> - (d) Small‑GPU fine‑tuning: 4‑bit optimizer states (with zero‑point‑free second‑moment quantization, rank‑1 normalization, and optional factorization) keep NLU/Vision/Instruction‑tuning accuracy high under Adam/AdamW, and mesh with LoRA/FSDP for practical scaling.
> 
> Cross‑cutting characteristics
> - Scalability and efficiency: Reduced detection heads (PBADet), plug‑and‑play diffusion guidance (DiffusionFake), and 4‑bit optimizers all target end‑to‑end throughput on standard hardware.
> - Generalization over time: The field is moving from handcrafted or constraint‑only designs (artifact cues; ColEI) to principled, pretrained‑model guidance (diffusion, JEPA) and spectral/quantization theory to ensure stability and accuracy.
> - Standard tooling: Common optimizers (SGD, Adam/AdamW), cosine similarity‑based probes, and CE/MSE losses remain the backbone while objectives are refocused toward latent prediction and spectrum/quantization‑aware training.
> 
> In sum, recent methods coalesce around end‑to‑end anchor‑free perception, pretrained diffusion/latent objectives for generalization, spectrum‑aware EI stabilization, and 4‑bit optimizer states—together enabling resource‑constrained yet accurate systems with strong cross‑domain performance.

**naive 最终答案**

> ## Papers to read
> 
> **(a) Hand/face→person association for HMI (fast anchor-free detector)**
> - **PBADet: One-Stage Anchor-Free Approach for Part-Body Association** (ICLR 2024). Extends anchor-free detection (FCOS/TOOD) with a single part-to-body center offset; evaluated on COCOHumanParts, BodyHands, CrowdHuman (face–body), COCO-WholeBody; state-of-the-art, one-stage/end-to-end, efficient.
> 
> **(b) Face-swap detection generalizing to unseen forgeries (diffusion + Transformer-style conditioning)**
> - **DiffusionFake** (guided Stable Diffusion). Reverses the forgery process: detector features are filtered/weighted, injected through a ControlNet-style Guide Module into a *frozen pre-trained* Stable Diffusion to reconstruct source and target images; training uses classification + diffusion (MSE) losses; inference adds no overhead; large cross-dataset AUC gains on Celeb-DF/DFDC/WildDeepfake/DiffSwap.
> - **Universal Guidance for Diffusion Models** (ICLR 2024). Training-free guidance for controlling frozen diffusion models via differentiable functions (face, segmentation, object detection) — relevant for guidance/conditioning design.
> 
> **(c) Stabilizing EI-constrained RNNs with exploding gradients (sensor streams)**
> - **"Learning better with Dale's Law: A Spectral Perspective"** (NeurIPS 2023). Explains why E/I sign-constrained (ColEI) RNNs learn poorly and explode: it's the initial singular-value spectrum, not sign constraints; DANN-RNNs keep good (quarter-circle/Marchenko–Pastur) spectra; gradient clipping stabilizes; NSE predicts trainability.
> 
> **(d) Fine-tuning vision+language with LoRA + 4-bit optimizer states on small GPUs (keep Precision/F1)**
> - **"Memory Efficient Optimizers with 4-bit States"** (NeurIPS 2023). 4-bit AdamW/Adam states (block-size B128, rank-1 normalization, zero-point exclusion, factorization); matches 32-bit AdamW on GLUE (accuracy), SQuAD (F1), ImageNet, GPT-2, and LLaMA-7B/13B/33B Alpaca tuning; up to ~57.7% memory savings, enabling LLaMA-7B on one 80GB GPU; built on the LoRA line of work.
> - **NEFTune** (ICLR 2024). Noisy-embedding instruction fine-tuning; compatible with QLoRA, boosts AlpacaEval without extra compute.
> 
> **Latent-space prediction vs pixel reconstruction (MSE vs CE), cosine-similarity probes, standard optimizers**
> - **DiffusionFake** — the clearest comparison anchor: it uses pixel-space diffusion reconstruction (MSE-style, plus CE classification) rather than predicting in latent space, showing reconstruction-as-auxiliary-objective improves feature disentanglement/generalization.
> - **CoBO: Correlated Latent Space Bayesian Optimization** — works *in* latent space with a reconstruction (negative log-likelihood) objective plus Lipschitz alignment; useful for the latent-vs-pixel trade-off framing.
> - **"On the Similarities of Embeddings in Contrastive Learning"** — direct cosine-similarity analysis of embedding pairs (positive/negative similarity statistics) as a representation probe.
> - The above papers consistently use standard stochastic optimizers: Adam (DiffusionFake), AdamW (4-bit optimizers, CoBO, LDReg), SGD/LARS/AdamW (LDReg pretraining); cosine LR schedules are standard.
> 
> ## Development trend of the methods
> - **(a) Detection/association:** two-stage/anchor-based + heuristic matching (Faster R-CNN, body-part joint detection, BPJDet's body-to-part offsets) → **one-stage anchor-free end-to-end part-to-body association** (PBADet), trading multi-stage complexity for efficiency, scalability to many parts, and robustness to occluded parts.
> - **(b) Deepfake generalization:** forgery-simulation augmentation and architecture engineering (attention, frequency, reconstruction, disentangling) → **inversion of the generation process via frozen pre-trained diffusion generators** with explicit guidance/conditioning (DiffusionFake; training-free Universal Guidance), moving from data-side simulation to model-side generative supervision for unseen forgeries.
> - **(c) EI RNNs:** naive sign-constrained partitioning (ColEI) that impairs learning and causes gradient explosion → **spectral-property analysis** showing the singular-value spectrum (not sign constraints) matters → **DANN-style EI architectures that respect Dale's law while preserving standard-RNN spectra**, with gradient clipping and NSE as diagnostics.
> - **(d) Fine-tuning:** full 32-bit-optimizer fine-tuning → **parameter-efficient low-rank adapters (LoRA) + progressively lower-bit optimizer states (8-bit → 4-bit AdamW)** with smarter quantization (smaller blocks, rank-1 normalization, zero-point exclusion) and light regularizers (NEFTune), preserving accuracy/F1 while enabling small-GPU training.
> 
> Note: I could not find a paper in the collection that directly and exclusively benchmarks "latent-space prediction vs pixel reconstruction (MSE vs CE)" as its headline question; that specific head-to-head must be inferred from DiffusionFake (pixel reconstruction), CoBO (latent-space modeling), and the video-representation paper comparing forward/reconstruction modeling vs temporal contrastive objectives.

> Based on the document collection, here are the papers matching your four requirements plus your two side questions, followed by the method trends.
> 
> ## Recommended papers
> 
> **(a) Anchor-free hand/face→person association for HMI**
> - **PBADet: One-Stage Anchor-Free Part-Body Association Detection** (ICLR 2024) — links hands/face to the correct body/person using a single part-to-body center offset on COCO-HumanParts/BodyHands/CrowdHuman; one-stage, anchor-free, evaluated with Precision/Recall/F1. Directly fits your HMI + fast anchor-free detector requirement.
> 
> **(b) Face-swap detection generalizing to unseen forgeries via diffusion + Transformer-style conditioning**
> - **DiffusionFake: Enhancing Generalization in Deepfake Detection via Guided Stable Diffusion** (NeurIPS 2024) — injects detector features into a frozen pre-trained Stable Diffusion via a ControlNet-style Guide Module; Feature Filter/Weight modules use channel/spatial attention + Multi-Head Attention (cross-attention) conditioning to reconstruct source/target faces, forcing disentangled features. Trained with Adam + MSE; boosts cross-dataset AUC without inference overhead.
> - **Universal Guidance for Diffusion Models** (ICLR 2024) — training-free conditioning/guidance of frozen diffusion models by arbitrary signals (incl. face recognition, detection); relevant for guiding a pre-trained generator without retraining.
> 
> **(c) Stabilizing EI-constrained RNNs against exploding gradients**
> - **Why Dale's Law Constrained Recurrent Neural Networks Learn Poorly** (NeurIPS 2023) — shows EI-constrained ColEI RNNs fail largely because of pathological (multimodal, dispersed) singular-value spectra, not sign constraints; gradient clipping substantially helps, and DANN RNNs (which keep good spectra) plus gradient clipping stabilize training. Directly addresses EI-constrained RNN stabilization.
> 
> **(d) 4-bit optimizer states for fine-tuning VLMs/LLMs on small GPUs with low-rank adapters**
> - **Memory Efficient Optimizers with 4-bit States** (NeurIPS 2023) — quantizes Adam/AdamW first/second moments to 4-bit (B128/DE + rank-1 normalization, zero-point exclusion), matching or exceeding 32-bit AdamW on GLUE (accuracy), SQuAD (F1), ImageNet, E2E-NLG, LLaMA Alpaca; up to ~57% memory savings, enabling 7B fine-tuning on one GPU. Fits your Precision/F1 + small-GPU + AdamW requirement (LoRA cited as the low-rank-adaptation baseline).
> - Supporting: **Investigating the Overlooked Hessian Structure** (ICML 2025) — analyzes LoRA fine-tuning; **NEFTune** — QLoRA-compatible instruction tuning.
> 
> **(Side) Latent prediction vs pixel reconstruction (MSE vs CE)**
> - **How JEPA Avoids Noisy Features: The Implicit Bias of Deep Linear Self Distillation Networks** (NeurIPS 2024) — directly compares latent-space prediction (JEPA-style, CE/similarity objectives) vs pixel reconstruction (MAE-style, MSE), proving JEPA biases toward "influential" features and ignores noisy ones, unlike MSE reconstruction.
> 
> **(Side) Cosine-similarity probes + standard optimizers (Adam/AdamW/SGD)**
> - **On the Similarities of Embeddings in Contrastive Learning** — a unified cosine-similarity framework for contrastive losses (SimCLR/DCL/DHEL), trained with **SGD**; provides the cosine-similarity probing/analysis tool. DiffusionFake and the 4-bit optimizer paper use **Adam/AdamW**, covering the optimizer variety you want.
> 
> ## Development trend of the methods
> 
> 1. **Part-body association**: two-stage/heuristic hand-body matching (Zhou 2018, BodyHands) → single-stage **anchor-based** body-to-part offsets (BPJDet) → **one-stage anchor-free** part-to-body offsets (PBADet). Trend: fewer stages, anchor-free dense prediction, smaller/extensible representations, end-to-end and resource-efficient.
> 
> 2. **Face forgery detection**: forgery-simulation augmentation and handcrafted detectors → framework engineering (attention, frequency) → **reconstruction-based decoupling** using pre-trained generators. Trend: from bespoke detectors to **plug-and-play guidance of frozen diffusion models** (ControlNet-style/Transformer conditioning, and training-free Universal Guidance), gaining generalization to unseen forgeries with zero added inference cost.
> 
> 3. **EI-constrained RNNs**: naive sign-constrained (ColEI) networks (which explode) → analysis showing the true culprit is the **singular-value spectrum**, not sign constraints → **principled spectral design (DANN) + gradient clipping** (and NSE as a pre-training diagnostic). Trend: from ad-hoc fixes toward initialization/spectral-property-aware stabilization.
> 
> 4. **Memory-efficient fine-tuning**: full fine-tuning → low-rank adapters (LoRA) → **lower-bit optimizer states (8-bit → 4-bit)** with better quantizers (small blocks, rank-1 normalization, zero-point exclusion). Trend: pushing bitwidth down while **preserving full-precision accuracy/F1**, democratizing large-model tuning on small GPUs.
> 
> 5. **Representation objectives**: pixel-space MSE reconstruction → **latent-space prediction**, with theory showing latent prediction's implicit bias toward informative features and away from noise; cosine-similarity analyses quantify embedding structure under standard SGD/Adam/AdamW optimization. Trend: understanding *why* latent objectives beat pixel objectives rather than just empirical gains.

**Gold（保持结果文件中的原始内容；部分条目本身为序列化字典字符串）**

Gold 1：

> Cross‑paper development trends across the requested areas
> 
> 1) Anchor‑free part–body association in detection (PBADet, ICLR 2024)
> - Shift in design: from two‑stage/anchor‑based (e.g., YOLO variants with body‑to‑part offsets) to one‑stage, anchor‑free part‑to‑body association with a single center offset per part.
> - Multi‑scale + task alignment: leverages multi‑level feature maps and task‑aligned learning (from TOOD) instead of extra matching heuristics. This reduces representation length and post‑processing complexity.
> - Scalability trend: representation size is constant in the number of parts for association (single 2D offset), enabling addition of more parts without proportional growth in outputs.
> - Empirical reporting broadens: beyond AP (VOC/COCO), comparisons include Precision/Recall/F1 (vs. pose methods in Appendix), and association‑specific miss‑match rates; qualitative diagrams show model outputs across datasets.
> - Practical training: standard PyTorch + SGD, standard classification/IoU/DFL losses; benefits generalize across YOLOv5/7 backbones at high input resolutions.
> 
> 2) Spectral and interpretability analyses under Dale’s Law (NeurIPS 2023)
> - From sign constraints to spectra: the community moved from attributing EI performance gaps to sign constraints to showing spectral properties (singular‑value distributions) are the primary driver of learning quality.
> - Diagnostics mature: adoption of normalized SVD entropy (NSE) and singular‑value histograms (vs. raw eigenvalues) to predict trainability, stability, and variance across seeds.
> - Scaling and architecture effects: larger EI networks and more balanced E/I ratios yield unimodal, clustered spectra (higher NSE) and better learning, even when some singular values are large—highlighting the role of overall spectrum shape.
> - Practical implication: to make EI‑constrained deep networks (trained with standard losses/SGD) learn well, initialize for unimodal, clustered singular‑value spectra; spectrum “transplant” tests show spectra matter more than sign constraints.
> 
> 3) Implicit bias of self‑supervision: JEPA vs. masked reconstruction (NeurIPS 2024)
> - Objective pivot: growing preference for joint‑embedding prediction (JEPA) over masked reconstruction (MAE, MSE‑optimized) due to a distinct depth‑dependent implicit bias.
> - Training‑dynamics insight: analytical ODEs for deep linear encoders show JEPA prioritizes high‑influence (predictive, low‑noise) features, while MAE prioritizes high‑variance/co‑varying features; the JEPA bias strengthens with depth.
> - Time‑resolved analyses: closed‑form dynamics and critical times t* quantify which features are learned first; controlled linear generative settings (temporal views, random masking) link theory to practice.
> - Practical takeaway: for feedforward encoders/Transformers, deeper JEPA encoders gravitate toward semantically useful embeddings faster than MSE‑based reconstruction, aligning with observed downstream performance.
> 
> 4) Memory‑efficient training with 4‑bit optimizer states (NeurIPS 2023)
> - Bit‑width trend: from 16/8‑bit to 4‑bit optimizer states for AdamW by addressing outlier and zero‑point issues in 1st/2nd moments.
> - Quantization advances: smaller block sizes and rank‑1 normalization (row/column statistics) improve first/second‑moment approximation; for v, excluding zero in mapping and using linear quantizers prevents catastrophic update scaling.
> - Practical fine‑tuning at scale: validated on image/NLP/MT tasks and instruction tuning of LLaMA‑7B/13B/33B; reduces total training memory by up to ~58% and enables larger models per GPU; compatible with optimizer offloading and fused kernels. (Implementation used common LLM fine‑tuning pipelines; LoRA repositories were used for some experiments.)
> - Outcome trend: low‑precision optimizer states increasingly become the default lever for scaling end‑to‑end fine‑tuning on commodity hardware without accuracy loss relative to full‑precision AdamW.
> 
> 5) Cross‑domain policy adaptation in RL via value‑guided filtering (NeurIPS 2023)
> - From dynamics‑gap to value‑consistency: methods shift from penalizing single‑step dynamics mismatch to selecting source transitions whose value targets match the target domain (measured via fictitious value proximity with an ensemble dynamics model).
> - Data‑efficiency trend: with limited target interactions, value‑guided filtering reuses large source buffers more safely, improving adaptation under both kinematic and morphology shifts; training curves over steps t confirm higher sample efficiency.
> - Theoretical underpinning: performance bounds re‑expressed in terms of value differences (and, in offline‑source settings, policy regularization), aligning the learning signal with long‑horizon returns rather than one‑step likelihoods.
> 
> Cross‑cutting patterns
> - Task‑aligned signals over generic proxies: part‑center offsets (association), singular‑value spectra (EI stability), value proximity (domain adaptation), and predictive latent targets (JEPA) all emphasize aligning learning signals with the end task, replacing heuristics (anchors, sign constraints) or myopic proxies (one‑step dynamics, raw variance).
> - Efficiency at scale: multi‑scale/anchor‑free heads reduce output dimensionality and decoding overhead; 4‑bit optimizer states lower memory/communication costs, enabling larger‑model fine‑tuning (e.g., LLaMA) on fewer GPUs.
> - Time‑aware diagnostics: several works characterize learning dynamics explicitly over time t—ODE solutions (JEPA/MAE), spectrum evolution vs. depth/size (Dale’s Law), and return curves vs. interaction steps (RL transfer)—supporting principled choices of objectives, inits, and data selection.
> - Reporting broadens: beyond task AP, studies incorporate Precision/Recall/F1 (association vs. pose), entropy/spectral metrics (NSE), and value‑based selection statistics, reflecting a maturing emphasis on interpretability and diagnostics.
> 
> Overall trajectory
> - 2023→2024 methods increasingly favor scalable, selection‑centric, and theory‑justified designs: anchor‑free association with multi‑scale alignment (detection), spectrum‑aware initialization/analysis (EI networks), value‑targeted data sharing (RL), predictive latent objectives (JEPA), and 4‑bit optimizer states (training systems). Together these trends improve robustness, sample/memory efficiency, and transfer while keeping performance competitive or superior to prior baselines.

**naive 最终答案**

> Based on the retrieved context, here are the papers matching your five topics, followed by the development trend.
> 
> ## Papers
> 
> 1) **PBADet: One-Stage Anchor-Free Part-Body Association** (doc `08b70bc3…`) — ICLR 2024. Extends one-stage anchor-free detection (YOLOv5/v7/v8) with a single part-to-body center offset over multi-scale feature maps plus task-alignment learning; reports Hand AP, conditional accuracy, joint AP (BodyHands/COCOHumanParts/CrowdHuman), and higher precision/recall/F1 than ED-Pose for hands/feet.
> 
> 2) **Why Dale's Law Constrained RNNs Learn Poorly: A Spectral Perspective** (doc `e63a94c4…`) — NeurIPS 2023. Spectral/interpretability analysis of networks with excitatory (E)/inhibitory (I) sign constraints (ColEI vs DANN); uses singular-value decomposition, spectrum "transplant" experiments, and normalized SVD entropy (NSE) as a diagnostic predicting performance; concludes singular-value spectra matter more than sign constraints.
> 
> 3) **How JEPA Avoids Noisy Features: The Implicit Bias of Deep Linear Self-Distillation Networks** (doc `40fde037…`) — NeurIPS 2024. Analyzes implicit bias of joint-embedding self-distillation (JEPA) vs masked reconstruction (MAE, MSE-style) in deep linear networks; JEPA prioritizes high-influence/"slow" features in a step-wise greedy manner while MAE prioritizes high-variance features; depth strengthens JEPA's bias; ImageNet-1K CCA experiments confirm faster alignment with perceptual low-variance subspace.
> 
> 4) **Memory Efficient Optimizers with 4-bit States** (doc `8d5e1455…`) — NeurIPS 2023. Pushes Adam/AdamW optimizer states from 8-bit to 4-bit (smaller block size, rank-1 normalization, zero-point-excluding linear quantizer, factorized second moment); enables LLaMA-7B fine-tuning on one 80GB GPU with up to 57.7% memory savings, matching 32-bit accuracy with closely aligned training-loss curves over steps; discusses LoRA-style low-rank tuning.
> 
> 5) **Cross-Domain Policy Adaptation via Value-Guided Data Filtering (VGDF)** (doc `27926829…`) — NeurIPS 2023. Selectively shares source transitions whose paired next-state values are close (Fictitious Value Proximity) under limited target interactions; extends to offline-source/online-target setting (VGDF+BC with behavior cloning); outperforms dynamics-discrepancy methods (DARC) on kinematic/morphology shifts.
> 
> ## Development trend
> 
> - **Detection (1):** from two-stage/anchor-based body-to-part offsets (BPJDet) → one-stage anchor-free with a *single* part-to-body offset on multi-scale features, giving simpler, scalable association with better AP/Precision/Recall/F1.
> - **EI networks (2):** from attributing poor learning to *sign constraints* → recognizing *initial spectral properties* (multimodal/dispersed singular values) as the dominant factor; diagnostics shift from raw performance to pre-training spectral measures (NSE).
> - **SSL (3):** from reconstruction in data space (MAE, MSE) → prediction in latent space (JEPA self-distillation); understanding shifts from "what is learned" to *implicit bias/order of feature learning*, with step-wise/greedy dynamics and depth-dependent effects.
> - **Optimization (4):** from full-precision (32-bit) → 8-bit → 4-bit optimizer states, with increasingly fine-grained quantization (smaller blocks, rank-1 normalization, zero-point exclusion, factorization) to stay lossless while shrinking memory for practical LLaMA fine-tuning, verified by aligned training curves over t.
> - **RL transfer (5):** from single-step dynamics-discrepancy correction (reward penalties, DARC) → long-horizon *value-consistency* filtering; from online source access → offline source + limited online target (VGDF+BC); from importance weighting → rejection sampling.
> 
> Overall: a common trend toward simpler/unified representations, replacing heuristics with principled analysis (spectra, implicit bias, value consistency), and aggressive compression (4-bit) with verified lossless convergence — each validated with quantitative metrics (AP/Precision/Recall/F1, accuracy, F1, memory savings) and training-dynamics curves over t.

**community 最终答案**

> Based on the collection, here are the papers covering your five areas:
> 
> **1) Anchor-free part-body association (PBADet, ICLR 2024, doc 08b70bc3…)**
> One-stage, anchor-free detection over **multi-scale feature maps** with a single part-to-body center offset; three-head design (classification, localization, displacement) with task-alignment learning. Reports Hand AP, Conditional Accuracy, Joint AP on BodyHands/COCO-HumanParts, and higher **precision, recall, and F1** vs ED-Pose. *Gap:* no explicit attention module is used (task-alignment replaces centerness); association loss, multi-scale offsets, and task-align are ablated.
> 
> **2) Spectral/interpretability analysis of excitatory-inhibitory sign constraints (Dale's Law, NeurIPS 2023, doc e63a94c4…)**
> Compares sign-constrained ColEI vs standard/DANN RNNs trained with (projected) gradient descent on MSE and cross-entropy tasks. **Singular-value (SVD) spectrum** and normalized SVD entropy (NSE) are the key diagnostics; spectrum-transplant experiments show singular values matter more than sign constraints. *Gap:* "cosine similarity" diagnostics are not used here; that appears instead in the contrastive-embedding paper (doc 160e1407…, embedding cosine similarities) and the Hessian power-law paper (doc 582d138d…, spectral + LoRA fine-tuning).
> 
> **3) Implicit bias of JEPA self-distillation vs masked reconstruction (MAE), both MSE-optimized (NeurIPS 2024, doc 40fde037…)**
> Solves the training dynamics of deep linear networks for both objectives and derives **critical times t*** — JEPA prioritizes "influential" (high regression-coefficient) features, MAE only high-variance ones; depth strengthens JEPA's bias. Feature-evolution diagrams over t and ImageNet ViT experiments with CCA confirm JEPA aligns faster to the low-variance perceptual subspace. *Gap:* experiments are on ImageNet ViTs, not CIFAR-100; the "Transformers" here are ViTs, and feedforward classifiers are the deep-linear proxies.
> 
> **4) 4-bit optimizer states for AdamW (NeurIPS 2023, doc 8d5e1455…)**
> Quantizes first/second moments (B128 + rank-1 normalization, zero-point-free linear quantizer, factorization). Enables **LLaMA-7B/13B/33B fine-tuning** on Alpaca (LLaMA-7B on one 80 GB GPU), ~57.7% memory saving, and reports a **training-loss-vs-step diagram** closely matching 32-bit AdamW; also Swin-T ImageNet, RoBERTa-L, GPT-2. *Gap:* LoRA appears only as related work ("delta tuning"); the paper does full-parameter fine-tuning, not explicit end-to-end LoRA, and no ResNet-50 setup.
> 
> **5) Cross-domain RL policy adaptation via value-guided transition filtering (VGDF, NeurIPS 2023, doc 27926829…)**
> Selectively shares source-domain transitions whose **fictitious value proximity** (paired value targets across domains) exceeds a quantile, using a dynamics ensemble + optimistic exploration, under limited target interactions; offline-source variant VGDF+BC. Outperforms DARC/dynamics-discrepancy baselines on kinematics/morphology shifts, with reward-vs-target-steps curves.
> 
> **Development trend across these methods:**
> - **From handcrafted to learned/implicit association:** part-body detection moved from multi-stage, anchor-based heuristics to a single one-stage anchor-free offset over multi-scale features (PBADet), simplifying representation and boosting AP/Precision/F1.
> - **From performance-only to spectral/interpretability diagnostics:** EI networks are now understood through singular-value spectra (NSE) rather than sign constraints alone; this spectral-diagnostic view extends to Hessian power-laws for fine-tuned/LoRA models.
> - **From comparing final accuracies to analyzing training dynamics:** both JEPA-vs-MAE (critical times, feature-evolution over t) and 4-bit optimizers (loss-vs-step curves) emphasize *how* methods converge over time, matching the request for dynamics-over-t diagrams.
> - **From memory-hungry full-precision training to compressed/PEFT-compatible training:** 4-bit optimizer states preserve full-precision convergence while drastically cutting memory, the direction needed for practical LLaMA-scale fine-tuning.
> - **From dynamics-mismatch heuristics to value-consistency principles:** RL transfer shifted from modeling transition gaps (DARC) to filtering source data by long-horizon value proximity (VGDF), enabling adaptation with minimal target interaction.
> 
> **What could not be established:** an attention-based variant of anchor-free part-body detection; cosine-similarity diagnostics in the EI/sign-constraint paper; CIFAR-100 JEPA experiments; ResNet-50 fine-tuning; and end-to-end LoRA fine-tuning with the 4-bit optimizer — none of these appear in the retrieved documents.

**问题：** I’m building an on-device perception and control stack with tight GPU memory. I need a self-supervised detector that can discover many objects (and their parts) in COCO-like scenes using cosine-similarity of feature embeddings, train end-to-end on Transformers/ResNet-50 with a 4‑bit optimizer, and also plug in an interpretable recurrent module for time-series control that follows excitatory/inhibitory constraints. I plan to pretrain the vision backbone with a JEPA-style (latent-space MSE) objective. Which works should I study to design this system?Please summarize the development trend of their methods.

Gold 1：

> {'answer': 'Development trends across the five works converge on a practical recipe for your on‑device, self‑supervised perception+control stack. The key trajectories are:\n\n1) From “one prominent object” to many objects and parts, with explicit composition\n- Earlier self-supervised detectors (e.g., CutLER) bias toward a single salient object; HASSOD moves to hierarchical adaptive clustering that merges adjacent regions by cosine similarity of DINO/ViT features, ensembling multiple merge thresholds to adaptively discover many objects per COCO-like scene. It then builds whole/part/subpart trees from mask coverage relations and trains a detector with a Mean-Teacher scheme (teacher targets ramp up; pseudo-label targets ramp down). Trend: feature-similarity clustering + hierarchical composition + efficient teacher–student replaces multi-round self-training, improving recall (e.g., LVIS Mask AR 20.2→22.5; SA‑1B 17.0→26.0) while using fewer images/iterations.\n\n2) From anchor-based, body→part offsets to anchor-free, part→body association that scales\n- BPJDet (2023) extends YOLO with body→part center offsets but grows representation with each new part and can break under occlusion. PBADet (ICLR 2024) flips to part→body: a single 2D center offset branch atop anchor-free heads and multi-level features. Trend: one-stage, anchor-free heads with a single, always-valid part→body offset, better scalability to many parts, simpler post-processing, and strong results on COCOHumanParts/BodyHands.\n\n3) From pixel-space reconstruction to latent-space prediction for pretraining\n- MAE vs JEPA: the deep-linear analysis shows JEPA-style (latent-space MSE with stop-grad teacher) prioritizes high-influence, predictive features (high regression coefficients), especially as encoder depth increases, whereas MAE favors high-variance covarying features. Trend: self-distillation/JEPA-style pretraining for vision backbones to hone predictive, lower-variance semantics that downstream detection and part reasoning benefit from.\n\n4) From full/8-bit to 4-bit state optimizers with structure-aware quantization\n- 4-bit Optimizers (NeurIPS 2023) push Adam/AdamW states to 4-bit by: (a) smaller blocks (e.g., B128) for first moment, (b) eliminating zero in the second-moment quantizer (linear mapping) to avoid division blow-ups, and (c) rank‑1 normalization (row+column scales) or factorization for second moment. Trend: robust 4‑bit training on ViT/ResNet‑50 class models (e.g., Swin‑T) with comparable accuracy to FP32 while cutting optimizer memory >50% and enabling larger models under the same budget—well-suited for on-device fine-tuning.\n\n5) From “Dale’s Law hurts learning” to spectrum-aware EI RNNs for interpretable control\n- Recurrent DANNs (vs simple ColEI partitions) show that spectral properties—not just sign constraints—govern learning stability and performance. Multimodal, dispersed singular-value spectra (common in naive EI partitions) impair learning; unimodal, clustered spectra (high normalized SVD entropy) correlate with good performance. Trend: for EI-constrained, interpretable time-series controllers, use DANN-style EI parameterization with spectrum-aware initialization/monitoring (NSE), gradient clipping as needed, and small-to-moderate sizes; performance is robust even with few inhibitory units and scales with network size.\n\nWhat to study for your system\n- Object/part discovery and self-supervised training: HASSOD (hierarchical adaptive clustering by cosine similarity of ViT features + whole/part/subpart trees + Mean Teacher with adaptive targets; trained Cascade Mask R‑CNN on ResNet‑50/Transformer backbones).\n- Scalable part association head: PBADet (one-stage anchor-free det., multi-scale features, single part→body center-offset branch; task-aligned learning). Use its offset head atop your detector once pseudo-labels are available.\n- Backbone pretraining objective: JEPA implicit-bias analysis—why latent-space MSE self-distillation helps learn predictive, low-variance semantics versus MAE; use this for your ViT/ResNet‑50 pretraining.\n- Memory-constrained training: 4‑bit Optimizers—B128/DE for first moment; rank‑1 normalization + zero‑free linear quantizer for second moment; optional factorized v for further savings. Demonstrated on Swin‑T and RoBERTa/GPT.\n- Recurrent control module under Dale’s Law: “Learning better with Dale’s Law”—adopt recurrent DANNs, ensure clustered singular-value spectra (high normalized SVD entropy), and use gradient clipping; the analysis covers adding problem, sequential MNIST, and language modeling tasks.\n\nOverall trend line\n- Detection moves from saliency-only to many-object discovery with explicit whole/part/subpart structure; from iterative re-labeling to Mean‑Teacher self-training; from anchor-based to lean anchor-free part association. Pretraining shifts from MAE to JEPA-style latent prediction. Training shifts from FP32/8‑bit to reliable 4‑bit states with structured normalization and zero‑point handling. Control shifts from naive EI constraints to spectrum-aware EI RNNs (DANNs) that preserve interpretability and stability. These trends collectively enable end‑to‑end, self‑supervised, memory‑efficient, interpretable perception+control on COCO‑like scenes using Transformers/ResNet‑50 backbones with cosine‑similarity feature clustering.'}

**naive 最终答案**

> Based on the collection, study these works:
> 
> **1. HASSOD (Hierarchical Adaptive Self-Supervised Object Detection)** — for your detector. It discovers objects and their parts (whole/part/subpart) in MS-COCO-like scenes with no labels: it runs hierarchical adaptive clustering on frozen DINO ViT features, merging adjacent regions by pairwise **cosine similarity** of patch embeddings, adaptively determining the number of objects per image, and builds tree structures from mask coverage relations to label hierarchical levels. It then trains a Cascade Mask R-CNN (ResNet-50 initialized with DINO weights) with a Mean Teacher self-training scheme, evaluated class-agnostically with AR.
> 
> **2. Memory Efficient Optimizers with 4-bit States (NeurIPS 2023)** — for your 4-bit optimizer. It compresses Adam/AdamW first/second moments to 4 bits (smaller block size B128 for the first moment; rank-1 normalization, zero-point-excluding linear quantizer, and factorization for the second), achieving memory savings up to ~57.7% with accuracy matching 32-bit on vision (Swin-T image classification) and language Transformers.
> 
> **3. Learning Better with Dale's Law: A Spectral Perspective (NeurIPS 2023)** — for your interpretable excitatory/inhibitory recurrent module. It studies RNNs obeying Dale's Law (E/I sign constraints): classic column-constrained "ColEI" RNNs learn poorly, while Dale's ANNs (DANN) — reparameterizing weights into separate non-negative E-to-E, E-to-I, I-to-E matrices — learn as well as standard RNNs on time-series tasks (adding problem, sequential MNIST, language modeling). It shows the recurrent weight spectrum (multimodal/dispersed vs. unimodal), not just sign constraints, drives performance; normalized SVD entropy predicts learning quality.
> 
> **4. How JEPA Avoids Noisy Features (NeurIPS 2024)** — for your JEPA-style latent-space MSE pretraining. It analyzes JEPA objectives (predicting a target view's representation in latent space, e.g., I-JEPA) vs. MAE, proving via deep linear networks that JEPA implicitly prioritizes "influential" features and suppresses noise, aligning faster with the low-variance subspace containing perceptual features.
> 
> **5. LDReg (Local Dimensionality Regularization, ICLR 2024)** — supporting your backbone/embeddings. It regularizes local intrinsic dimensionality of SSL encoders to prevent local dimensional collapse, improving SimCLR/BYOL/MAE on ResNet-50/ViT-B, including downstream COCO detection/segmentation.
> 
> **Development trend of their methods:**
> - **Self-supervised object discovery:** evolved from saliency-based methods and Normalized Cuts (LOST/FOUND/FreeSOLO, TokenCut/CutLER) that find only one or a few prominent objects, to **hierarchical adaptive clustering (HASSOD)** that discovers many objects plus part-to-whole composition; training moved from inefficient multi-round self-training to smoother **Mean Teacher** self-training; evaluation shifted from AP to class-agnostic AR.
> - **Memory-efficient training:** optimizer-state compression went from 8-bit block-wise quantization to **4-bit** with finer-grained (small-block, rank-1, zero-point-free) quantizers and factorization, enabling near-lossless training of larger models under tight memory.
> - **Excitatory/inhibitory RNNs:** went from naive sign-constrained partitions (ColEI) that impair learning to **DANN-style reparameterization** that preserves E/I structure while learning well, with spectral analysis explaining the failure mode and guiding architecture choice.
> - **SSL pretraining:** shifted from reconstruction in input space (MAE) to **latent-space predictive (JEPA)** objectives, with theory showing JEPA's bias toward influential/noisy-robust features; complementary work (LDReg) counters dimensional collapse so embeddings stay useful for detection tasks.

**community 最终答案**

> Based on the context, study these four works:
> 
> 1. **HASSOD (Hierarchical Adaptive Self-Supervised Object Detection)** – for your self-supervised detector. It discovers many objects per image and whole/part/subpart levels via hierarchical adaptive clustering on DINO ViT features using pairwise **cosine similarity**, then trains a detector (Cascade Mask R-CNN) end-to-end with Mean Teacher self-training. Evaluated on COCO-derived datasets (LVIS, Objects365, SA-1B), improving zero-shot Mask AR.
> 
> 2. **4-bit Optimizers: Training Large Models with 4-bit Optimizer States** – for tight GPU memory. Compresses Adam/AdamW first/second moments to 4-bit (smaller block size, rank-1 normalization, zero-point exclusion, optional factorization), achieving near-lossless accuracy on vision Transformers (Swin-T), RoBERTa, GPT-2, LLaMA with up to ~57% memory savings.
> 
> 3. **Learning better with Dale's Law: A Spectral Perspective** – for the interpretable recurrent control module. Analyzes excitatory/inhibitory (E/I) constrained RNNs (ColEI vs Dale's ANNs) on sequential time-series tasks, showing E/I sign constraints alone aren't the problem — the recurrent weight spectrum is; DANN reparameterization (E→E, E→I, I→E projections) respects Dale's Law and learns as well as standard RNNs.
> 
> 4. **How JEPA Avoids Noisy Features: The Implicit Bias of Deep Linear Self Distillation Networks** – for your JEPA-style latent-space MSE pretraining. Shows JEPA (predicting latent targets via MSE) prioritizes high-influence features and suppresses noise better than MAE reconstruction, with deep-linear-network theory and ImageNet I-JEPA/MAE comparisons.
> 
> **Development trend:** (a) Detection: saliency/normalized-cut methods that find one or few prominent objects (LOST, FOUND, FreeSOLO, TokenCut, CutLER) → HASSOD's adaptive hierarchical clustering discovering many objects and their parts, with multi-round self-training replaced by efficient Mean Teacher. (b) Optimization: 32-bit → 8-bit block-wise → 4-bit states with finer quantization (smaller blocks, rank-1 normalization, zero-point exclusion, factorization) for lossless, memory-efficient training. (c) Recurrent E/I networks: simple sign-partitioned columns (ColEI, which train poorly) → DANN-style reparameterized E/I architectures that keep constraints yet match standard RNN performance, guided by spectral analysis. (d) SSL pretraining: input-space reconstruction (MAE, learns noisy high-variance features) → latent-space JEPA objectives (MSE in embedding space, prioritizes semantically influential features), with additional local-dimensionality regularization (LDReg) against collapse.

### paperscope:trend:258 — 评分与执行路径对照

**问题：** Help me find papers that, taken together, address: (a) sub‑byte optimizer state compression for Adam/AdamW to cut training memory without hurting accuracy; (b) the implicit bias of joint‑embedding self‑distillation in self‑supervised learning and why it favors predictive (not noisy) features; (c) biologically constrained deep networks that respect excitatory/inhibitory structure (Dale’s principle) with a spectral analysis of learning stability; (d) a one‑stage, anchor‑free method to associate parts with whole objects, evaluated on COCO‑style detection metrics; and (e) a benchmark for evaluating pretrained vision‑language Transformers on fine‑grained biological trait discovery (grounding, counting, reasoning) with interpretability measures such as F1/Precision/AUROC. I’m interested in works that also discuss fine‑tuning and practical evaluation.Please summarize the development trend of their methods.

**Gold（保持结果文件中的原始内容；部分条目本身为序列化字典字符串）**

Gold 1：

> Papers that collectively meet (a)–(e) and the development trends they reveal
> 
> (a) Sub‑byte optimizer state compression (Adam/AdamW): “Memory Efficient Optimizers with 4‑bit States” (NeurIPS 2023)
> Trend: pushing optimizer state precision from 8‑bit to 4‑bit without accuracy loss by diagnosing and fixing quantization failure modes.
> - From coarse, block‑wise 8‑bit quantization to sub‑byte (4‑bit) with targeted design: smaller blocks (B128) to handle heterogeneous outliers in moments; rank‑1 normalization to mix row/column scales; and, critically, excluding zero from the second‑moment map (DE‑0 or linear) to avoid the zero‑point failure that explodes step sizes through 1/√v.
> - Hybridization with factorization (for v) gives further memory savings; end‑to‑end results show parity with full‑precision AdamW on RoBERTa, Swin‑T, GPT‑2 Medium, machine translation, and instruction tuning of LLaMA‑7B/13B/33B, with up to 57.7% training memory reduction and practical speedups with offloading.
> - Overall direction: robust sub‑byte states via problem‑specific quantization (zero‑point handling, fine‑grained normalization) plus selective factorization—scaling fine‑tuning to larger backbones under fixed memory.
> 
> (b) Implicit bias of JEPA self‑distillation: “How JEPA Avoids Noisy Features” (NeurIPS 2024)
> Trend: theory clarifies why joint‑embedding self‑distillation favors predictive (not noisy) features as depth increases.
> - In deep linear models, JEPA shows greedy learning toward features with large regression coefficients (high “influence”), while MAE prioritizes high covariance/variance features; JEPA’s bias strengthens with encoder depth, reversing MAE’s order when variance and predictiveness disagree.
> - This yields a principled shift from reconstruction objectives (which chase variance and can absorb noise) to joint‑embedding prediction that emphasizes informative, low‑noise structure—aligning with empirical JEPA advantages.
> 
> (c) Biologically constrained deep networks (Dale’s principle): “Learning better with Dale’s Law: A Spectral Perspective” (NeurIPS 2023)
> Trend: moving from sign‑constraint explanations to spectrum‑aware design and diagnostics for EI networks.
> - Naïve column‑EI (ColEI) RNNs learn poorly primarily due to pathological, multimodal singular value spectra; spectrum “transplants” show spectral shape matters more than the mere sign constraints.
> - Dale’s ANNs (DANNs, extended to recurrent) recover unimodal, clustered spectra and match standard RNNs’ performance.
> - Normalized SVD entropy (NSE) emerges as a simple predictor of learnability/stability across EI ratios and network sizes; larger nets and more balanced E/I improve spectra and training stability.
> - Practical implication: spectral initialization/diagnostics—not just sign enforcement—are key to stable, Dale‑compatible deep networks.
> 
> (d) One‑stage, anchor‑free part–whole association: “PBADet: A One‑Stage Anchor‑Free Approach for Part‑Body Association” (ICLR 2024)
> Trend: from two‑stage/anchor‑based schemes to a single, anchor‑free head with a scalable, interpretable geometric link.
> - Replaces body‑to‑part multi‑offset encodings with a single 2D part‑to‑body center offset per location, keeping representation length fixed as parts grow and avoiding invalid links under occlusion.
> - Built on task‑aligned, multi‑scale anchor‑free detection; decoding is simple (predict body center and pick nearest enclosing body).
> - Strong COCO‑style evaluations (AP, APM/APL, mMR−2) on COCOHumanParts, BodyHands, and CrowdHuman; outperforms or matches anchor‑based baselines while scaling cleanly to many parts.
> 
> (e) Benchmarking VLMs for biological trait discovery: “VLM4Bio: A Benchmark Dataset…” (NeurIPS 2024 D&B)
> Trend: from generic VQA to domain‑specific, multi‑skill biological evaluation with grounding, counting, and reasoning checks.
> - 469K QA pairs over ~30K images (fish, birds, butterflies) spanning species classification, trait identification, trait grounding/referring, and trait counting—probing both prediction and visual reasoning.
> - Comprehensive practical evaluation: open vs MC formats, difficulty stratification by taxonomy, prompting (context, dense caption, chain‑of‑thought), and reasoning hallucination tests (False Confidence Test, NOTA).
> - Findings: pretrained VLMs do better on MC than open questions; struggle with fine‑grained classes, grounding, and counting; prompting helps mainly for the largest models (e.g., GPT‑4V/4o). Domain‑tuned models (e.g., BioCLIP) can surpass generic VLMs on species classification, motivating fine‑tuning on domain data.
> 
> Cross‑cutting development trends
> - Scalability under constraints: Sub‑byte (4‑bit) optimizer states and factorization materially reduce training memory while preserving accuracy, enabling fine‑tuning of larger SFT backbones; anchor‑free, single‑offset association scales to many parts without inflating heads; spectral diagnostics (NSE) guide stable scaling of Dale‑constrained deep nets.
> - From heuristics to mechanisms: Optimizer work identifies the zero‑point pitfall in v‑quantization and fixes it; JEPA theory explains why latent prediction avoids noisy features as depth grows; Dale’s‑law RNNs shift from “sign constraints” to “spectral properties” as the true knob for stability.
> - Evaluation sophistication: COCO‑style AP suites, mMR−2 and joint AP quantify detection/association quality; biological VLM benchmarks add reasoning‑focused diagnostics (FCT/NOTA) and task difficulty controls. Some works also report Precision/Recall/F1 (e.g., PBADet’s comparison to ED‑Pose) when contrasting detectors to pose estimators.
> - Fine‑tuning and practice: 4‑bit AdamW is validated across NLU, QA, CLS, MT, and instruction tuning (LLaMA‑7B/13B/33B), including fused kernels and offloading; PBADet trains with standard SGD and reuses YOLO backbones; VLM4Bio compares zero‑shot VLMs and highlights gains from domain‑tuned models (BioCLIP), outlining a path toward fine‑tuning on biological images.
> 
> Together, these works mark a consistent trend: practical scaling (memory, representation, and biological constraints) is now guided by explicit failure analyses and theory (zero‑point, spectral entropy, JEPA dynamics), while evaluation has broadened from accuracy to grounded reasoning and stability across real scientific tasks.

**naive 最终答案**

> ## Matching Papers
> 
> **(a) Sub-byte optimizer states for Adam/AdamW** — *4-bit Optimizers: Training Large Models with 4-bit Optimizer States* (NeurIPS 2023). Compresses Adam/AdamW first/second moments to 4-bit via smaller block sizes, rank-1 normalization, zero-point-excluding linear quantization, and factorization; matches 32-bit accuracy (lossless on fine-tuning, e.g., LLaMA-7B on one 80GB GPU, ~57.7% memory savings) across NLU/MT/vision/instruction tuning.
> 
> **(b) Implicit bias of joint-embedding self-distillation** — *Why JEPA Self-Distillation Avoids Noisy Features: A Deep Linear Network Analysis* (NeurIPS 2024). Shows JEPA self-distillation implicitly prioritizes high-influence ("predictive," low-variance) features over noisy ones via critical-time analysis of deep linear networks, with depth strengthening noise suppression; validated on ImageNet-1K (I-JEPA aligns faster with the perceptual low-variance PCA subspace than MAE).
> 
> **(c) Dale's-principle-constrained networks with spectral analysis** — *Learning better with Dale's Law: A Spectral Perspective* (NeurIPS 2023). Compares ColEI vs. DANN RNNs respecting excitatory/inhibitory sign constraints; shows learning stability is governed more by the initial singular-value spectrum (multimodal/dispersed for ColEI) than by sign constraints, proposing normalized SVD entropy (NSE) as a pre-training diagnostic of learning stability.
> 
> **(d) One-stage anchor-free part–whole association** — *PBADet: A One-Stage Anchor-Free Approach for Part-Body Association* (ICLR 2024). Extends anchor-free detection (YOLOv5/7 heads) with a single part-to-body center offset; handles multiple parts per body without degrading detection, evaluated on COCO-HumanParts (AP/AP.5/AP.75/AP S,M,L), COCO val, BodyHands, CrowdHuman (COCO-style metrics), outperforming BPJDet and ED-Pose.
> 
> **(e) Benchmark for VLMs on biological trait discovery** — *VLM4Bio* (NeurIPS 2024, Datasets & Benchmarks). ~469K QA pairs over Fish/Bird/Butterfly-10K covering species classification, trait identification, trait grounding, trait referring, and trait counting, plus reasoning/hallucination tests (FCT, NOTA), zero-shot evaluation of 12 pretrained VLMs, and comparison with the biologically fine-tuned BioCLIP. **Caveat:** the paper's reported metrics are micro-averaged accuracy (plus agreement scores); I did not find F1/Precision/AUROC interpretability metrics for biological trait discovery in the collection.
> 
> ## Development Trend of the Methods
> 
> 1. **From full precision to extreme compression (efficiency):** optimizer states went 32→8→4-bit with increasingly adaptive quantization (rank-1 normalization, zero-point exclusion, factorization), enabling larger models in fixed memory while keeping accuracy; fine-tuning (LLaMA/Alpaca, instruction tuning) became the key evaluation regime.
> 2. **From empirical tricks to mechanistic/theoretical understanding:** rather than just reporting gains, the works analyze *why* methods work — the JEPA paper derives critical-time/implicit-bias dynamics for feature ordering, and the Dale's Law paper replaces the "sign constraints hurt learning" assumption with a spectral (singular-value/NSE) explanation of learning stability, using spectral transplants as causal evidence.
> 3. **From complex pipelines to simpler, constraint-driven designs:** PBADet collapses multi-stage/anchor-based part-body pipelines into one-stage anchor-free detection with a single universal part-to-body offset; similarly, E/I networks are (re)designed so their spectra match unconstrained networks rather than merely adding sign constraints.
> 4. **From general-domain training to evaluation of pretrained/foundation models on fine-grained, domain-specific tasks:** VLM4Bio shifts focus to zero-shot assessment of pretrained VLMs on fine-grained biological traits, with prompting (CoT, dense captions) and hallucination tests, and shows fine-tuning (BioCLIP) still yields large gains — echoing the fine-tuning emphasis in the optimizer and detection works.
> 5. **Common thread:** all five works pair methodological innovation with rigorous practical evaluation on standard benchmarks (GLUE/ImageNet/COCO/Alpaca/COCO-HumanParts) and treat fine-tuning, stability, and measurable diagnostics (NSE, CCA, AP, accuracy, memory savings) as first-class concerns.

> **(a)** "4-bit Optimizers: Training Large Models with 4-bit Optimizer States" (NeurIPS 2023) — compresses Adam/AdamW first/second moments to 4-bit via smaller blocks, zero-point-excluding linear/rank-1 quantization and optional factorization; matches 32-bit accuracy on NLU, MT, image classification and LLaMA instruction tuning while cutting memory up to ~57.7%.
> 
> **(b)** "Why JEPA Self-Distillation Avoids Noisy Features: A Deep Linear Network Analysis" (NeurIPS 2024) — shows JEPA/self-distillation has an implicit bias toward high-influence (predictive, low-variance) features, with depth strengthening noise suppression versus MAE; validated on ImageNet with CCA alignment to perceptual PCA subspaces.
> 
> **(c)** "Why Dale's Law Constrained Recurrent Neural Networks Learn Poorly" (NeurIPS 2023) — recurrent networks respecting Dale's principle (excitatory/inhibitory, ColEI vs DANN); spectral (singular-value) analysis shows initial weight spectrum, not sign constraints, drives learning stability; normalised SVD entropy predicts performance.
> 
> **(d)** PBADet (ICLR 2024) — one-stage, anchor-free part-body association using a single part-to-body center offset on YOLOv5/v7 anchor-free heads; evaluated with AP/conditional accuracy/joint AP on COCO-HumanParts, BodyHands, CrowdHuman.

Caveat: its reported metric is micro-averaged accuracy, not F1/Precision/AUROC, so that specific part of the request is not established in the context.
> 
> **Development trend:** Across these works the field moves (1) from 32-bit/8-bit optimizer states to sub-byte (4-bit) compression with theoretical convergence support, explicitly evaluated on fine-tuning; (2) from empirical SSL observations to mechanistic analyses of implicit bias (deep linear dynamics, feature prioritization); (3) from sign-constraint explanations to spectral/dynamical explanations of biological constraints, using spectral diagnostics to guide architecture design; (4) from multi-stage, anchor-based pipelines to simplified one-stage anchor-free formulations that scale to many parts; and (5) from task-specific supervised evaluation to large zero-shot benchmarks probing fine-grained, interpretable capabilities (grounding, counting, reasoning, hallucination) of pretrained vision-language transformers, including comparisons with fine-tuned domain models. Overall: more theory-driven design, more efficiency, and more interpretability-oriented practical evaluation.

**问题：** I’m building a biodiversity pipeline on limited GPUs: a Transformer‑based system that must classify species from museum photos, ground and count traits (e.g., fins, beaks), and robustly reason about them—while keeping training memory low during fine‑tuning (possibly with parameter‑efficient updates). What papers cover these pieces end‑to‑end?Please summarize the development trend of their methods.
