**Gold（保持结果文件中的原始内容；部分条目本身为序列化字典字符串）**

Gold 1：

> Development trends across the five works (ICLR/NeurIPS 2023–2024) show a common shift away from “just scale the model” toward structure-aware objectives, spectra-/embedding-aware diagnostics, and hardware/efficiency–conscious training that together deliver robustness and practical scalability.
> 
> 1) Part–body association detection (PBADet, ICLR’24)
> - Method shift: from anchor-based, multi-stage pipelines (e.g., BPJDet) to one-stage, anchor-free detectors that add a single, part-to-body center-offset head on multi‑scale feature maps.
> - Scalability pattern: representation length becomes constant w.r.t. number of parts (2D center offset), so accuracy does not degrade as parts increase. Post‑processing is simplified (one-to-one decoding), and the method generalizes beyond humans (e.g., wheels–cars). 
> - Backbones/datasets/optimizers: implemented on YOLOv5/YOLOv7 with SGD and evaluated on COCO-HumanParts, BodyHands, CrowdHuman. Trend is toward compact association representations that scale across datasets without adding branches.
> 
> 2) EI‑constrained recurrent nets (Dale’s Law, NeurIPS’23)
> - Diagnosis moves from sign constraints to spectra: performance gaps are explained better by singular‑value spectra than by Dale sign constraints. Normalized SVD entropy (NSE) becomes a predictive, interpretable metric for learning success.
> - Scaling pattern: larger networks and more balanced E/I ratios increase NSE and reduce error; small nets with few inhibitory units suffer multi‑modal, dispersed spectra and poor learning. Spectral “transplant” experiments show spectrum > sign constraints for performance impact.
> - Training dynamics: closed‑form ODEs yield critical times that depend on depth and regression coefficients; gradient clipping helps ColEI stability. Overall trend: use spectrum‑aware initializations/architectures to make EI networks trainable and interpretable.
> 
> 3) Self‑supervision in latent space (JEPA, NeurIPS’24)
> - Objective shift: from pixel‑space reconstruction (MAE; MSE) to joint‑embedding prediction with cosine‑type matching. In deep linear analysis, JEPA implicitly prioritizes influential features (high regression coefficients) rather than high‑variance ones.
> - Depth trend: the bias toward influential/“slow” features strengthens with encoder depth; critical times show greedy, feature‑by‑feature learning that differs from MAE’s ordering. 
> - Practical implication: to get semantic, low‑variance features quickly, predict in latent space (JEPA) rather than reconstruct pixels (MAE); fine‑tuning or data design can leverage this bias.
> 
> 4) Memory‑efficient optimization (4‑bit states, NeurIPS’23)
> - Precision trend: optimizer state precision pushed from 8‑bit to 4‑bit by handling outliers and the zero‑point failure mode in the second moment. Rank‑1 normalization and linear (zero‑excluded) quantizers stabilize 4‑bit Adam/SGD.
> - Scalability/efficiency: factorizing the second moment where possible and quantizing the rest cuts total training memory (e.g., up to ~58% end‑to‑end savings in instruction tuning) while matching or closely tracking full‑precision performance across tasks (GLUE, SQuAD EM/F1, ImageNet classification with Swin‑T, WMT14 en‑de, GPT‑2 E2E‑NLG, and LLaMA instruction tuning). This enables training larger models per‑GPU (e.g., LLaMA‑7B on a single 80GB card) and reduces offload communication.
> - Cross‑method leverage: efficiency gains here directly support scaling of detectors, VLMs, and JEPA‑style pretraining under fixed memory budgets.
> 
> 5) Visual data‑type understanding in VLMs (ICLR’24)
> - Empirical finding: zero‑shot cosine‑similarity (C‑VLMs like CLIP) and log‑likelihood scoring (LMMs) reveal that current VLMs are good at semantics but fail at visual data‑type identification (rotations, noise, contrast) despite handling stylized types (cartoon, sketch) better. The largest LMMs underperform smaller contrastive models; scaling laws are weak.
> - Representation trend: CLIP image embeddings are clustered by semantics and remain largely invariant to data‑types; t‑SNE, KNN and linear probes confirm less separability for data‑types than for objects.
> - Data trend over scaling: performance correlates with the prevalence/alignment of data‑type cues in pretraining data; scaling alone does not fix it. Fine‑tuning with captions that include data‑type tokens (TeDaTy) and freezing the image encoder significantly improves in‑distribution ID and can help OOD generalization.
> - Generation tie‑in: synthetic benchmarks (SyntheticTypeIdent) were created with a diffusion model (guided prompting), reinforcing that modern generators facilitate controlled data‑type evaluation.
> 
> Cross‑cutting developments
> - From invariance to compositionality: JEPA emphasizes feature influence in latent space; PBADet models compositional part–body structure explicitly; VLM work shows that invariance learned during pretraining can hide data‑type information, so compositional data‑type labels in captions are needed to recover it.
> - From naïve scaling to structure‑ and data‑aware scaling: spectral metrics (NSE) predict EI‑RNN trainability; VLMs require data‑type–rich pretraining/fine‑tuning rather than bigger LLMs; detectors prefer compact, universally applicable offsets; optimizers reduce precision safely by matching the true error geometry (rank‑1 normalization, zero‑excluded second moment).
> - Tooling for practical scale: 4‑bit optimizers and factorization unlock larger models per device; anchor‑free heads keep detection heads simple as parts grow; spectrum‑aware initializations reduce training instability.
> 
> What changes over time (2023→2024)
> - Detection: convergence on one‑stage, anchor‑free association with fixed‑size outputs to scale to many parts/datasets.
> - RNNs: shift from enforcing signs to designing spectra; NSE adopted as an interpretable early predictor of performance across EI ratios/sizes.
> - SSL: renewed focus on JEPA‑style latent prediction (cosine space) over pixel MSE for faster emergence of semantic, low‑variance features, especially at depth.
> - Optimization: precision lowered from 8‑bit to 4‑bit states without accuracy loss by fixing zero‑point issues and exploiting rank‑1 structure; combined with offloading/FSDP.
> - VLMs: recognition that “data‑type understanding” does not emerge from scale; zero‑shot cosine scoring exposes the gap; targeted fine‑tuning with data‑type captions and freezing vision encoders is the effective remedy.
> 
> In short: across detection, recurrent modeling, self‑supervision, optimization, and VLM evaluation, the trend is away from brute‑force scale and toward objectives, spectra, embeddings, and quantization schemes that explicitly encode the structure of the problem (associations, spectra, latent prediction, state distributions, and data‑types) while using efficiency techniques to make those choices practical at scale.

**naive 最终答案**

> Based on the available documents, here are the papers matching each requirement, followed by the development trend.
> 
> **Papers found**
> 
> **(a) Anchor-free one-stage part–body association (COCO-style):** PBADet (ICLR 2024) — one-stage, anchor-free part-body association via a single part-to-body center offset on COCO-HumanParts, COCO-WholeBody, CrowdHuman, BodyHands, using YOLOv5/YOLOv7 backbones with task-alignment (TOOD) learning. Note: it is anchor-free and COCO-based, but its backbone is CNN (YOLO), not a transformer; transformer-based detectors (DETR-family, ED-Pose with Swin-L) appear only as competitors.
> 
> **(b) Spectral behavior of Dale's-law RNNs:** "Learning better with Dale's Law: A Spectral Perspective" (NeurIPS 2023) — compares standard RNNs, sign-constrained ColEI and DANN recurrent networks; shows initial singular-value spectrum (multimodal/dispersed for ColEI) matters more than sign constraints; proposes normalized SVD entropy (NSE) as a spectrum-pathology measure anti-correlating with final test error; worse for small networks/fewer inhibitory units. I could not find explicit evidence for the "near-linear-in-D training-time" insight in the retrieved context.
> 
> **(c) JEPA self-distillation:** "How JEPA Avoids Noisy Features" (NeurIPS 2024) — analyzes JEPA self-distillation vs pixel-space MAE with deep linear networks; derives critical times showing JEPA's implicit bias toward high-influence features (large regression coefficients), prioritizing low-variance/"slow" perceptual features, validated by I-JEPA vs MAE ImageNet CCA experiments. The simplified JEPA objective uses L2 latent matching; cosine-based matching is characteristic of the JEPA family (BYOL/I-JEPA/V-JEPA) it generalizes. Fine-tuning aspects appear via linear-probing evaluation and, in related work, LDReg (local intrinsic dimensionality regularization improving SimCLR/BYOL/MAE) and CLIP-style fine-tuning.
> 
> **(d) 4-bit optimizer states:** "Memory Efficient Optimizers with 4-bit States" (NeurIPS 2023) — quantizes Adam/AdamW (and SGDM) first/second moments to 4-bit using smaller blocks (B128), zero-point-excluding linear quantizer and rank-1 normalization, optionally factorized second moment; preserves accuracy/F1 on GLUE, SQuAD, ImageNet (Swin-T), WMT and LLaMA fine-tuning with up to 57.7% memory savings. Note: the exact CIFAR/MNIST/COCO-scale evaluation with cross-entropy/F1/Precision is not in this paper's evidence; CIFAR/MNIST appear in other works (e.g., Hessian power-law analysis with SGD/Adam, MLMC compression on CIFAR-10) without 4-bit states.
> 
> **(e) Visual data-type understanding:** "Visual Data-Type Understanding Does Not Emerge from Scaling Vision-Language Models" (ICLR 2024) — introduces Visual Data-Type Identification; benchmarks 39 transformer-based VLMs (100M–80B) zero-shot using cosine-similarity scoring of image/text embeddings (log-likelihood for LMMs); shows scaling gives marginal gains and weak power laws (would need >10¹² params for strong performance); a diffusion model is used to generate style/semantic data-type images; fine-tuning with data-type-aware captions (TeDaTy) improves ID and OOD generalization.
> 
> **Development trend of the methods**
> 
> Across these five lines, the trend is: **(1) simplifying pipelines** — from two-stage/anchor-based systems to one-stage anchor-free formulations where association is folded into a single offset (PBADet); **(2) explaining rather than only training** — methods increasingly use spectral/initialization analysis (NSE for Dale's-law RNNs; power-law Hessian spectra across SGD/Adam optimizers) and exact deep-linear dynamics (JEPA critical times) to explain why architectures learn well or poorly; **(3) moving supervision from pixel space to latent/embedding space** — JEPA-style predictive distillation replaces pixel MSE with representation matching, biasing learning toward influential, low-variance features; **(4) compressing training itself** — optimizer state bit-width is pushed 8-bit → 4-bit (with smarter quantization/factorization) to retain full-precision accuracy at lower memory; and **(5) questioning brute-force scaling** — for vision–language data-type understanding, zero-shot cosine scoring shows scaling alone fails, shifting emphasis to data distribution, fine-tuning with targeted mixtures, and compositional understanding rather than model size.

**community 最终答案**

> ## Papers identified per topic
> 
> **(a) Anchor-free one-stage part–body association (COCO-style):** *PBADet* (ICLR 2024, doc `08b70bc3…`). It extends anchor-free detection (FCOS/TOOD) with a single part-to-body center offset, evaluated on COCO-WholeBody/COCO-HumanParts, CrowdHuman, BodyHands. **Partial match:** its backbones are YOLOv5/YOLOv7 (CNN); transformer backbones (DETR, Deformable-DETR, ED-Pose with Swin-L) appear only as comparison baselines, not as its own backbone.
> 
> **(b) Dale's-Law RNNs, spectral behavior, NSE:** *Learning better with Dale's Law: A Spectral Perspective* (NeurIPS 2023, doc `e63a94c4…`). It shows initial singular-value spectra (not sign constraints) dominate learning, uses normalised SVD entropy (NSE) as a predictive diagnostic, and trains via projected gradient descent with gradient clipping. Relatedly, *Investigating the Overlooked Hessian Structure* (doc `582d138d…`) studies spectra under SGD and Adam (incl. CIFAR/MNIST). **Partial match:** the "near-linear-in-D training time" insight was not found in the retrieved content.
> 
> **(c) JEPA-style SSL, implicit bias, fine-tuning:** *How JEPA Avoids Noisy Features* (NeurIPS 2024, doc `40fde037…`). It contrasts JEPA self-distillation with MAE pixel reconstruction, proving JEPA's implicit bias toward "influential features" (high regression coefficients / low-variance perceptual subspace), verified with I-JEPA on ImageNet via CCA. **Partial match:** the toy objective is L2 latent MSE rather than cosine; cosine-based matching appears in the contrastive-analysis paper (doc `160e1407…`) and in CLIP fine-tuning details in the data-type paper.
> 
> **(d) 4-bit optimizer states:** *Memory Efficient Optimizers with 4-bit States* (NeurIPS 2023, doc `8d5e1455…`). 4-bit Adam/AdamW (smaller blocks, rank-1 normalization, zero-point-excluded linear quantizer, factorization) matches 32-bit accuracy on GLUE (incl. QA F1), SQuAD, ImageNet (Swin-T), E2E-NLG, WMT, LLaMA fine-tuning. **Partial match:** it is AdamW-focused (the framework supports SGD but experiments don't show 4-bit SGD), and CIFAR/MNIST/COCO results with 4-bit states are not in this collection (those appear in the Hessian paper with full precision).
> 
> **(e) Visual data-type understanding in VLMs:** *Visual Data-Type Understanding Does Not Emerge from Scaling Vision-Language Models* (ICLR 2024, doc `b0d9a0b2…`). It introduces Visual Data-Type Identification, benchmarks 39 VLMs (100M–80B) **zero-shot by cosine similarity** between image and data-type text embeddings, shows scaling gives marginal gains and large LMMs underperform smaller contrastive CLIP models, ties performance to data-type scarcity in LAION-2B (abundancy correlation r≈0.80), and improves performance by fine-tuning with TeDaTy. The **diffusion-guided pipeline** is the use of Kandinsky 2.1 to synthesize style/semantic data-type images.
> 
> ## Development trend of the methods
> 
> - **Detection (a):** moving from multi-stage, anchor-based, heuristic/learned association (DA-RNN, JointDet, HierR-CNN, BPJDet) toward **one-stage, anchor-free, end-to-end** designs — a single part-to-body center offset replaces per-part body-to-part offsets, with task-alignment learning; transformer (DETR) detectors are the comparison frontier, and the anchor-free version beats the anchor-based version of the same backbone.
> - **Recurrent spectral analysis (b):** from blaming sign constraints to showing **initialization spectra matter more**, using NSE to predict performance before training, and extending spectral diagnostics (power-law Hessian spectra) as generalization predictors across both SGD and adaptive-momentum optimizers.
> - **SSL (c):** from pixel-space reconstruction (MAE) to **latent-space predictive distillation (JEPA)**, with theory (deep linear networks) explaining the implicit bias toward influential/low-variance features and faster semantic-feature learning; evaluation shifts to linear probing/CCA and downstream fine-tuning.
> - **Optimization (d):** from 32-bit to 8-bit to **4-bit optimizer states**, via empirically designed quantization (smaller block sizes, rank-1 normalization, zero-point exclusion, factorization) that preserves accuracy/F1 while cutting memory (e.g., LLaMA-7B on one 80GB GPU, ~57.7% savings).
> - **VLMs (e):** from assuming robustness emerges from scaling to showing **data-type understanding does not emerge from scaling**; zero-shot cosine scoring is the standard probe, and the fix is systematic training-data change (data-type-rich captions, fine-tuning on TeDaTy) plus diffusion-generated data-type imagery rather than larger models.
> 
> Overall, the trend is: **simpler unified architectures (anchor-free/one-stage, latent-space prediction) + spectral/init-level understanding of learning dynamics + aggressive precision reduction for efficiency + recognition that scaling alone fails without targeted data/objective design.**

Gold 1：

> {'answer': '- Detector design (part–body association in COCO-like scenes): Methods have moved from multi-stage, anchor-based pipelines to one-stage, anchor-free detectors. PBADet (ICLR 2024) replaces body-to-part multipliers with a single part-to-body center offset learned on multi-scale feature maps with task-aligned learning (TOOD) and standard SGD. This reduces representation length, simplifies decoding, and scales to many parts without expanding output heads. The trend is toward compact, anchor-free joint detection that preserves AP while keeping association robust across datasets (BodyHands, COCO-HumanParts, CrowdHuman).\n- Spectral diagnostics for EI-constrained RNNs (stability for control loops): Earlier practice blamed sign constraints (Dale’s Law) for poor learning; recent work (NeurIPS 2023) shows the dominant factor is the singular-value spectrum of the recurrent weights. Performance correlates with a unimodal, clustered spectrum (quantified by Normalised SVD Entropy), not with relaxing EI signs. Over time and scale, larger networks and more balanced E/I ratios improve spectra and learning; gradient clipping helps. The design trend is to enforce/diagnose favorable spectra at initialization (or via architecture like recurrent DANNs) rather than abandon EI constraints, yielding more stable RNNs on sequential tasks (adding problem, sequential MNIST, PTB).\n- Low‑memory training (4‑bit optimizer states for Adam/SGD without hurting CE/F1/Precision): Optimizer compression has progressed from 8‑bit to 4‑bit states. The latest 4‑bit methods (NeurIPS 2023) address (i) heterogeneous outliers via smaller block sizes and rank‑1 normalization that uses both row/column maxima, and (ii) the “zero‑point” issue for the second moment by excluding zero with a linear mapping, sometimes combined with factorization of v. These yield accuracy comparable to full precision across classification (e.g., Swin‑T on ImageNet), NLU/QA (e.g., RoBERTa‑L with CE/F1), MT (Transformer on WMT14), and instruction tuning (LLaMA), while cutting optimizer memory and improving offloaded throughput. The trend is a hybrid of quantization+factorization, making optimizer state the new lever for scaling under fixed memory.\n- Self‑supervised representation learning (avoiding noisy pixel features): Analyses of deep linear self‑distillation JEPAs (NeurIPS 2024) find an implicit bias toward “influential” features (high regression coefficients), whereas reconstruction (MAE) emphasizes high‑variance, often noisy directions. Depth amplifies this JEPA bias and drives step‑wise, greedy learning of predictive features. The community trend is shifting from reconstruction toward JEPA‑style non‑contrastive, stop‑grad self‑distillation (e.g., I‑/V‑JEPA), to learn abstract embeddings that de‑emphasize unpredictable pixel details.\n- Visual data‑type identification at runtime (snow, blur, rotation) with transformer VLMs: Systematic evaluations (ICLR 2024) show that zero‑shot cosine‑similarity with contrastive VLMs (e.g., CLIP) works better than auto‑regressive LMMs, but overall data‑type recognition remains weak and does not improve much with model scaling (100M→80B). Pretraining distributions explain per‑type performance differences; training‑free adapters and in‑context learning underperform. Adding explicit data‑type supervision during fine‑tuning (e.g., TeDaTy mixes) significantly boosts in‑distribution performance and can improve OOD. The practical trend is: (1) use CLIP‑style cosine matching for zero‑shot filtering; (2) fine‑tune with data‑type‑labeled mixtures for reliability if the application demands precise filtering.\nOverall trajectory across components:\n- From heavy, inflexible heads to compact, anchor‑free joint detectors for scalable association (PBADet).\n- From “sign‑constraints are the problem” to spectrum‑first diagnostics for EI RNN stability; introduce spectral metrics (NSE) and initialization/ratio/size design rules.\n- From 8‑bit to robust 4‑bit optimizer states by fixing quantization pathologies (zero‑point, outliers) and mixing with factorization—maintaining CE/F1/Precision across vision and language tasks while enabling larger models under the same memory.\n- From reconstruction‑heavy SSL to JEPA‑style self‑distillation that preferentially learns predictive, low‑noise features; depth is used intentionally to steer feature priority.\n- From the assumption that VLM scaling suffices to identify data‑types to targeted fine‑tuning with data‑type‑aware corpora; contrastive encoders plus cosine similarity remain strong baselines; explicit fine‑tuning is often required for dependable visual data‑type filtering.'}

**naive 最终答案**

> Here are the matching works and the development trend of each method line:
> 
> **1. Detector design (anchor-free part-body association)**
> - **PBADet: A One-Stage Anchor-Free Approach for Part-Body Association** (ICLR 2024, doc `08b70bc3…`). It links hands/face/feet to bodies via a single part-to-body center offset on multi-scale anchor-free feature maps, with task-alignment learning; evaluated on COCO-HumanParts, BodyHands, CrowdHuman.
> - **Trend:** Earlier methods were multi-stage or anchor-based (DA-RNN double-anchor RPN, JointDet head-body discrimination, BFJDet embedding matching, HierR-CNN two-branch, Detector-in-Detector, and BPJDet's body-to-part center offsets integrated into anchor-based YOLO, whose representation grows with the number of parts). The trend moved toward simplification: one-stage, dense per-pixel anchor-free prediction with a single concise part-to-body offset, which is more efficient, more robust to occlusion, and scales to many parts.
> 
> **2. Spectral diagnostics for EI-constrained RNNs**
> - **"Learning better with Dale's Law: A Spectral Perspective"** (NeurIPS 2023, doc `e63a94c4…`). It shows ColEI (column-constrained E/I) RNNs have multimodal, dispersed singular-value spectra with large max singular value even when eigenvalue radius is fixed, whereas standard RNNs and recurrent Dale's ANNs match the Marchenko–Pastur quarter-circle. It proposes **normalized SVD entropy (NSE)** as a pre-training diagnostic that anti-correlates with final error.
> - **Trend:** The explanation shifted from "sign constraints hurt E/I networks" to "initialization spectral properties matter more than sign constraints"; diagnostics evolved from eigenvalue-radius checks to whole-spectrum measures (NSE) that predict learning performance before training, guiding better EI architecture/initialization design.
> 
> **3. Low-bit (4-bit) optimizer states**
> - **"Memory Efficient Optimizers with 4-bit States"** (NeurIPS 2023, doc `8d5e1455…`). It quantizes Adam/AdamW states to 4-bit (smaller B128 blocks for the first moment; zero-point-excluding linear quantizer and rank-1 normalization for the second moment; optionally factorized second moment). It matches 32-bit accuracy on GLUE, SQuAD (F1), ImageNet, E2E-NLG, MT, and LLaMA fine-tuning, with up to ~57.7% memory savings; SGD(M) also covered by the compression framework and convergence proof.
> - **Trend:** Optimizer-state precision went 32-bit → 8-bit block-wise quantization → 4-bit, enabled by increasingly fine-grained quantization/normalization (row-wise + column-wise rank-1 normalization) and handling of the second-moment zero-point problem, achieving lossless convergence with growing memory savings.
> 
> **4. JEPA-style self-supervision avoiding noisy pixel features**
> - **"How JEPA Avoids Noisy Features: The Implicit Bias of Deep Linear Self Distillation Networks"** (doc `40fde037…`). It analyzes self-distillation JEPA (BYOL, SimSiam, data2vec, I-JEPA/V-JEPA) vs. MAE in deep linear networks, showing JEPA's implicit bias toward high-influence, low-variance ("slow") features, so it learns noisy pixel features slower/lower-amplitude than MAE.
> - **Trend:** SSL moved from reconstruction/contrastive paradigms toward non-contrastive self-distillation JEPA that predicts in latent space (with stop-gradient to avoid collapse); research then progressed from empirical observations to mechanistic/analytical understanding of the implicit bias, e.g., critical times, eigenspace alignment, and slow-feature prioritization (with related SSL work like LDReg addressing local dimensional collapse).
> 
> **5. Limits of scaled VLMs on visual data-type identification**
> - **"Visual Data-Type Understanding Does Not Emerge from Scaling Vision-Language Models"** (ICLR 2024, doc `b0d9a0b2…`). It introduces Visual Data-Type Identification (27 types: rotation, blur/noise, snow/brightness, cartoon, etc.) and zero-shot benchmarks 39 VLMs (100M–80B) using cosine similarity of image/text embeddings. Scaling yields marginal gains for contrastive CLIP and the largest autoregressive VLMs (OpenFlamingo) drop sharply; few-shot training-free adaptation doesn't help; fine-tuning with data-type-rich data (TeDaTy) significantly improves ID and OOD performance.
> - **Trend:** The assumption that VLM scaling/robustness implies compositional data-type understanding was tested and falsified; the field is moving from "scale-up" to explicit data-type-aware fine-tuning and analysis of pre-training data scarcity (LAION-2B) and vision-embedding invariance, since data-type identification does not emerge from scaling alone.
> 
> **Overall trend:** across all five lines, methods evolve from complex, multi-stage/heuristic or brute-force (scale/precision/anchor-based) designs toward simpler, more efficient, and analytically grounded approaches: one-stage anchor-free association, spectral diagnostics replacing sign-constraint hypotheses, fine-grained 4-bit quantization with proven lossless convergence, theoretically explained latent-space self-distillation, and explicit data-centric fine-tuning instead of relying on scaling for data-type perception.

**community 最终答案**

> Here are the matching works from the collection, each with the development trend of its methods:
> 
> **1. Detector design — "PBADet: A One-Stage Anchor-Free Approach for Part-Body Association" (ICLR 2024)**
> - One-stage, anchor-free detector that links hands/face/feet to their parent body via a single *part-to-body center offset*, built on multi-scale anchor-free feature maps with classification/localization/association branches (YOLOv5/YOLOv7 backbones), evaluated on COCO-HumanParts, BodyHands, CrowdHuman.
> - *Trend*: two-stage heuristic/anchor-based pipelines (DA-RNN, JointDet, BFJDet, HierR-CNN, BodyHands, Detector-in-Detector) → one-stage anchor-based with costly body-to-part offsets (BPJDet) → one-stage anchor-free with a compact single offset (PBADet), gaining multi-part scalability, shorter representations, and higher Precision/Recall/F1 for hands/feet (e.g., 48.52 vs 31.51 F1 vs ED-Pose), with task-alignment learning and association loss as key components.
> 
> **2. Spectral diagnostics — "Learning better with Dale's Law: A Spectral Perspective" (NeurIPS 2023)**
> - Shows stability/learnability of E/I-constrained RNNs depends on the *singular-value spectrum* at initialization more than sign constraints; proposes **Normalised SVD Entropy (NSE)** as a pre-training diagnostic (higher NSE ⇒ lower test error), and shows recurrent DANNs learn as well as standard RNNs while naive ColEI networks have pathological multimodal spectra.
> - *Trend*: from attributing EI-RNN failure to sign constraints → spectral analysis (spectrum transplant experiments, random-matrix theory) → a spectrum-based diagnostic metric (NSE) guiding architecture/initialization design.
> 
> **3. Low-bit optimizers — "4-bit Optimizers: Training Large Models with 4-bit Optimizer States" (NeurIPS 2023)**
> - Compresses Adam/AdamW optimizer states to 4 bits: smaller block size (B128) for the first moment, rank-1 normalization + zero-point-excluding linear quantizer for the second moment, optionally factorized second moment; matches or exceeds 32-bit AdamW on GLUE, SQuAD, ImageNet, E2E-NLG, MT, and LLaMA Alpaca fine-tuning, saving up to ~57.7% memory (LLaMA-7B on one 80GB GPU).
> - *Trend*: 32-bit stateful optimizers → 16-bit (DALL-E) → 8-bit block-wise quantization (Dettmers) → 4-bit with finer-grained (smaller block, rank-1, zero-point-exclusion) quantization and hybridization with factorization (Adafactor-style) for lossless convergence at 4 bits.
> 
> **4. JEPA-style self-supervision — "How JEPA Avoids Noisy Features: The Implicit Bias of Deep Linear Self Distillation Networks" (NeurIPS 2024)**
> - Analyzes why JEPA self-distillation (BYOL/data2vec/SimSiam/I-JEPA/V-JEPA style latent-space prediction) suppresses noisy pixel features vs MAE pixel reconstruction: deep linear analysis shows JEPA prioritizes high-influence ("slow", low-variance) features with derived critical times and depth-strengthened noise suppression; ImageNet confirms I-JEPA aligns faster with the low-variance perceptual subspace.
> - *Trend*: from pixel-reconstruction MAE (which learns variance-dominating, often uninformative features) → JEPA latent predictive objectives → theoretical characterization of JEPA's implicit bias (why latent prediction avoids noisy features), complementing practical SSL improvements like LDReg (local-dimensionality regularization against dimensional collapse).
> 
> **5. VLMs on data-type identification — "Visual Data-Type Understanding Does Not Emerge From Scaling Vision-Language Models" (ICLR 2024)**
> - Introduces Visual Data-Type Identification with SyntheticTypeIdent (27 types) and NaturalTypeIdent datasets; zero-shot evaluation of 39 VLMs (100M–80B) shows contrastive VLMs (CLIP-style, cosine-based zero-shot matching) beat much larger auto-regressive LMMs; scaling gives marginal gains; style/semantic types are easier than geometric/pixel types (rotation, snow, blur, noise); data-type signal is scarce in LAION-2B and its abundance correlates (r≈0.80) with performance; fine-tuning with the TeDaTy subset (8 types, captions embedding data-type info) improves identification and OOD generalization.
> - *Trend*: zero-shot cosine matching of CLIP-style contrastive VLMs is the baseline → showing that scaling alone fails and data-type understanding must be injected via fine-tuning with data-type-aware captions (a "systematic change of training data" rather than model size).
> 
> **Overall trend**: in every area, the progression is from heavier, multi-stage/anchor-based or higher-precision approaches toward more streamlined, resource-efficient designs — anchor-free one-stage detection with compact association representations; spectral-diagnostic-guided initialization instead of ad-hoc constraints; 4-bit quantized/factorized optimizer states; latent-space (JEPA) objectives over pixel reconstruction; and explicit fine-tuning/curation of data-type knowledge rather than reliance on scaling.

**Gold（保持结果文件中的原始内容；部分条目本身为序列化字典字符串）**

Gold 1：

> Across the five works, recent methods show converging trends toward training efficiency and stability, spectrum-aware learning dynamics, prompt-informed continued pretraining, and streamlined detection pipelines with practical metrics.
> 
> 1) Memory-efficient training at lower precision
> - Trend: Optimizer state compression is moving from 8-bit to 4-bit while maintaining accuracy and stability across vision and NLP tasks. This is achieved by task-aware quantization schemes that explicitly handle moment outliers and zero-point issues.
> - Evidence and characteristics: 4-bit optimizers introduce smaller block sizes, rank-1 normalization, and zero-excluding mappings (DE-0 or linear) for second moments, often combined with factorization of higher-dimensional states. They retain performance on NLU, QA, MT, and ImageNet-classification (Swin-T) and yield reliable F1/Macro-F1 and Accuracy, while reducing total training memory and speeding up sharded/offloaded pipelines.
> - Scalability: Applicable to a wide range of Transformer backbones (RoBERTa, LLaMA) and CNN-based detectors, and compatible with optimizer offloading/fusing; provides a clear path for near-term scaling without sacrificing CE-driven training reliability.
> 
> 2) Spectrum-aware EI constraints and stability
> - Trend: In recurrent deep networks that obey Dale’s Law, performance depends more on the singular value spectrum than on sign constraints. Normalized SVD entropy (NSE) emerges as a predictive diagnostic: unimodal, clustered singular values correlate with better learning.
> - Evidence and characteristics: Networks with classic “column EI” constraints exhibit multimodal, dispersed spectra and instability (especially small networks or fewer inhibitory units), while DANN-style architectures and spectrum-transplant experiments show that shaping the spectrum (not just enforcing signs) improves learning. NSE anti-correlates with test error across EI ratios and widths, offering a practical pre-training/initialization guide.
> - Field shift: Insights are argued to extend beyond RNNs to other deep architectures, encouraging spectrum-focused initialization/diagnostics for stable training in modern models.
> 
> 3) Implicit bias in latent prediction vs reconstruction
> - Trend: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPA) in deep linear self-distillation exhibit an implicit bias toward high-influence features (large regression coefficients), while masked reconstruction (MAE) favors highly covarying features. This bias becomes stronger with deeper encoders and shapes stepwise, greedy learning dynamics.
> - Evidence and characteristics: Exact ODE analyses and critical-time results show depth-dependent prioritization (JEPA: ρ; MAE: λ), explaining why latent-space prediction tends to avoid unpredictable/noisy pixel-level components and accelerates learning of semantically predictive features.
> - Practical takeaway: For deep encoders and representation learning, latent prediction objectives can stabilize and focus training on influential features (complementary to spectrum-aware guidance).
> 
> 4) Prompt-based continued pretraining (PCP) over conventional TAPT
> - Trend: Continued pretraining is shifting from task-only text (TAPT) to prompt-informed, template-augmented corpora (PCP), consistently improving prompt-based fine-tuning across single-sentence and sentence-pair tasks.
> - Evidence and characteristics: PCP builds a corpus by inserting task templates and golden/pseudo labels (akin to selecting D^c subsets with matched labels) and performs MLM before prompt-based FT. It delivers consistent gains (often large, up to ~20% absolute) in both semi- and fully-supervised settings—even with only hundreds of unlabeled examples—while TAPT can be detrimental (especially for sentence pairs or prompt-based FT).
> - Field shift: PCP simplifies semi-supervised pipelines versus iterative self-training, reduces reliance on data augmentation, and scales across model sizes (RoBERTa-Base/Large). It also aligns with instruction-tuning trends while keeping unsupervised objectives during continued pretraining.
> 
> 5) One-stage, anchor-free part–body association detection
> - Trend: Detectors are moving from multi-stage, anchor-based association (and expanding representations per part) to one-stage, anchor-free designs that use a single part-to-body center offset across multi-scale feature maps.
> - Evidence and characteristics: PBADet reduces representation length and post-processing complexity, scales to multiple parts without performance collapse, and reports practical metrics (AP, MR-2) plus part-level Precision/Recall/F1 against pose baselines. Pipeline and representation diagrams clarify the design and decoding steps.
> - Scalability: The concise offset and anchor-free heads generalize across parts and datasets, and qualitative/quantitative results show robust association in crowded scenes and multi-part settings.
> 
> Overall development pattern
> - Efficiency: Aggressive memory reduction (4-bit + factorization) and anchor-free detection shorten pipelines without sacrificing CE/Macro-F1/Precision/Recall.
> - Stability and guidance: Spectrum-aware initialization/diagnostics (NSE) and latent-prediction bias (JEPA) now inform how features emerge and when training is robust.
> - Pretraining strategy: Prompt-informed continued pretraining (PCP) supersedes domain/task-only TAPT for prompt-based FT, with consistent gains using small unlabeled sets and pseudo-labeling.
> - Evaluation and communication: Works increasingly report F1/Precision (not just AP) and provide clear diagrams of pipelines and representations, easing adoption and scaling.

> 
> 1. **4-bit Optimizers** (NeurIPS 2023) – quantizes Adam/AdamW optimizer states to 4-bit (smaller B128 blocks, zero-point-excluding linear quantizer, rank-1 normalization, factorized second moment), matching full-precision accuracy on NLU/CLS/NLG/QA/MT and saving up to ~57.7% memory.
> 2. **Why JEPA Self-Distillation Avoids Noisy Features** (NeurIPS 2024) – deep-linear analysis of implicit bias: JEPA prioritizes "influential" (high regression-coefficient) features while MAE tracks high-variance features; the bias strengthens with depth; I-JEPA aligns faster with the perceptual PCA subspace than MAE.
> 3. **Learning better with Dale's Law: A Spectral Perspective** (NeurIPS 2023) – shows EI (ColEI) RNNs learn poorly not because of sign constraints but because of multimodal/dispersed singular-value spectra; recurrent DANN keeps unimodal spectra; normalized SVD entropy (NSE) at initialization anti-correlates with test error and predicts performance.
> 4. **Prompt-based Continued Pre-training (PCP)** (NeurIPS 2023) – conventional continued pre-training (TAPT) can hurt prompt-based FT; PCP integrates prompt templates + golden/pseudo labels into the unsupervised objective, boosting prompt-based FT (up to ~20% absolute) on RoBERTa with few hundred unlabelled examples; ablations show both templates and pseudo-labels are needed.
> 5. **PBADet** (ICLR 2024) – one-stage, anchor-free part–body association detector using a single part-to-body center offset (replacing BPJDet-style body-to-part offsets), with multi-scale features and task-alignment learning; reported with F1/Precision/conditional accuracy and joint AP, outperforming SOTA on BodyHands/COCOHumanParts/CrowdHuman.
> 
> **Development trend of the methods:**
> - **Efficiency through compression/simplification**: optimizer states go 8-bit → 4-bit via finer-grained quantization (rank-1 normalization, zero-point exclusion, factorization); detection moves from multi-stage/anchor-based pipelines to a one-stage anchor-free head with a single universal offset — both trade away complexity for memory/speed while preserving accuracy (F1/Precision reported, not just AP).
> - **From ad-hoc constraints to principled diagnostics**: in EI RNNs, emphasis shifts from sign constraints to spectral properties at initialization (NSE as a predictive tool); in SSL, focus shifts from reconstruction losses to joint-embedding prediction with a formally characterized implicit bias.
> - **Unification of training stages**: continued pretraining and instruction/prompt tuning are merged into one PCP objective (templates + pseudo-labels) to better align with downstream prompt-based FT, and the paper notes future extension toward PEFT (e.g., LoRA).
> - **Theory-guided practice**: analyses (deep-linear JEPA dynamics, singular-value spectra, Hessian/power-law structure, convergence rates) increasingly guide design choices rather than pure empiricism; bonus items include pipeline diagrams (PBADet Figure 2, PCP Figure 2) and complexity-oriented analyses (e.g., MLMC convergence/communication bounds).

**community 最终答案**

> Based on the collection, here are the matching papers and the development trend of their methods:
> 
> **The papers**
> 1. **4-bit Optimizers (NeurIPS 2023)** – Pushes optimizer-state quantization from 32-bit → 8-bit → 4-bit, using smaller block sizes (B128), rank-1 normalization, zero-point-excluding linear quantizers, and optional second-moment factorization. Matches or exceeds 32-bit AdamW on NLU (RoBERTa GLUE), QA (SQuAD F1), CLS (Swin-T ImageNet), NLG, MT, and LLaMA/Alpaca tuning, cutting memory up to 57.7%.
> 2. **"Why JEPA Avoids Noisy Features" (NeurIPS 2024)** – Analyzes implicit bias of joint-embedding predictive (JEPA/self-distillation) vs masked reconstruction (MAE) in deep linear networks: JEPA prioritizes high-influence (high regression coefficient) features and suppresses noise (strengthened by depth), whereas MAE tracks covariance; verified on ImageNet via CCA. (Related: LDReg counteracts local dimensional collapse in SSL/MAE.)
> 3. **"Learning better with Dale's Law: A Spectral Perspective" (NeurIPS 2023)** – Shows poor EI-constrained (Dale's Law) RNN training stems not from sign constraints but from the initialization spectrum: ColEI's rank-one-nilpotent column-mean structure yields multimodal, dispersed singular values vs the quarter-circle/Marchenko-Pastur forms of standard/DANN RNNs; proposes normalized SVD entropy (NSE) as a pathology diagnostic that anti-correlates with test error.
> 4. **PCP (NeurIPS 2023)** – Prompt-based Continued Pre-training: shows naive task-adaptive pre-training (TAPT) can hurt prompt-based FT, and instead pre-trains with task texts + prompt templates and golden/pseudo labels under MLM, boosting prompt-based FT (up to +20.1% abs.) with only hundreds of unlabeled examples; ablations show both templates and pseudo-labels are needed; PEFT/LoRA compatibility is listed as future work (the Hessian paper separately finds LoRA-only fine-tuning does not induce the power-law spectrum that full fine-tuning does).
> 5. **PBADet (ICLR 2024)** – One-stage, anchor-free part–body association detector: a single part-to-body center offset replaces multi-stage/anchor-based body-to-part offsets (BPJDet), giving one-to-one correspondence, scalability to many parts, and a pipeline figure; reported with practical metrics (Hand AP, conditional accuracy, joint AP, MR⁻², mMR⁻²) and substantially higher precision/recall/F1 than ED-Pose for hands/feet, plus AP on COCOHumanParts/CrowdHuman.
> 
> **Development trend**
> - **Optimizers:** 32-bit → 8-bit → 4-bit (with factorization), shifting from "does quantization preserve accuracy" to fine-grained quantization design (block size, rank-1, zero-point) enabling larger models within fixed memory.
> - **Self-supervised learning:** from pixel reconstruction (MAE) toward joint-embedding prediction (JEPA), with theory replacing folklore: explicit analyses of implicit bias, feature prioritization, and dimensional-collapse regularization.
> - **Biologically constrained RNNs:** from blaming sign constraints to diagnosing initialization spectra (NSE as a predictive diagnostic), guiding architecture design (DANN-style reparameterization) toward spectra resembling standard RNNs.
> - **Fine-tuning/pretraining:** from generic continued pretraining (TAPT) to instruction-style prompt-based continued pretraining with templates + pseudo-labels, and toward parameter-efficient methods (LoRA/PEFT) to make continued pretraining affordable for LLMs.
> - **Detection:** from multi-stage, anchor-based part–body pipelines to a single-stage anchor-free design with one association offset, emphasizing efficiency, scalability, and reporting F1/Precision-style metrics rather than AP alone.
> 
> **Caveats:** The corpus does not exactly match every detail in the query—the 4-bit optimizer paper uses Swin-T/ImageNet and RoBERTa/SQuAD (F1) rather than MNIST/CIFAR-100+ResNet-50 (those appear in the Hessian-spectrum paper); no paper uses the literal "D^c" pseudo-label subset notation; and LoRA appears only as related/future work and in the Hessian power-law analysis, not as part of PCP itself.

**问题：** I’m building a resource‑constrained pipeline that: (1) fine‑tunes Transformer models with attention for both vision and NLP; (2) runs real‑time part–body association (hands/face) in a multi‑person setting; and (3) updates text models via prompt templates and pseudo labels without heavy iterative loops. I need guidance on: compressing optimizer states to ~4‑bit while keeping CE/F1/Precision stable; avoiding noisy features in representation learning with a JEPA‑style approach; improving prompt‑based fine‑tuning via continued pretraining on task‑related text; and understanding spectral pitfalls when enforcing EI (Dale’s Law) in recurrent controllers. End‑to‑end LoRA fine‑tuning or an SFT backbone is preferred, and I’ll validate on small/standard datasets (e.g., MNIST/CIFAR‑100) before deployment. Can you point me to works that cover these needs together?Please summarize the development trend of their methods.

Gold 1：

> Across the five works (2023–2024), the common development trend is toward simpler, more scalable, and resource‑efficient training/inference pipelines, guided by theory and task structure:
> 
> 1) Detection and multi‑person association (PBADet, ICLR 2024)
> - Shift: From two‑stage, anchor‑based joint detection (e.g., Faster R‑CNN/YOLO+post‑matching) and body‑to‑part offsets (BPJDet) to a one‑stage, anchor‑free design with a single part‑to‑body center offset.
> - Scalability: Representation shrinks from 6+K+2K (body‑to‑part, K parts) to 5+K+2 (part‑to‑body), avoiding growth in offsets as K increases and enabling multi‑part and cross‑domain (e.g., quadruped animals) association without redesign.
> - Efficiency/robustness: Multi‑scale, task‑aligned learning simplifies decoding and improves accuracy; the single offset remains valid even with occlusions.
> 
> 2) EI (Dale’s Law) in recurrent controllers (NeurIPS 2023)
> - Shift: From naïve column E/I sign constraints (ColEI) that often learn poorly to EI architectures (recurrent DANNs) and initializations chosen for healthy spectral properties.
> - Theory‑guided criterion: Singular value spectra (unimodal, clustered) predict learnability better than sign constraints. Normalized SVD entropy correlates with accuracy; spectrum transplant experiments show spectrum > sign constraint in impact.
> - Design implications: Larger networks and balanced E/I ratios improve spectra and learning; small nets with few inhibitory units suffer (guidance for resource‑constrained RNN controllers that enforce EI).
> 
> 3) Self‑supervised representation learning (NeurIPS 2024)
> - Shift: From reconstruction (MAE) to joint‑embedding predictive architectures (JEPA) for feature learning.
> - Depth‑driven bias: In deep linear analysis, JEPA prioritizes high‑influence (high regression‑coefficient) features and avoids noisy ones; MAE prioritizes high covariance (often less predictive) features. The difference strengthens with encoder depth and holds in temporal models.
> - Practical takeaway: For semantically stable, predictive features (vision/time‑series), JEPA‑style training becomes preferable as models deepen.
> 
> 4) Optimizer state compression (NeurIPS 2023)
> - Shift: From 8‑bit to 4‑bit optimizer states with convergence parity across NLP and vision tasks.
> - Key enablers: Smaller blocks (B128) for first moment; addressing the second‑moment zero‑point problem (exclude zero via linear mapping) and using rank‑1 normalization (row/column scales) to handle heterogeneous outliers; hybrid factorization+quantization for further savings.
> - Impact/scale: Up to 57.7% total memory savings in practice; enables larger models (e.g., LLaMA‑7B on a single 80GB GPU) and better offload throughput, with stable CE/F1/Precision on standard benchmarks.
> 
> 5) Continued pretraining for prompt‑based FT (NeurIPS 2023)
> - Reassessment: Conventional TAPT (continued PT on raw task text) is not reliably helpful—often harmful on sentence‑pair tasks and unstable with prompt‑based FT.
> - Shift: Prompt‑based Continued Pretraining (PCP)—injecting task‑related text plus templates during MLM—consistently boosts prompt‑based FT (up to +20.1% absolute), even with only hundreds to ~1k unlabeled examples; benefits grow with model scale.
> - Process simplification: Outperforms or matches state‑of‑the‑art semi‑supervised methods without iterative pseudo‑label loops or heavy augmentation; remains effective across model sizes and datasets.
> 
> Overall trajectory (2023–2024)
> - Scalability and simplicity: One‑stage anchor‑free detection; single offset for many parts; 4‑bit optimizer states; prompt‑aware continued pretraining that avoids iterative complexity.
> - Theory‑guided robustness: Spectral criteria for EI‑constrained RNNs; JEPA’s depth‑induced bias toward predictive features; explicit handling of optimizer outliers/zero‑point.
> - Resource awareness: Methods are designed to retain accuracy on small/standard datasets (e.g., MNIST/CIFAR‑100; GLUE/SNLI/CoLA; ImageNet) while enabling larger models or real‑time operation.
> - Field pattern: Vision moves from anchor‑based to anchor‑free, association‑aware detection; representation learning moves from reconstruction to predictive JEPA; optimization moves from 8‑bit to 4‑bit with structure‑aware quantization; NLP adaptation moves from raw‑text continued PT to template‑aware PCP. These changes collectively favor end‑to‑end, efficient fine‑tuning backbones (compatible with LoRA/SFT) under tight memory/latency budgets.

**naive 最终答案**

> Here are the works that cover your needs, grouped by topic, followed by the development trend.
> 
> **1. 4-bit optimizer states (keeping CE/F1/Precision stable)**
> - **"4-bit Optimizers: Training Large Models with 4-bit Optimizer States" (NeurIPS 2023)** – pushes optimizer-state precision from 8-bit to 4-bit for Adam/AdamW. Uses smaller block size (B128) for the first moment and, for the second moment, a linear quantizer that excludes the zero point plus rank-1 normalization, optionally factorized. Evaluated on NLU (RoBERTa), image classification (Swin-T), QA (F1), MT, and instruction tuning (LLaMA-7B/13B/33B): accuracy, F1, and CE are comparable to 32-bit AdamW with ~43–58% memory savings.
> - Related: **"A Multilevel Monte Carlo Approach for Mitigating Compression Bias in Distributed Learning"** – reduces compression bias under heavy quantization (down to 2-bit), improving CIFAR-10/BERT fine-tuning efficiency.
> 
> **2. Avoiding noisy features in JEPA-style representation learning**
> - **"Why JEPA Self-Distillation Avoids Noisy Features" (NeurIPS 2024)** – proves with deep-linear dynamics that JEPA prioritizes "influential" features (high regression coefficient) and suppresses noisy, high-variance directions, with suppression increasing with depth; MAE instead learns noisy high-covariance features. Confirmed on ImageNet-1K with I-JEPA.
> - **"LDReg: Local Dimensionality Regularization for SSL" (ICLR 2024)** – counters (local) dimensional collapse via Fisher-Rao-based local intrinsic dimensionality regularization for BYOL, SimCLR, MAE, etc.
> 
> **3. Prompt-based fine-tuning via continued pretraining on task-related text**
> - **"Don't Stop Pretraining? Make Prompt-based Fine-tuning Powerful Learner" (PCP, NeurIPS 2023)** – shows conventional continued pretraining (TAPT) can hurt, especially for sentence-pair tasks and prompt-based FT. PCP presents task-related texts together with prompt templates and golden/pseudo labels under an unsupervised MLM objective; it consistently improves prompt-based FT (up to 20.1% absolute) with only hundreds of unlabeled examples and **no iterative loops**.
> - **"GOT-D: Optimizing Gradient-based Data Selection for Pre-fine-tuning LLMs" (ICLR 2024)** – selects unlabeled data via optimal transport to warm up (pre-fine-tune) the model before targeted fine-tuning, improving F1 under constrained budgets.
> 
> **4. Spectral pitfalls when enforcing EI (Dale's Law) in recurrent controllers**
> - **"Learning better with Dale's Law: A Spectral Perspective" (NeurIPS 2023)** – explains why column-constrained EI RNNs (ColEI) learn poorly: the column-mean rank-one nilpotent structure yields multimodal, dispersed singular value spectra (pathological), not the sign constraints per se. Recurrent Dale's ANNs (DANN), which keep unimodal spectra like standard RNNs, learn well. Normalized SVD entropy (NSE) at initialization predicts performance; gradient clipping mitigates ColEI instability.
> 
> **5. LoRA / SFT backbone and small-dataset validation (MNIST/CIFAR-100)**
> - **"Investigating the Overlooked Hessian Structure" (ICML 2025)** – on MNIST/CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 and LLMs, well-trained networks show power-law Hessian spectra; LoRA-only fine-tuning does not induce this structure the way full fine-tuning does, and Hessian-based measures predict generalization.
> - **"NFTS: Neural Fine-Tuning Search for Few-Shot Learning" (ICLR 2024)** – NAS over per-layer freeze/fine-tune and adapters for ViT/ResNet backbones in few-shot recognition (Meta-Dataset, Meta-Album).
> 
> **Development trend of the methods**
> - **Optimizer state compression:** 32-bit → 8-bit (block-wise dynamic exponent) → 4-bit via finer-grained quantization (smaller blocks, rank-1 normalization, zero-point-free linear mapping, factorized second moment) — the direction is "lossless accuracy at ever-lower bitwidth through better handling of moment outliers," and toward hybrid quantized+factorized states.
> - **Representation learning:** from input-space reconstruction (MAE) to latent-space prediction (JEPA/self-distillation); the trend is theoretical characterization of implicit bias (influential vs. noisy features) plus explicit regularization (LID-based) to prevent collapse and noisy directions.
> - **Prompt/continued pretraining:** from naive task-adaptive pretraining (TAPT) to prompt-aware continued pretraining (PCP) that fuses templates + (pseudo) labels into unsupervised objectives — moving toward simple, non-iterative, data-efficient adaptation — plus principled data selection (GOT-D) for pre-fine-tuning.
> - **EI recurrent controllers:** from simple sign-constrained ColEI (which fails) to spectral-aware reparameterizations (DANN) and spectral diagnostics (NSE) — the trend is designing E/I architectures by their singular-value spectra at initialization rather than by sign constraints alone.
> - **End-to-end fine-tuning:** from full fine-tuning toward parameter-efficient adaptation (LoRA, adapters, prompts) and NAS-searched adaptation strategies for few-shot regimes, with spectral (Hessian) analysis used to understand generalization differences between LoRA and full FT — validated on small/standard datasets (MNIST, CIFAR-10/100).
> 
> Note: the collection contains these works individually but none covers all five topics in a single paper; they form a coherent set for your pipeline.

**community 最终答案**

> Here are the works in this collection that map to your pipeline needs, followed by the development trend.
> 
> **Works that cover your needs**
> 1. **4-bit optimizer states** — "4-bit Optimizers: Training Large Models with 4-bit Optimizer States" (NeurIPS 2023): compresses Adam/AdamW first/second moments to 4-bit via small block size (B128), rank-1 normalization, and zero-point-excluded linear mapping; matches 32-bit accuracy on NLU (GLUE), QA (SQuAD F1), NLG (BLEU), image classification, and instruction tuning (LLaMA 7B/13B/33B on Alpaca/MMLU) — i.e., CE/F1/Precision stay stable.
> 2. **Real-time multi-person part–body association** — PBADet: one-stage anchor-free detector treating hands/face as parts linked to a parent body by a single part-to-body center offset (validated on BodyHands, COCOHumanParts, CrowdHuman face-body).
> 3. **Prompt templates + pseudo labels without iterative loops** — PCP (Prompt-based Continued Pre-training): continued pretraining on task-related texts with prompt templates and golden/pseudo labels via MLM, then prompt-based fine-tuning; explicitly eliminates iterative self-training and extra data augmentation.
> 4. **JEPA-style noise avoidance** — "Why JEPA Self-Distillation Avoids Noisy Features": deep linear analysis showing JEPA's implicit bias toward high-influence features, with depth strengthening suppression of noisy directions; related LDReg regularizes local dimensionality to prevent (local) collapse.
> 5. **Spectral pitfalls of Dale's Law (EI) recurrent controllers** — "Learning better with Dale's Law: A Spectral Perspective" (NeurIPS 2023): column-constrained EI (ColEI) RNNs get a multimodal, dispersed singular-value spectrum (rank-one nilpotent column-mean component); DANN reparameterization preserves a standard RNN-like spectrum; normalised SVD entropy (NSE) diagnoses pathology before training.
> 6. **LoRA / SFT backbone and small-dataset validation** — "Investigating the Overlooked Hessian Structure": power-law Hessian analysis on MNIST/Fashion-MNIST/CIFAR-10/100 (LeNet, ViT-B on CIFAR-100) and LoRA fine-tuning of LLMs, showing LoRA-only fine-tuning does not induce the power-law structure that full fine-tuning does.
> 
> **Development trend of these methods**
> - **Optimizer compression:** 8-bit block-wise quantization (Dettmers) → 4-bit states, with progressively finer handling of outliers (smaller blocks, rank-1 row/column normalization, zero-point exclusion) and hybridization with factorization (4-bit Factor) — moving from "lossy compression" toward lossless convergence with greater memory savings.
> - **Part–body association:** complex multi-stage body-to-part offsets (BPJDet, HierR-CNN) → simple one-stage anchor-free single part-to-body center offset that scales to multi-part and multi-person settings.
> - **Prompt-based adaptation:** naive continued pretraining (TAPT) → instruction-tuning-style continued pretraining (PCP) that injects templates + pseudo labels into the unsupervised objective, replacing iterative semi-supervised loops with a single cheap pretraining step.
> - **Representation learning:** reconstruction (MAE) and contrastive SSL → JEPA self-distillation, with theory moving from "what works" to implicit-bias analysis (noise suppression, depth effects), plus regularization (LDReg) targeting collapse at local scale.
> - **EI recurrent networks:** naive sign constraints (ColEI) → reparameterized DANN architectures that keep the spectrum healthy, shifting the design principle from sign constraints to spectral properties (NSE as a predictive diagnostic).
> - **Fine-tuning backbone:** full-parameter fine-tuning vs LoRA are increasingly analyzed spectrally (Hessian power-law), and LoRA is noted to behave differently from full fine-tuning, with small standard datasets (MNIST/CIFAR-100) used for validation.
> 
> Caveat: no single paper in the collection covers all six needs jointly; the set above covers each individually, and their shared thread is a move toward simpler, cheaper, and more principled (spectral/theoretical) methods.

> - Anchor-free part–body association (PBADet, ICLR 2024): Methods have shifted from anchor-based, multi-stage association (e.g., YOLO-style extensions and BPJDet) toward one-stage, anchor-free detectors that encode a single part-to-body center offset. This reduces representation length, cuts decoding complexity, and scales to many parts without expanding offsets, while keeping accuracy on COCO-derived datasets. Training has standardized on CNN backbones with common losses and optimizers (e.g., cross-entropy and SGD) and multi-scale features, yielding state-of-the-art AP/mMR and improved association quality. Over time, this reflects a move from anchor dependence and heuristic post-hoc matching to end-to-end anchor-free association that generalizes across datasets (COCOHumanParts, BodyHands, CrowdHuman).
> 
> - Spectral behavior in EI recurrent nets (NeurIPS 2023): The focus has shifted from enforcing Dale’s Law via naïve sign constraints (ColEI) to designing EI networks with favorable spectral properties (e.g., DANNs), as performance and stability correlate strongly with unimodal, clustered singular value spectra. Stability improves with gradient clipping and higher normalized SVD entropy, and learning degrades in small, inhibition-scarce settings. The trend emphasizes spectral diagnostics (NSE) over strict sign constraints, guiding choices of EI ratio, width, and initialization to reduce training instability under standard stochastic optimizers.
> 
> - JEPA’s implicit bias in deep linear self-distillation (NeurIPS 2024): Representation learning has shifted from masked reconstruction (MAE) to joint-embedding prediction (JEPA), which—especially with deeper encoders—greedily prioritizes high-influence (predictive, low-variance) features rather than merely high-covariance ones. This depth-driven bias explains quicker focus on semantically informative directions (e.g., sequential MNIST, Imagenet analyses) and complements non-contrastive self-supervised training dynamics that avoid collapse via stop-grad. Over time, JEPA objectives are preferred when the goal is informative latent features over pixel-level fidelity.
> 
> - Anytime-valid RCPS with active labeling (NeurIPS 2024): Risk-controlling prediction sets have progressed from one-shot batch calibration to sequential, anytime-valid guarantees using nonnegative martingales (e-processes). New active labeling policies operate under budgets, using predictors to reduce variance and optimize label usage online. This yields label-efficient, time-uniform safety guarantees suitable for gating model outputs (e.g., online vision or language pipelines), with regret analyses linking policy/predictor quality to test power over streams. The trend is toward operational safety that updates continually and respects resource constraints.
> 
> - Modular diffusion for decision making (CleanDiffuser, NeurIPS 2024 D&B): Practice has coalesced around modular libraries that decouple diffusion backbones (DDPM/DDIM/DPM-Solver/EDM/Rectified Flow), solvers, guided sampling (CG/CFG), and architectures (CNN/UNet/Transformers/MLP). Cross-solver sampling without retraining, masking/inpainting, noise/data prediction switching, and warm-starting reflect an emphasis on flexibility and scalability. Empirical analyses show: (1) fewer sampling steps (often ~5) can suffice; (2) SDE vs ODE solvers behave differently across tasks; (3) higher EMA rates stabilize training; and (4) diffusion policies generally outperform planners across RL/IL benchmarks. The field is moving from bespoke, tightly coupled implementations to standardized, configurable pipelines that ease evaluation and adaptation across tasks.
> 
> Overall, across detection, EI-RNN training, SSL representation learning, sequential risk control, and diffusion-based decision making, the trajectory is toward methods that are (a) simpler and more scalable (anchor-free offsets, modular pipelines), (b) stability-aware (spectral diagnostics, EMA, gradient clipping), (c) focused on informative features (JEPA over MAE), and (d) operationally safe in the wild (anytime-valid RCPS with active labeling), while leveraging widely used backbones and losses (CNNs, CE/SGD) and flexible diffusion components (Transformers/CNNs, guided sampling).

**naive 最终答案**

> ## Matched papers (one per topic)
> 
> **(a)** **PBADet: One-Stage Anchor-Free Part-Body Association** (ICLR 2024). One-stage anchor-free detector with CNN backbones (YOLOv5/v7/v8, adapted to anchor-free heads). Association is done with a single part-to-body center offset on multi-scale feature maps; losses are IoU + DFL + classification (TOOD/GFocal-style) + a dedicated association loss with task-alignment anchor assignment. Evaluated on COCO-HumanParts, BodyHands, CrowdHuman (also AnimalPose/AP-10K). Note: explicit SGD/Adam optimizer details are not in the retrieved content.
> 
> **(b)** **Why Dale's Law Constrained Recurrent Neural Networks Learn Poorly** (NeurIPS 2023). Studies E/I RNNs obeying Dale's Law: column-constrained (ColEI) nets have multimodal, dispersed singular-value spectra (from a rank-one nilpotent column-mean term), learn worse and with higher variance across seeds/initializations, and are highly unstable without gradient clipping; DANN recurrent nets match standard RNN spectra and learn as well. Normalized SVD entropy (NSE) at initialization anti-correlates with final error. Sign constraints matter less than spectral properties. Specific SGD/Adam comparisons for these RNNs are not in the retrieved content (training uses projected gradient descent).
> 
> **(c)** **How JEPA Avoids Noisy Features: The Implicit Bias of Deep Linear Self-Distillation Networks** (NeurIPS 2024). In deep linear settings, JEPA self-distillation is biased toward "influential" (high-regression-coefficient) features, suppressing noisy ones; the effect strengthens with encoder depth, and critical-time analysis shows feature ordering differences vs MAE. Experiments use ImageNet-1K with CCA (I-JEPA vs MAE). **Caveat:** the CIFAR-100/MNIST/SVHN and AUROC/F1/Precision specifics in your description are *not* covered by this paper or any document found here — those parts cannot be matched.
> 
> **(d)** **Active, Anytime-Valid Risk-Controlling Prediction Sets** (NeurIPS 2024). Extends RCPS (Bates et al.) to a sequential, anytime-valid setting via e-processes/testing-by-betting: risk control holds simultaneously at all time steps on adaptively collected data; active labeling policies with a label budget (IPW, lower-bounded query probabilities) and a predictor/control variate; log-optimal policy/predictor derivations with regret bounds on wealth growth. This directly supports safety gating of black-box outputs (e.g., ImageNet experiments, θ=0.1, α=0.05).
> 
> **(e)** **CleanDiffuser: An Easy-to-use Modularized Library for Diffusion Models in Decision Making** (NeurIPS 2024 D&B). Decoupled modules — diffusion models/solvers (DDPM, DDIM, DPM-Solver(++), EDM, RectifiedFlow), network architectures (MLPs, UNet1d/CNN variants, DiT1d and Transformer backbones), guided sampling (CG/CFG), masking, cross-solver/Diffusion-X sampling, warm-starting, noise/data-prediction switching — assembled into pipelines (~10 lines of code) covering planner, policy, and data-synthesizer roles; benchmarked on D4RL and IL environments. **Caveat:** LoRA/SFT fine-tuning, feature-embedding, SSL, and vision-language discussions are *not* part of CleanDiffuser (they appear in other documents, e.g., LoRA fine-tuning of Stable Diffusion in the RTB paper), so (e) is only partially matched.
> 
> ## Development trend of their methods
> 
> - **From multi-stage/anchor-based to one-stage anchor-free end-to-end designs** (a): hand-crafted two-stage association pipelines gave way to dense per-pixel anchor-free representations with a single offset vector and task-aligned, multi-objective supervision, simplifying decoding and scaling to many parts.
> - **From blaming sign constraints to understanding spectral structure** (b): diagnosis of poor E/I learning shifted from parameter constraints to the singular-value spectrum at initialization, yielding predictive diagnostics (NSE) and design guidance for biologically constrained networks.
> - **From empirical observations to exactly solvable theory of learning dynamics** (c): the implicit bias of SSL objectives (latent prediction vs reconstruction) is now characterized analytically in deep linear models, explaining why JEPA prioritizes informative, low-noise features.
> - **From static batch guarantees to sequential, label-efficient safety guarantees** (d): risk control moved from one-shot calibration to anytime-valid, active-labeling frameworks built on e-processes and betting, with regret-optimal policies and bounded labeling budgets.
> - **From coupled, algorithm-specific code to modular, unified libraries** (e): decision-making diffusion methods are being consolidated into swappable modules (backbones, solvers, sampling, guidance), enabling reproducible benchmarking, ablation, and customization.
> 
> Overall, the trend is consolidation and unification: simpler one-stage pipelines, principled spectral/theoretical diagnostics, rigorous anytime-valid statistical guarantees, and modular open-source tooling to standardize and democratize these methods.

**community 最终答案**

> Here are the papers from the collection that best match each criterion (some criteria are only partially covered):
> 
> **(a) PBADet: One-Stage Anchor-Free Approach for Part-Body Association** (ICLR 2024) — one-stage anchor-free detector linking human parts (hands, face, feet) to the correct body via a single part-to-body center offset; CNN backbones (YOLOv5/YOLOv7), classification + localization losses with task alignment (TOOD-style), and SGD optimizer; benchmarked on COCO-HumanParts (COCO 2017 based), BodyHands, CrowdHuman (AP, mMR−2, Precision/Recall/F1 vs ED-Pose).
> 
> **(b) Learning Better with Dale's Law: A Spectral Perspective** (NeurIPS 2023) — studies excitatory–inhibitory (E/I) recurrent nets obeying Dale's Law (ColEI vs DANN). Shows spectral properties of the recurrent weights at initialization (multimodal, dispersed singular value spectra; normalized SVD entropy) matter more than sign constraints for learning; ColEI nets show higher training variance and instability without gradient clipping — i.e., training dynamics/stability under gradient-based (stochastic) optimization.
> 
> **(c) How JEPA Avoids Noisy Features: The Implicit Bias of Deep Linear Self-Distillation Networks** (NeurIPS 2024) — analytically solves JEPA vs MAE training dynamics in deep linear networks, proving JEPA's implicit bias toward high-influence (informative) features, strengthened by depth, steering away from high-variance/noisy subspaces. Note: the requested datasets (CIFAR-100, MNIST, SVHN) and metrics (AUROC/F1/Precision) are *not* evidenced in this paper's retrieved content (its experiments use ImageNet-1K; the related LDReg paper covers CIFAR-100 linear probing but not JEPA).
> 
> **(d) Active, Anytime-Valid Risk-Controlling Prediction Sets** (NeurIPS 2024) — extends RCPS to the sequential/streaming setting with anytime-valid guarantees via e-processes and betting, adds active labeling with a label budget (IPW, lower-bounded policies, ML control variates), optimal policy/predictor characterization with regret bounds, and deployment of calibrated thresholds for safety gating of black-box model outputs (e.g., medical imaging, QA).
> 
> **(e) CleanDiffuser: An Easy-to-use Modularized Library for Diffusion Models in Decision Making** (NeurIPS 2024) — modular library decoupling diffusion models/solvers (DDPM, DDIM, DPM-Solver(++), EDM, RectifiedFlow), network architectures (1D U-Nets, Transformers/DiT1d, CNN-based FiLM architectures), guided sampling (classifier/classifier-free), environment wrappers and dataloaders; benchmarked across 37 RL/IL environments (D4RL, Robomimic) with guidance on sampling steps, solvers, EMA, and fine-tuning (e.g., AdaptDiffuser self-fine-tuning; the RTB paper uses LoRA for efficient fine-tuning of text-to-image diffusion). LoRA/SFT, feature embeddings, and vision-language topics are only touched via references, not core content.
> 
> **Development trend of the methods:**
> - **Detection (a):** From multi-stage, anchor-based pipelines → one-stage anchor-free dense prediction, with part-to-body association encoded as a single center offset, task-alignment learning, standard classification losses and SGD, evaluated on COCO-derived benchmarks — moving toward simpler, scalable, universal part-body association.
> - **Recurrent E/I nets (b):** From "sign constraints cause poor learning" → recognition that spectral properties at initialization dominate; use of random-matrix theory and normalized SVD entropy as diagnostics; architecture redesign (DANN) to recover standard spectra, with gradient clipping for stability — i.e., understanding training dynamics through spectral/optimization lens.
> - **SSL theory (c):** From empirical observations that JEPA avoids noisy features → exact deep-linear analyses of greedy feature-learning dynamics, identifying an implicit bias toward influential (predictive) features over variance-explaining ones, with depth amplifying the effect.
> - **Safety/uncertainty (d):** From batch risk-controlling prediction sets → anytime-valid, active, label-budgeted sequential risk control via betting/e-processes with regret guarantees, enabling continuous online calibration and safety gating.
> - **Diffusion decision-making (e):** From tightly coupled, algorithm-specific code → decoupled modular libraries with swappable diffusion models, architectures, and guided sampling, extensive benchmarking, and fine-tuning strategies (self-evolution, LoRA) to improve sample quality — a move toward standardization, reproducibility, and efficient customization.
> 
> Overall trend: **simplification and modularization** (one-stage detection, decoupled libraries), **theory-driven design** (spectral analysis, deep-linear implicit bias, anytime-valid guarantees), and **efficiency/label-economy** (anchor-free, active labeling under budgets, parameter-efficient fine-tuning) across all five areas. Note: the precise dataset/metric combinations in (c) and the LoRA/SFT/VLM breadth in (e) could not be fully verified in the provided context.
